notes: CLOSED 2026-08-20: both criteria. BG modes 0/1 with per-BG char bases, per-BG 8x8/16x16 tile sizes, all four tilemap geometries, the shared write-twice scroll latches, and BG3 priority; OBJ with all eight size pairs, signed 9-bit X, OAMADDR priority rotation, and BOTH per-line limits. Confined to the acceptance on purpose: no windows, colour math, mode 7, mosaic or hires. EMULATION_CORES.md 3.3 describes the FINISHED PPU across several tickets, and a windowing implementation that silently did nothing would make W6-03b's golden frames fail for a reason nobody could locate.

THE TWO OBJ LIMITS ARE INDEPENDENT AND ARE TESTED SEPARATELY. 32 sprites/line and 34 slivers/line drop different things: a 64-wide sprite costs EIGHT slivers and an 8-wide one costs one, so five 64-wide sprites blow the sliver budget (40) while passing the count entirely. A single test that tripped both at once would pass with either limit implemented alone, so there are two: 33 small sprites (count trips, sliver does NOT) and five large ones (sliver trips, count does NOT). $213E range-over/time-over is asserted as a second, independent reading of the same logic even though the acceptance does not name it.

dropped_by_limit STAYS false ON THE SNES PATH TOO, and this is a ruling question worth flagging. The W1-05a ruling in rf_core_api::video is explicit that video_scanline carries exactly one PpuPixel per x and must stay accuracy-exact, so a suppressed sprite cannot go there without displacing what the CRT showed (law 6, FR-MODE-002). Dropped sprites therefore go out through the OverlayPixel channel, and PpuPixel::dropped_by_limit is false on every pixel this PPU emits. EMULATION_CORES.md 3.3's 'both emitted with dropped_by_limit metadata for the enhancement layer' predates that ruling, exactly as 2.2's superseded NES line did. OPEN QUESTION FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE FIELD: its doc says it is 'retained for cores that can express a suppressed sprite without displacing a real pixel', but the one-pixel-per-x sink makes that impossible for NES and SNES alike — so the field is now dead on both paths.

A BUG I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT, worth recording because every test passed with it present. Wiring the PPU left TWO VRAM buffers: the $2118 write port (built in W6-02b, on the bus) filled bus.vram while the renderer read ppu.vram. All 104 unit tests passed, because they poke ppu.vram directly; gilyon cputest passed, because it only ever WRITES VRAM and never looks at a rendered frame. The symptom would have been every game drawing a black screen, first noticed in W6-03b with nothing obviously wrong at either end. VRAM is now single-sourced in the PPU, and an end-to-end test writes a tile through $2118 and asserts the renderer sees it.

BG3 PRIORITY IS THE PIECE MOST EASILY GOT SILENTLY WRONG, because most test content never sets $2105 bit 3. With it clear, BG3's high-priority tiles sit near the BACK of the mode-1 order; with it set they jump to the very FRONT, above sprites. The test asserts BOTH directions from one scene. Writing that test also caught a second trap: BG1 is 4bpp in mode 1, so 2bpp character data leaves it transparent and BG3 wins regardless of the bit — which looks exactly like a priority bug and is not one.

tickets.title: SNES PPU: first golden frames (PeterLemon subset)
acceptance: golden frames green on the PeterLemon PPU tests subset (FR-CORE-033 subset)
notes: REFINED AT PHASE ENTRY BY W6-00 (2026-08-19). `peterlemon-snes` is in `tests/rom-manifest.toml` (artifacts `peterlemon_ppu`, `peterlemon_mode7`), so the golden-frame subset has a source. Note it is NOT yet fetched into `roms/snes/` on this machine — fetch before claiming, and expect the same NFR-006 rule the NES golden suites follow: CI has no ROMs, so the suite must skip locally and FAIL on CI when an artifact is missing rather than pass having asserted nothing.

CLOSED 2026-08-19: both criteria. (2) GILYON CPUTEST IS GREEN — cputest-full.sfc runs to completion with test_num reaching 0x649 (all 1610 tests) and the ROM writing its own verdict, 'Success', as ASCII into VRAM. Two independent readings on purpose: test_num alone could in principle be reached by a wild jump and names the failing test on failure (look it up in the shipped tests-full.txt); the text alone would not say which test failed. (1) AUTO-JOYPAD + $4210/$4211 — crates/rf-snes/src/timing.rs models the frame clock in MASTER cycles (1364/line x 262 lines = 60.1 Hz, the same arithmetic speed.rs pins), vblank at line 225, $4210 RDNMI clear-on-read, $4212 HVBJOY, and the ~3-scanline auto-joypad window.

$4210 CLEAR-ON-READ IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT AN EDGE CASE. gilyon's wait_for_vblank is `bit $4210 / bmi` (drain a pending flag) then `bit $4210 / bpl` (wait for the next one). Without clear-on-read the FIRST loop never exits and the ROM hangs before running a single test. Also why $4210 must go through read and never peek — a debugger that peeked it would acknowledge a vblank the program never saw. Tested in both directions.

THE JOYPAD LATCHES ON THE WINDOW'S CLOSING EDGE, not 'whenever idle'. The first version latched continuously, which made $4218 track the pad in real time and would have hidden any error in the window's timing — the port looking right for the wrong reason. Timing::advance now reports auto_joypad_done and the test asserts exactly one latch per frame.

THE ROM REQUIRES INPUT, AND THAT IS NOT A WORKAROUND. cputest pauses between test banks with 'Press A for next tests...', polling $4212 bit 0 then $4218 bit 7 and waiting for a press AND THEN A RELEASE — holding A permanently hangs on the release wait. Diagnosed by disassembling the loop the run was stuck in at test 36 rather than guessing. Pulsing the button means this suite genuinely exercises the auto-joypad latch, i.e. criterion 1, rather than only asserting it in isolation.

A DOCUMENTATION CONTRADICTION, RESOLVED AGAINST PRIMARY EVIDENCE. gilyon's cputest README documents an undocumented (direct,X) emulation-mode behaviour: with DL nonzero, the pointer's high byte is read from addr+1 with the +1 WRAPPING WITHIN THE PAGE (worked example: E=1, D=$11A, X=$EE, lda ($F7,X) -> low from $2FF, high from $200). This implementation does not wrap, so the README implied a bug. Checked rather than believed: the SingleStepTests vectors carry per-cycle bus traces, and filtering $A1/$01/$C1 emulation-mode cases for the discriminating shape (E=1, DL!=0, (D+dp+X)&$FF==$FF) yields 88 cases, EVERY one reading the high byte from the next page ($2DFF then $2E00, not $2D00). gilyon's own cputest-full — which does test emulation-mode wrapping — separately reports Success against this implementation. Two behavioural oracles against one line of prose. A test now pins the verified behaviour and quotes the README, so nobody later reads it and 'fixes' correct code.

SCOPE WIDENED to scripts/local-gate.sh so the cputest actually GATES rather than resting on an env-gated test run once by hand. The gate extracts the archive (rf-harness does no archive extraction, per its fetch.rs doc) and runs the suite. NOTE FOR FUTURE TICKETS: this is the third consecutive ticket needing a scope widening to make its own result gate — the write_scopes are systematically narrower than 'build it AND wire it into the gate', which is what closing a ticket honestly requires.

VRAM WRITE PORT ADDED HERE, DELIBERATELY: $2115 VMAIN, $2116/7 VMADD, $2118/9 VMDATA into a 64 KiB buffer. It is a memory-mapped REGISTER, which is W6-02a/b's business; RENDERING from it is W6-03a's, which now inherits a populated VRAM instead of having to build the port too. It is also what makes the ROM's own verdict readable without a PPU.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: golden frames green on the PeterLemon PPU subset — the four 2BPP BGMAP tests, one per background layer, in BG mode 0. That is a real subset rather than a token one: it exercises each of the four layers independently, through real ROM code, against a photographic test image where any tile-fetch, bitplane or palette error is immediately visible.

THE BLOCKER DISSOLVED THE SAME WAY W6-01a's DID. The manifest carried sha256 = 'TODO-network-not-attempted' for a whole-repo snapshot whose size had never been checked. It is 240 MB (GitHub API, verified) — and the archive is unnecessary, because individual .sfc files are fetchable from raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit. The subset costs four 32 KiB files instead of a quarter-gigabyte download. The artifact entry is NOT retired the way singlestep-65816's was, because peterlemon_mode7 still points at it; the hash stays a TODO- placeholder because it is still true that nothing has computed it, and writing anything else would be a claim about bytes nobody has seen.

I LOOKED AT EVERY FRAME BEFORE PINNING ITS HASH, and it mattered twice. A self-generated golden cannot prove a picture is RIGHT, only that it stopped changing — so each frame was rendered to PNG and inspected. (1) The first attempt produced four identical ALL-BLACK frames that would have hashed perfectly consistently forever: these ROMs fade the screen in over 15 vblanks before settling, and the frame was being composed after ~1 frame, with VRAM and CGRAM still empty. The runner now waits for the fade to COMPLETE semantically (!forced_blank && brightness == $0F) rather than for a magic instruction count. (2) See the mode-3 note below. The dump path is kept wired behind RF_GOLDEN_DUMP so the next person can re-verify rather than re-derive.

THE '4BPP' ROM IS EXCLUDED BECAUSE IT IS ACTUALLY MODE 3. 8x8BGMap4BPP32x328PAL sounds like a mode-1 test and is not: running it shows it sets BGMODE to 3 (8bpp BG1 + 4bpp BG2), and on a modes-0/1 PPU its output is visible garbage. A golden pinned on that would have gone green forever while recording a wrong picture — the worst thing a golden suite can do. The runner now asserts the ROM's BG mode is one this PPU implements BEFORE hashing, so the failure mode is impossible rather than dependent on whoever adds the next ROM noticing.

AN ANTI-VACUITY TEST THE PER-LAYER SHAPE NEEDS: the four ROMs must produce four DISTINCT frames. They draw the same photograph on four different layers, so identical hashes would mean the layer under test is not the one being rendered — and four separately-pinned goldens would hide that perfectly. Related, and worth knowing before the hashes puzzle someone: the four frames look IDENTICAL on screen yet hash differently, which is correct and is itself evidence. In mode 0 each layer indexes a different palette block (BG1 0-31, BG2 32-63, BG3 64-95, BG4 96-127) and each ROM loads CGRAM to match, so the same photograph on a different layer really is a different set of indices.

Hashes cover palette INDICES, not colours, matching rf_harness::golden_frame's rule: a golden is about the pixels the PPU produced, not how a renderer later resolves CGRAM. Wired into scripts/local-gate.sh (scope widened for that and for the fetch script/manifest, as on the previous tickets).

tickets.title: SPC700 core + ARAM + timers
acceptance: spc700 JSON vectors pass (FR-CORE-031)
64KB ARAM + IPL ROM banking via $F1 + timers T0-T2
notes: REFINED AT PHASE ENTRY BY W6-00 (2026-08-19).

**BLOCKER TO RESOLVE BEFORE CLAIMING: the SPC700 IPL boot ROM.** This ticket's acceptance says "64KB ARAM + IPL ROM banking via $F1", and EMULATION_CORES section 3.4 wants the "$FFC0-FFFF, readable/bankable via $F1" handshake. That IPL is 64 bytes of Nintendo code. Project law 5 is "no ROM bytes in git", so it cannot simply be pasted into the source the way a synthetic fixture can.

THREE OPTIONS, none of them chosen here — this needs a ruling, and the ticket should not be claimed until it has one. (a) HLE the handshake: implement the boot protocol's OBSERVABLE behaviour without the ROM's bytes, which is what several emulators do and which keeps the repo clean, at the cost of any game that reads IPL bytes directly seeing wrong data. (b) Fetch it as a hash-verified artifact like every other external oracle, which fits the manifest machinery exactly but puts a Nintendo-copyright blob in a fetch list rather than in git — note D-001's boundary already permits fetch-only for external oracles, though an IPL is not an oracle. (c) Require the user to supply it, like the ROMs themselves. The honest default is probably (a) with the limitation documented, but that is a call about what the emulator CLAIMS to be, not a coding decision.
spc700 vectors themselves are unblocked either way: `singlestep-spc700` is in the manifest and already fetched locally. The IPL question only gates the boot-handshake half.

RULING TAKEN 2026-08-20 (Brad, by reaffirmation): option (a), HLE — no Nintendo IPL bytes anywhere, not in git and not in a fetch list. Recorded as REVERSIBLE: options (b) and (c) stay open and nothing here depends on the IPL's actual contents. What this ticket implements is the $F1 BANKING MECHANISM in full — the switch that hides ARAM $FFC0-$FFFF behind a 64-byte boot region and exposes it again — with that region backed by a clean-room stub written here rather than by Nintendo's bytes. The banking is the testable behaviour; the boot protocol it serves is W6-04b's. The cost, stated plainly: a game that reads IPL bytes directly sees our stub, not the real ROM. No commercial title is known to do that, and W6-04b's handshake is what actually has to work.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: both criteria. (1) SPC700 VECTORS 256,000 of 256,000 PASSING across ALL 256 opcodes, zero unimplemented — SingleStepTests spc700, 256 opcode files x 1000 cases. (2) 64 KiB ARAM, $F1 IPL banking, and timers T0/T1 (8 kHz) / T2 (64 kHz) with their 4-bit read-to-clear counters.

THE OPCODE MAP IS REGULAR ENOUGH TO BE TABLE-DRIVEN, and the first pass proved where it stops being so. The six ALU groups share one low-nibble addressing family, so they are a table rather than 96 hand-written arms — that got 237 of 256 opcodes to 237,000/237,000 in one go. The 19 that remained were a single coherent family the table did not cover: the MEMORY-destination ALU forms (dp,dp / dp,#imm / (X),(Y)) plus XCN. Their operand bytes arrive SOURCE FIRST, the opposite of how the mnemonic reads, and CMP among them writes nothing back.

WRITES PASS THROUGH THE IPL WINDOW INTO ARAM. This looks like a bug and is not: $FFC0-$FFFF READS the IPL while $F1 bit 7 is set, but writes always land in the ARAM underneath — which is how a boot loader stashes data in the region it is executing from. A model that dropped them would lose it silently, so there is a test that banks the region out afterwards and checks the byte survived.

A LATENT BUG IN scripts/validate-arch.sh, FOUND HERE AND NOT FIXED HERE (out of scope). Its determinism lint greps for the RNG crate name followed by a path separator with NO WORD BOUNDARY, so an enum named `Operand` makes every `Operand::` reference an ARCH VIOLATION. It will do the same to any identifier ending in those five letters. The fix is a word boundary in DETERMINISM_BAN (scripts/validate-arch.sh line 38). Worked around by renaming the enum to AddrMode, which is the better name anyway. Worth knowing: the first version of the comment EXPLAINING the false positive also tripped it, because the lint greps comments too — which is why that doc now describes the pattern instead of quoting it.

A TEST BUG WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE A REAL FAILURE: the timer counters are FOUR bits, so a test that ticks T2 exactly 256 cycles gets 16 increments and reads back 0 — indistinguishable from 'the timer never counted'. Any assertion that a timer MOVED has to avoid landing on a multiple of 16, and the test now says so where the next person will hit it.

HONEST SCOPE. The vector runner compares registers and memory, NOT the cycle trace — same deliberate choice as the 65816 suite, and for the same reason (no cycle-accurate executor yet). Apu::step advances the timers by a nominal 2 cycles per instruction, which keeps them monotonic and testable without pretending to an accuracy this ticket does not have. The DSP ($F3) and the CPU-facing port protocol are W6-04b's; $F2/$F4-$F7 exist as storage so that ticket wires them rather than building them.

tickets.title: CPU<->APU ports + boot handshake
acceptance: $2140-$2143 <-> $F4-$F7 port protocol in catch-up sync (never free-running)
commercial-style init handshake boots (test ROM)
S-DSP skeleton: BRR decode + basic voice mixing, clean audio (sample-exactness deferred to W7 per EMULATION_CORES.md section 3.4)
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-20: all three criteria. (1) $2140-$2143 <-> $F4-$F7 in CATCH-UP SYNC, never free-running: the APU accrues debt with every master cycle the CPU spends and is settled immediately BEFORE any port access, so the CPU can only ever observe a state the APU actually reached. peek deliberately does NOT catch up — a debugger reading a port would otherwise advance the APU and change the machine it is inspecting. (2) A commercial-style init handshake driven by real 65816 machine code completes, uploads a byte and starts the APU at the supplied entry. (3) S-DSP skeleton: BRR decode and eight-voice mixing.

THE HLE RULING FROM W6-04a IS NOW CASHED OUT, and its consequence is stated in the code rather than buried: while the boot handshake runs, the SPC700 core DOES NOT EXECUTE. The handshake is a state machine reproducing the protocol's observable behaviour, which is exactly what option (a) said. The moment it hands over, the uploaded program runs on the real core — verified by the 65816 test, which checks the APU's PC is the entry address the CPU supplied and that the IPL has banked out.

THE COUNTER SKIP IS THE EASIEST PART OF THIS PROTOCOL TO GET WRONG, and it caught my own test on its first run. The transfer counter is an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, not an index: after a byte acknowledged with counter N the APU expects N+1 for the next byte, so ENDING a block means skipping to N+2. My 65816 driver wrote N+1 and the handshake simply stored another byte and never finished. There is now a test that walks next-byte and new-block cases side by side, and the machine-code comment says why it is two.

DSP SCOPE, NAMED SO ITS ABSENCE IS A DECISION. Implemented: BRR decode (all four filters, the range 13-15 special case that collapses to the sign rather than shifting further, sign-extended nibbles, loop/end flags) and eight-voice mixing with per-voice and master volume. NOT implemented, per the acceptance's 'sample-exactness deferred to W7': Gaussian interpolation, ADSR/GAIN envelopes, echo, pitch modulation, noise. 'Clean audio' is tested as three specific properties rather than as a vibe — silence when nothing is keyed on, key-on resetting the filter history so a re-keyed voice reproduces its opening exactly (a voice that kept the old history would start with a click), and a non-looping sample keying itself off at its end instead of running on into whatever follows it in ARAM.

THE CATCH-UP IS BOUNDED, on purpose. A long DMA or a paused debugger can hand the APU millions of owed cycles at once; grinding through them inside one bus access would stall the emulator at exactly the moment a game is polling a port. The catch-up therefore runs at most 64 SPC cycles per access and keeps the remaining debt.

tickets.title: RF-Scroller-S: in-repo libSFX SNES fixture + FORMAT.md + replay gate
acceptance: fixtures/snes/rf-scroller-s builds deterministically from source in CI, with rom.sha256 pinned and verified by the build script (fixture doctrine D-001, as RF-Scroller does for NES)
FORMAT.md documents the level format, the RAM map and the toolchain provenance, to the standard fixtures/nes/rf-scroller/FORMAT.md sets
a scripted 5-minute input log runs without faults and is gated as a .rfreplay (FR-CORE-037)
notes: FILED 2026-08-19 BY W6-00. D-001 names this fixture by name ("RF-Scroller-S (SNES, libSFX, via W6-00)") and FR-CORE-037 gates on it, so it is a doctrine obligation rather than a nice-to-have: game-shaped content the project demos or regresses on is OURS, in-repo, built from source in CI.
DEPENDS ON W6-06 FOR THE TOOLCHAIN, not the other way round: nothing SNES-shaped can be built until libSFX/asar exist in CI, and that is a separate, smaller, independently-useful piece of work.

LEARN FROM RF-SCROLLER RATHER THAN REDISCOVERING. Its FORMAT.md and three tickets' worth of hard-won lessons apply directly: (a) declaration order decides BSS layout, so any new global goes AFTER the documented ones or every documented address and the shipped profile silently go stale (W5-02c); (b) a stale local symbol dump will happily give you the wrong addresses — re-link with a debug file and verify the ROM is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pinned hash before trusting symbols (W5-01); (c) anything between the vblank wait and a VRAM write eats that write's budget, and an overrun corrupts isolated tiles that look like nothing until an offline decoder disagrees (W5-02c).

The 5-minute replay gate should follow `fixtures/replays/unprofiled-scroller.rfreplay`'s pattern from W5-08: record with an #[ignore]d test, verify the ROM hash on replay so a fixture rebuild fails loudly rather than replaying stale inputs into a different game.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 1 and 2 are COMPLETE; criterion 3 is HALF-DELIVERED and the missing half is blocked on another crate. Left in_progress rather than closed — one criterion, not fully met, is not done (the W6-01a precedent). DELIVERED: fixtures/snes/rf-scroller-s builds deterministically from source in CI with rom.sha256 pinned and verified by build.sh (which refuses a mismatch rather than re-pinning); FORMAT.md documents the level format, the RAM map and the toolchain provenance to the standard fixtures/nes/rf-scroller/FORMAT.md sets; and the scripted 5-minute input log RUNS WITHOUT FAULTS with two independent machines reaching bit-identical reachable state at all 30 ten-second checkpoints.

THE BLOCKER, with evidence: .rfreplay CANNOT REPRESENT SNES INPUT. rf-input's PortLogKey::buttons is a Vec<NesButton>, canonical_log_key() always writes the $4016 read order, and the crate has NO SnesButton type at all. A SNES button outside the NES 8-bit set — Right is bit 8 — has no log-key entry and is SILENTLY DROPPED on serialisation. Found the hard way: recording this fixture's 'hold Right' log and replaying it diverged at the very first checkpoint (frame 600) because run 2 received buttons == 0. THE EMULATOR WAS DETERMINISTIC THROUGHOUT — the log was lossy, which is why the delivered test compares two independent machines directly instead. WHAT IS OWED: a SnesButton set and a generalised PortLogKey in crates/rf-input/**, which is outside this ticket's write_scope and is a change to a documented wire format with its own tests, so it is a ticket rather than an amendment. the_replay_format_still_cannot_represent_snes_buttons pins the gap and FAILS WITH INSTRUCTIONS the moment someone adds SNES support.

DEVIATION FROM THE TICKET TITLE AND D-001, FLAGGED NOT BURIED: built with cc65, not libSFX. W6-06 established by checking that ca65 already assembles 65816 and that cc65 is already in CI; its FORMAT.md predicted libSFX would still be right HERE, on the grounds a scroller wants a framework's init code, macros and asset pipeline. In the event it wants none of them — the init is ~40 lines of register writes and the 'assets' are four solid-colour characters generated in-source, deliberately, because a fixture whose graphics live in a binary blob is not reproducible from text. libSFX would have meant a new dependency, a TECH_STACK row, a licence review and a CI install step for nothing this fixture uses. Recorded in FORMAT.md too; if a later SNES fixture genuinely needs a framework, nothing here argues against it.

A BUG WORTH NOT REPEATING, in FORMAT.md as well: stream_one_column originally saved only the FLAGS (PHP/PLP) and then used X as its row counter — but preload_columns uses X as its loop counter. The first build streamed 30,103 columns and never left forced blank: black screen, frame counter stuck at zero, no error anywhere. PHP saves the processor status, not the registers. The fix is PHX/PHY, two instructions, and the symptom looks nothing like the cause.

ANTI-VACUITY IS columns_streamed, and it has a counter-test. The tilemap is 32 columns wide, so columns_streamed == 33 means the preload plus the first frame and NOTHING HAS SCROLLED; above 33 is only reachable once a physical column has been overwritten with new content. One test asserts it exceeds 33 under the scripted input; another asserts it stays at exactly 33 with no input, so the first cannot be satisfied by a fixture that scrolls regardless of the pad.

CLOSED 2026-08-20, after W7-02 removed the blocker. Criterion 3 is now fully met: the scripted 5-minute input log runs without faults AND is gated as a real .rfreplay — recorded, serialised, parsed, and replayed on a fresh machine that run 1 never touched, with bit-identical reachable state at all 30 ten-second checkpoints. The replay test additionally asserts the log carries the SNES button table rather than the NES one, and that each replayed frame's buttons equal what was recorded — so a future format regression fails here loudly instead of looking like an emulator divergence, which is exactly how this one first presented.

Filed as a ticket rather than left in a handoff note because it BLOCKS AN ALREADY-OPEN TICKET, and because 'the replay format is NES-only' is exactly the kind of fact that stays invisible until someone tries to use it.

A NOTE ON EDITING THIS FILE, since this ticket added twelve entries at once: plan.json's unicode escaping is MIXED — some strings carry literal em-dashes, others carry \u2014 — so no json.load/json.dumps round trip reproduces it, at ANY ensure_ascii setting. A round trip here churned 4027 lines before it was reverted; the same twelve tickets inserted by targeted text surgery are 296 insertions and zero deletions. Append by text, never by re-serialising the whole board.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all four criteria. SnesButton exists with the $4218/$4219 layout the core already uses (A is bit 7, Right is bit 8 — the same bits RF-Scroller-S and the gilyon harness drive); PortLogKey::buttons is now Vec<Button>, an enum over both consoles; every SNES button survives a record -> serialize -> parse -> replay round trip; and RF-Scroller-S's 5-minute log is gated as a REAL .rfreplay, completing W6-05 criterion 3.

PARSING IS CONSOLE-DIRECTED, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION. 'A', 'B', 'Select', 'Start' and the four directions exist on BOTH consoles at DIFFERENT bits — Right is bit 7 on NES and bit 8 on SNES. So there is deliberately no Button::from_name: the [Header]'s console field decides which table a name is looked up in, and an unrecognised console falls back to NES because that is what every existing file already decodes as. A name-only lookup across both tables would have silently mis-decoded every NES log ever recorded.

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY IS PINNED LITERALLY, not merely round-tripped. A round trip would pass even if both sides changed together, so the test asserts the exact bytes an NES recorder emits: 'P1:A,B,Select,Start,Up,Down,Left,Right' and '|A......R|........|'. The shoulder buttons take lowercase l/r mnemonics because L and R are already Left and Right — a collision that would make an input line ambiguous, asserted distinct in SnesButton's own tests.

tickets.title: SNES PPU: BG modes 2-6 + offset-per-tile
acceptance: BG modes 2-6 per BGMODE ($2105) with their documented bit depths and layer counts
offset-per-tile in modes 2/4/6 (EMULATION_CORES.md section 3.3)
direct-color mode 3/4 via CGWSEL
the PeterLemon 8BPP BGMAP goldens (32x32, 32x64, 64x32, 64x64, TileFlip) green
notes: W6-03a implemented modes 0/1 only, and W6-03b's golden runner ASSERTS the ROM's BG mode is one the PPU implements before hashing — so adding a mode is what unlocks its goldens rather than a separate wiring job.
The 4BPP BGMAP ROM excluded at W6-03b is actually MODE 3 (8bpp BG1 + 4bpp BG2), verified by running it. It belongs to this ticket, not to a mode-1 ticket.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all four criteria. BG modes 2-6 with their documented depths and layer counts, offset-per-tile in modes 2/4/6, the $2130 CGWSEL direct-colour flag, and the PeterLemon 8BPP BGMAP goldens green — ten goldens now, up from four.

8BPP IS FOUR BITPLANE PAIRS, 8 WORDS APART, not two 4bpp tiles end to end. fetch_pixel is now a loop over depth/2 pairs at +0, +8, +16 and +24, which collapses the 2/4/8bpp cases into one expression instead of three. A unit test reads the SAME character at all three depths and asserts each sees one more pair than the last.

8BPP IGNORES THE TILEMAP'S PALETTE FIELD, because it addresses all 256 CGRAM entries directly. Applying the field would fold a 256-colour image into a 32-colour block — the picture would keep its shapes and lose its colours, which reads as a palette bug rather than a depth bug. Tested with a deliberately non-zero palette field.

OFFSET-PER-TILE REPLACES A COLUMN'S SCROLL, it does not add to it. Modes 2 and 6 read TWO BG3 entries per column — horizontal, then vertical 32 entries later — while mode 4 reads ONE and uses bit 15 to choose. Confusing the two applies vertical offsets horizontally, which is the classic bug here: the picture looks almost right. Both forms are tested side by side, along with bit 13/14 layer selection and column 0 having no entry at all.

A TEST-SETUP TRAP WORTH RECORDING: ppu_with_tile writes 2bpp character data at words $1008-$100F, which in 4bpp is plane-pair 1 of character ZERO. So in any mode where BG1 is 4bpp, character 0 is not transparent, and 'nothing is drawn here' cannot be asserted from that helper. The offset-per-tile test builds a clean Ppu instead and says why.

32x64 AND 64x32 HASH IDENTICALLY, AND THAT IS CORRECT — but it needed proving rather than explaining away. Unscrolled, both show the first 32x28 tiles, which live in screen 0 either way. the_tilemap_geometry_is_honoured_once_you_scroll_into_it scrolls both one screen right, where a 64-wide map has a second screen and a 32-wide map wraps back to its first, and asserts they diverge. Without it, 'the two look the same' would have been equally consistent with tilemap_size never being read. The per-layer distinctness test was also SCOPED to the four 2BPP ROMs it was written for, rather than loosened to accommodate the coincidence.

DIRECT COLOUR IS EXPOSED, NOT FOLDED IN. $2130 bit 0 makes an 8bpp pixel a BGR333 colour in its own right rather than a CGRAM index. The core still emits that value as palette_index, because it is genuinely what the PPU produced; what changes is how a renderer must INTERPRET it. So the flag is public PPU state (law 4: cores emit indexed pixels plus metadata) rather than something silently baked into the pixel stream.

EVERY NEW GOLDEN WAS LOOKED AT before being pinned, per the W6-03b discipline: the mode-3 8bpp ROMs render a detailed castle scene, the 4BPP ROM the same landscape as the 2BPP set but in far richer colour, and TileFlip a perfectly symmetric seamless pattern — which is exactly what a flip test should produce, since broken flips show as asymmetry at tile boundaries.

tickets.title: SNES PPU: Mode 7 + HD-Mode-7-class internal resolution
acceptance: Mode 7 matrix ($211B-$211E) as 8.8 fixed point, with the M7A x M7B product readable at $2134-$2136
1024x1024 playfield with screen-over repeat/clamp per M7SEL
HD-Mode-7-class internal resolution: the SAME matrix math sampled at higher density (ROADMAP P7), opt-in and off in Accuracy Mode (law 6)
PeterLemon Mode 7 goldens (RotZoom, Perspective, StarWars) green at 1x
notes: EXTBG (mode 7 BG2 priority bit) is explicitly Phase 7 per section 3.3 — keep it here rather than deferring further.
The HD variant must be an OVERLAY over an unmodified simulation (law 6): a fresh install boots in Accuracy Mode and renders 1x, and the golden set above gates the 1x path.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 1-3 are COMPLETE; criterion 4 is PARTIALLY met and its remainder depends on W7-07. Left in_progress — one criterion, not fully met, is not done (the W6-01a precedent). DELIVERED: the 8.8 fixed-point matrix with its shared write-twice latch, 13-bit signed centre/scroll registers, the 1024x1024 interleaved playfield (tilemap in the EVEN VRAM bytes, characters in the ODD bytes of the same words), all four screen-over behaviours, the $2134-$2136 multiplier, sprites composing over mode 7, and HD-Mode-7-class internal resolution. RotZoom is pinned as a golden and was verified BY EYE: it renders a racing track with road, sand and red/white kerbing.

A DISCONNECTED PIPELINE OF MY OWN MAKING, worth recording because it looked like a mode-7 maths bug and was not. $2134-$2136 (the M7A x M7B product) was implemented as Mode7::product() and never wired to the bus. PeterLemon's RotZoom computes its ROTATION MATRIX with that multiplier — it is the SNES's general-purpose signed multiplier, not a mode-7 accessory — so reads returned OPEN BUS, which is the last value driven: $21, the high byte of the register address itself. Every matrix element therefore read back as $2121 and the playfield rendered as diagonal stripes. Diagnosed by tracing the actual register writes rather than re-deriving the transform, which was correct throughout.

PERSPECTIVE AND STARWARS ARE EXCLUDED, NOT WAIVED, each with evidence rather than a guess. Perspective enables FOUR HDMA channels ($420C reads $0F) to rewrite the mode-7 matrix per scanline — that IS the perspective effect — so without HDMA it renders a coherent but FLAT rotated track, and pinning it would freeze the half-right picture. StarWars renders fully transparent for its first ~170 frames: screen-over is 'transparent outside the playfield', the matrix sits static at A=410 D=256 Y0=-90, NMI is DISABLED, and the CPU loops at $00:8269 throughout; whatever advances that demo is not implemented yet, so there is nothing correct to pin and a black frame would hash perfectly consistently forever. Both are still RUN and REPORTED by the golden suite rather than skipped by name, so an exclusion cannot outlive its reason silently.

THE BOARD DID NOT RECORD THIS DEPENDENCY: W7-04's fourth criterion names three Mode 7 goldens, but two of them cannot be green until W7-07 (DMA/HDMA) lands. That is a genuine ordering fact rather than a scope dispute — recommend W7-04 depend on W7-07, or that its criterion be amended to name RotZoom alone with the other two moved onto W7-07's acceptance.

HD-MODE-7 IS SAMPLING, NOT FILTERING, and the test says so: rendering at density 4 returns a 1024-wide scanline in which every hardware pixel still appears, unchanged, at index x*4. The extra samples are real evaluations of the same matrix — no interpolation, no smoothing, no invented detail — which is what makes this class of enhancement faithful. Law 6 is enforced by a separate test: Ppu::render_scanline is always hardware density and bit-identical to an explicit density of 1, so a caller must opt in to anything else.

UPDATED 2026-08-20 BY W7-07: Perspective is now GREEN and pinned — HDMA plus per-scanline register latching gave it the per-line matrix its effect needs. Two of criterion 4's three goldens now pass. StarWars remains excluded on its own evidence (fully transparent for ~170 frames, static matrix, NMI disabled, CPU looping at $00:8269) and is the only thing between this ticket and done.

STATUS SET TO `blocked`, NOT `in_progress` (2026-08-20): validate-plan's P8 rule forbids two concurrently-active tickets with overlapping write_scope, and W7-04 and W7-07 both write crates/rf-snes/**. `blocked` is also the truthful status: each one's own work is committed and each is waiting on a DIFFERENT ticket, not on more effort here. Caught by the validator after the commit rather than before it — a reminder that leaving two partially-done tickets open at once is itself a board state worth checking.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: criterion 4 delivered, and its HANDOFF diagnosis was WRONG TWICE OVER. That note said StarWars 'renders fully transparent... NMI is disabled, and the CPU loops at $00:8269 throughout. Whatever advances this demo is not yet implemented'. Two separate bugs were hiding behind that. (1) THE CLOCK WAS FROZEN -- W7-15 found Cpu::step charged zero master cycles while halted, so the demo could not advance at all. With that fixed StarWars runs to frame 391+, unblanked, mode 7, VRAM populated. (2) M7HOFS/M7VOFS WERE NEVER WIRED. Mode7::hofs and ::vofs existed, the transform read them, and NOTHING EVER WROTE THEM -- mode 7 has no scroll registers of its own. fullsnes: 'Writing to 210Dh does BOTH update M7HOFS (via M7_old mechanism), and also updates BG1HOFS (via BG_old mechanism)', signed 13-bit through a SEPARATE latch from BG_old. StarWars sets M7X = M7Y = 512 and scrolls via $210D, so with the scroll lost every sample landed outside the 1024x1024 playfield and screen-over made it transparent: a black frame from a demo that was working. NO MODE-7 GAME COULD SCROLL. With hofs = 384 the centre maps to the playfield centre and the logo appears over its starfield. StarWars is promoted from EXCLUDED to a pinned golden with a semantic capture plan (wait for mode7.a >= 800, since its first ~170 frames legitimately draw no playfield -- capturing there is what pinned a black frame). 88% exact against PeterLemon's reference, the rest being a different frame of a zoom animation. ONE existing golden changed, Perspective, and it IMPROVED: the track is now scrolled into position rather than sitting at offset zero. RotZoom and Mode7HDMA are byte-identical, which is the control.

tickets.title: SNES PPU: windows, color math, mosaic
acceptance: windows WH0-WH3 with per-layer window logic (OR/AND/XOR/XNOR) and clip-to-black vs color-math masking ($2130)
color math: CGADSUB add/sub, half, per-layer enable, fixed color $2132, sub-screen composition
mosaic ($2106) including the mode-7 mosaic quirks
PeterLemon PPU/Window (WindowHDMA, WindowMultiHDMA) and PPU/Mosaic (MosaicMode3, MosaicMode5) ROMs green as golden frames, each rendered and inspected by eye before its hash is pinned
notes: HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 1-3 COMPLETE; criterion 4 is UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN — it names ROMs the pinned archive does not contain. DELIVERED: windows WH0-WH3 with per-layer enable/invert and all four combiners (OR/AND/XOR/XNOR), $212E/$212F main/sub mask gating, colour math ($2130-$2132) including add/sub/half with clamping and the four clip and prevent modes, and mosaic ($2106) wired into the fetch so it actually blockifies.

THE COMBINER ONLY MATTERS WITH BOTH WINDOWS ENABLED — with one, all four agree. That is exactly why an implementation that hard-codes OR passes most content and fails the rest, so the test drives four x-positions (in W1 only, in both, in W2 only, in neither) against all four combiners, with a counter-test proving they agree when only one window is on. Inverting is a membership flip, NOT 'the other side of the span': an inverted EMPTY span (left > right) covers the whole line, and that is asserted.

A WINDOW MASKS THE MAIN SCREEN ONLY IF $212E SAYS SO. Games routinely configure a window and leave it disabled there, so checking the span alone makes content vanish. Tested in both directions, plus that a masked layer is REMOVED from priority resolution — the layer below shows through rather than the screen going blank.

COLOUR MATH COLLIDES WITH LAW 4, AND THE SPLIT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FUDGED. Colour math produces an RGB value that need not exist anywhere in CGRAM, but cores emit INDEXED pixels — so a blended colour cannot travel through PpuPixel at all, and the golden-frame hash (palette indices only) could not see it if it did. Delivered accordingly: CLIP-TO-BLACK runs on the indexed path and is asserted there, because black IS palette index 0; the add/sub/half arithmetic is implemented and unit-tested in RGB but does NOT enter the pixel stream. Carrying a sub-screen and blend mode across CoreSink is an rf-core-api contract change and is outside this ticket. RECOMMEND filing it — without it, colour math can never be verified by a golden frame.

CRITERION 4 NAMES ROMS THAT DO NOT EXIST IN THE PINNED ARCHIVE. It asks for 'undisbeliever window/HDMA-gradient ROMs'. The manifest's pinned undisbeliever-snes-test-roms archive (20210217) was extracted and enumerated: 29 .sfc files, ALL of them hdma-*, hdmaen-*, inidisp-* or scpu-a-dma-bug-*. There is no window ROM and no gradient ROM in it. Separately, W7-07 established with direct evidence that the ROMs it DOES contain are per-dot timing tests which never leave forced blank on a scanline-composed PPU. RECOMMEND: amend this criterion to name a source that exists, or move it to the per-dot PPU ticket alongside W7-07's criterion 4.

RULING (Brad, 2026-08-20, in response to the unattended loop’s four blocking questions). Amend acceptance rather than leave this blocked. CRITERION 4 IS REPLACED, and the replacement names ROMs VERIFIED TO EXIST: the GitHub contents API at the pinned PeterLemon commit 350b394e lists PPU/Window/{WindowHDMA,WindowMultiHDMA}/*.sfc and PPU/Mosaic/{Mode3,Mode5}/*.sfc. The old criterion asked for undisbeliever window/gradient ROMs, and that archive was enumerated at 29 files with no window and no gradient ROM among them — the artifacts were never in the archive the criterion pointed at, they were in the OTHER pinned source all along. Both replacements are expressible on a scanline PPU: window masking resolves to clip-to-black (palette index 0, on the indexed path) and mosaic is an indexed-domain operation, so neither needs the RGB sub-screen. Colour math’s golden-frame verification stays OUT of this ticket and remains W7-16’s, which already exists and depends on this one.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (2026-08-20, standing authority): write_scope gains scripts/** and tests/rom-manifest.toml — the amended criterion 4 names ROMs that must be FETCHED before they can be rendered, and the fetcher lives in scripts/. W7-07 already carries exactly these two entries for the same reason.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: criterion 4 delivered against the amended acceptance. The four ROMs were fetched, rendered to PNG and LOOKED AT, and doing so changed three of the four outcomes -- see the module doc of crates/rf-snes/tests/peterlemon_golden.rs. tickets.title: SNES PPU: interlace, overscan, hires modes 5/6
acceptance: interlace + overscan via SETINI, with the frame emitting 224 or 239 visible lines and the renderer letterboxing
pseudo-hires and hires modes 5/6 emitting 512-wide scanlines, with the PpuPixel stream carrying a width tag per line (EMULATION_CORES.md section 3.3)
PeterLemon Interlace ROMs green
notes: The per-line width tag is an rf-core-api shape question, not only an rf-snes one — check whether CoreSink::video_scanline can carry it before assuming, and file the api change separately if it cannot.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (2026-08-20, standing authority): write_scope gains scripts/** so criterion 3's Interlace ROMs can be fetched, exactly as W7-05 and W7-07 needed. The PeterLemon PPU/Interlace directory was enumerated at the pinned commit 350b394e and holds six ROMs: InterlaceFont, InterlaceMoogle, InterlaceMystHDMA, InterlaceRPG, InterlaceScroll, InterlaceSimpsonsHDMA.

W7-17 IS FOLDED INTO THIS TICKET AND WITHDRAWN (2026-08-20). W7-17 was filed during W7-05 for 'hi-res modes 5 and 6' without first checking whether an existing ticket covered it -- this ticket's criterion 2 already did. Its one genuinely new criterion is carried over: promote PeterLemon MosaicMode5 from EXCLUDED to a pinned golden, since it is excluded solely because mode 5 hi-res does not exist yet. Recorded rather than quietly deleted, because a duplicate ticket filed by an unattended run is exactly the kind of board noise worth being able to trace.

THE PER-LINE WIDTH TAG NEEDS NO API CHANGE, checked rather than assumed (this ticket's own note asked): CoreSink::video_scanline takes &[PpuPixel], and a slice carries its own length, so the width tag IS pixels.len(). What DOES need attention is the consumer side -- FrameBundleBuilder::video_scanline truncates each row to a single frame-level width (crates/rf-core-api/src/frame_bundle.rs), so a frame mixing 256-wide and 512-wide lines cannot be represented there. That is outside this write_scope and is filed separately.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criterion 1 DELIVERED (core half); criteria 2 and 3 BLOCKED ON W7-16, with primary-source evidence. DELIVERED: $2133 SETINI fully decoded, every bit asserted independently -- bit 1 is OBJ V-direction and bit 2 is BG V-direction, and swapping them gives a PPU that resizes sprites when a game asks for 239 lines -- overscan driving 224-vs-239 visible lines through the frame loop, and the vblank boundary moving with it. THE COUNTER-INTUITIVE PART IS PINNED: overscan does not lengthen the frame (262 lines either way), it takes 15 lines FROM vblank, so turning it on makes vblank SHORTER and a vblank DMA routine that was comfortable at 224 starts writing VRAM during active display. The 'renderer letterboxing' clause of criterion 1 is rf-renderer and outside this write_scope. WHY 2 AND 3 CANNOT BE BUILT HERE: both routes to 512 dots are SUB-SCREEN effects, quoted from fullsnes rather than recalled. Pseudo-hires (bit 3) is 'SHIFT SUBSCREEN HALF DOT TO THE LEFT'; true hires in modes 5/6 works because 'the main/subscreen pixels are rendered as half-pixels of the high-resolution image'. This core composes ONE screen and emits indexed pixels (law 4), so it can produce the main screen's half-dots and nothing else. Criterion 3 falls to the same cause: ALL SIX PPU/Interlace ROMs run in mode 5 (checked, not assumed), and InterlaceFont makes it unmistakable -- its whole point is sharp hires text and every glyph renders shredded with alternate columns missing. InterlaceMoogle hashes byte-identically to MosaicMode5, the same half-picture from the same cause. All six are fetched and sit in EXCLUDED in tests/peterlemon_golden.rs, ready as W7-16's acceptance evidence.

SECOND PASS 2026-08-21: CRITERION 2 NOW DELIVERED; criterion 1 was already done; criterion 3 STILL BLOCKED but for a DIFFERENT AND MUCH SMALLER REASON. W7-16 closed and shipped exactly the missing mechanism (CoreSink::sub_scanline), so the old block — "this core composes ONE screen ... the missing half is not recoverable" — stopped being true. Ppu::render_scanline_hires composes the full 512 dots for modes 5/6 and for pseudo-hires in every mode. 6 new tests; rf-snes ppu: 46 passing.

TWO THINGS THAT MADE CRITERION 2 FIT INSIDE THIS write_scope. (1) THE WIDTH TAG IS THE SLICE LENGTH: CoreSink::video_scanline already takes &[PpuPixel], so a 512-long line IS a 512-wide line and rf-core-api needed no change. Adding a separate width field would have created a second source of truth able to disagree with the data beside it — the pattern that bit this project three times in one day (shape.rs, plugin.wit, example-mode7). (2) WHICH SCREEN OWNS WHICH HALF-DOT: fullsnes defines pseudo-hires as SHIFT SUBSCREEN HALF DOT TO THE LEFT, so the SUB screen takes the even/left dot and MAIN the odd/right; true hires agrees ("main/subscreen pixels are rendered as half-pixels of the high-resolution image"). Swapping them shifts the picture half a dot, which makes a hires ROM look subtly SOFT rather than obviously wrong — an eyeball passes it, a screenshot comparison catches it, exactly like the off-by-one row this file already documents. Hires is decided from the LATCHED registers, so a mid-frame BGMODE/SETINI write changes the line it was written on rather than rewriting earlier ones.

CRITERION 3 IS BLOCKED ON VERIFICATION, NOT RENDERING — and the six waiver reasons in tests/peterlemon_golden.rs were REWRITTEN because the old ones had become FALSE (leaving them would be the example-mode7 rot again). This module pins a golden only after the frame was rendered to a PNG and LOOKED AT, a standard that CHANGED THREE OF FOUR OUTCOMES when W7-05 applied it — load-bearing, not ceremonial. PeterLemon ships a reference .png beside every ROM but scripts/fetch-peterlemon-ppu.sh fetches only .sfc, and comparing one programmatically needs a PNG decoder this workspace does not carry (a TECH_STACK row, outside this write_scope). Pinning the hash of our own unverified output would assert correctness nobody checked — the same error the old waiver warned about, one step further along. TO UNBLOCK: fetch the reference PNGs and compare programmatically, or have a human look at the six frames and pin them.
ALSO STILL OUT OF SCOPE: criterion 1’s "renderer letterboxing" clause is rf-renderer, which this write_scope (crates/rf-snes/**, scripts/**) does not include — unchanged from the first pass.

THIRD PASS 2026-08-21 — CRITERION 3 IS NOT A VERIFICATION BLOCK ANY MORE, IT IS A DEFECT. Brad looked at the six frames (the human check the previous note asked for) and called them jagged. He is right, and TWO CLAIMS THE PREVIOUS NOTE MADE ARE FALSE. (1) It said swapping the half-dot order would look 'subtly SOFT rather than obviously wrong' and that 'an eyeball passes it'. Swapping it changes 9,012 bytes of InterlaceFont and is plainly visible — and it does not matter which way round, because BOTH orders render mangled serrated glyphs. Order was never the question. (2) The real defect, MEASURED: split a composed 512-dot frame into its two half-dot planes and 55,842 of 57,344 pairs are IDENTICAL (97.4%), while each plane is individually sharp. The 512 picture is the 256 picture with columns duplicated; the residual 2.6% along glyph edges is the serration on screen. ROOT CAUSE, INSTRUMENTED NOT GUESSED: every Interlace ROM reports bg_mode=5 pseudo_hires=false, i.e. TRUE HIRES, and hires_requested() conflates two routes needing different implementations. For pseudo-hires (SETINI bit 3) interleaving two independent 256-wide renders IS the hardware and the current code is right; for modes 5/6 main and sub are the even and odd columns of ONE 512-wide picture from a DOUBLE-RATE BG FETCH, and interleaving two 256-wide renders of the same BG1 at the same scroll is a duplication, not an approximation. render_scanline_hires does the same thing on both routes — that is the bug. SETINI bit 3 is latched CORRECTLY (value & 0x08); that was checked, not assumed, because the ROM names say 'Interlace' (bit 0) and a wrong bit index produces the same signature. DO NOT PIN THESE SIX GOLDENS. AND NOTE THE GATE CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT: swapping the order left all three golden tests passing, because every mode 5/6 ROM is waived, so no gate covers render_scanline_hires at all — any fix is unverifiable until one hires golden is pinned.

CLOSED 2026-08-21 (third pass). CRITERION 3 IS GREEN: all six PeterLemon Interlace ROMs are pinned goldens, and so is MosaicMode5 — which also discharges the criterion folded in from the withdrawn W7-17. Two real defects were found and fixed, neither of them the half-dot ORDER everyone kept looking at. (1) DOUBLE-RATE FETCH: modes 5/6 are ONE 512-wide picture whose even columns feed the sub screen and odd the main, not two independent 256-wide screens interleaved — that is pseudo-hires, a different mechanism sharing the same 512 output. bg::HiresPhase now distinguishes them; hires_requested() answers 'does this line emit 512 dots?' and deliberately still answers yes to both. (2) HIRES TILE WIDTH: in modes 5/6 the $2105 size bit selects 16x8 or 16x16, so a tile is SIXTEEN half-dots wide and 32 tiles span the line. Treating it as eight read 64 tiles where 32 exist, wrapped a 32-wide tilemap, and rendered the whole line TWICE side by side — which is how it was caught, from the font chart appearing twice. Also corrected: mosaic must snap in the same space the fetch walks (512 on a hires line), or every mosaic block fills with a two-colour vertical stripe instead of a flat colour; both were rendered and looked at rather than argued. EVIDENCE: InterlaceFont renders the full printable-ASCII chart sharp; Moogle, RPG, Scroll, MystHDMA and SimpsonsHDMA all render their intended pictures; MosaicMode5 shows flat mosaic blocks. Three new unit tests in src/tests/ppu.rs, each MUTATION-CHECKED to fail on its own defect and only its own. Workspace 1617 passing (was 1614); nine-command gate green; ignored golden suite green with 7 newly pinned goldens. THE BLIND SPOT THIS CLOSES: before the pin, deliberately swapping the half-dot order left all nine gate commands AND the ignored golden suite green, because every mode 5/6 ROM sat on the excluded list — the hires path had zero coverage. Re-running that swap now FAILS the golden suite. ONE CLAUSE OF CRITERION 1 IS NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE AND NEEDS BRAD: 'the renderer letterboxing'. It is rf-renderer and this write_scope is crates/rf-snes/** + scripts/**, unchanged through all three passes. That asymmetry is deliberate — offset_per_tile masks its index to the 32 columns the dot-rate fetch implies, so a 512-space column would wrap it — but it is a CHOICE MADE WITHOUT AN ORACLE: no ROM in the PeterLemon corpus runs mode 6, no golden covers it, and no unit test exercises it.
