tickets.title: SNES DMA/HDMA: edge cases and the HDMA table walker
acceptance: HDMA ($420C) per-scanline table walker: line-counter reload semantics (repeat bit, $00 terminator), indirect-mode bank register, HDMA init at start-of-frame and per-line timing windows
HDMA/MDMA collision (HDMA steals mid-MDMA)
DMA-to-$2180 and $4300-region open-bus edge cases
PeterLemon PPU/HDMA set (WaveHDMA, RedSpaceHDMA, RedSpaceIndirectHDMA, Mode7HDMA) green as golden frames, each rendered and inspected by eye before its hash is pinned
notes: W6-02a delivered MDMA basics only, explicitly scoped to 'sufficient to boot libSFX fixture ROMs' per section 3.2. HDMA is what makes gradients, wavy effects and most split-screen HUDs work, and it feeds rf-enhance's HUD-separation heuristics (ScrollWrite + HDMA events) — so this gates W8 work too.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 1-3 COMPLETE; criterion 4 is BLOCKED on work EMULATION_CORES.md itself defers. DELIVERED: the full HDMA table walker — per-frame init latching HDMAEN, line-counter reload with the repeat flag in bit 7, the $00 terminator ending a channel for the frame, indirect mode dereferencing through the $43x7 bank, all eight channels walking independently, and the master-cycle cost. Plus a pattern-5 fix: it ALTERNATES between two registers (b, b+1, b, b+1), it does not write b once and b+1 three times.

PER-SCANLINE REGISTER LATCHING WAS THE REAL WORK, and it was not in the acceptance. EMULATION_CORES.md 3.3 specifies each scanline is composed 'from register state LATCHED AT LINE START'. Until HDMA existed, composing the whole frame from the registers' final values was indistinguishable from that, because nothing changed them mid-frame. HDMA's entire purpose is changing them mid-frame. The first wiring produced a WORSE picture than no HDMA at all — PeterLemon's Perspective went from a coherent flat track to a uniform sand texture, because all 224 lines composed from the LAST line's matrix. Ppu::line_state now latches the mode-7 matrix, BG mode and per-layer scroll once per visible line, after that line's HDMA.

THAT UNBLOCKED W7-04's PERSPECTIVE GOLDEN, which is now pinned and verified by eye: a ground plane receding to a horizon with road, grass and kerbing converging with depth, where before it was flat. RotZoom's hash is unchanged, which is the control — HDMA and line latching did not disturb the ROM that needs neither.

CRITERION 4 IS NOT ACHIEVABLE WITH A SCANLINE-COMPOSED PPU, and the evidence is direct. All eighteen undisbeliever DMA/HDMA ROMs were extracted and run: every one executes (PC advances, frames progress) but none leaves forced blank within 12,000,000 instructions — hdmaen_latch_test is still on frame 0 at that point. They are per-DOT timing tests (mid-scanline $2100/$21FF writes during HDMA, the 'scpu-a-dma-bug' family), and 3.3 states plainly that the v1 PPU is 'scanline-based ... per-dot deferred'. This criterion therefore depends on the per-dot upgrade that document already defers, not on anything missing from HDMA. RECOMMEND: move criterion 4 onto a per-dot PPU ticket, or amend it to the PeterLemon HDMA ROMs, which a scanline PPU can express.

STATUS SET TO `blocked`, NOT `in_progress` (2026-08-20): validate-plan's P8 rule forbids two concurrently-active tickets with overlapping write_scope, and W7-04 and W7-07 both write crates/rf-snes/**. `blocked` is also the truthful status: each one's own work is committed and each is waiting on a DIFFERENT ticket, not on more effort here. Caught by the validator after the commit rather than before it — a reminder that leaving two partially-done tickets open at once is itself a board state worth checking.

RULING (Brad, 2026-08-20, in response to the unattended loop’s four blocking questions). Amend acceptance rather than leave this blocked, exactly as this ticket’s own HANDOFF recommended. CRITERION 4 IS REPLACED with the PeterLemon HDMA set, VERIFIED TO EXIST at the pinned commit 350b394e: PPU/HDMA/{WaveHDMA,RedSpaceHDMA,RedSpaceIndirectHDMA,Mode7HDMA}/*.sfc. These are per-SCANLINE HDMA effects — gradients and wave distortion driven by per-line register writes — which is precisely what the line-latching this ticket already built can express. The undisbeliever per-dot timing ROMs are NOT abandoned: they remain W7-15’s criterion 2, which already exists and depends on this ticket.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: criterion 4 delivered against the amended acceptance. WaveHDMA (per-line $210D scroll -> a rippling water surface) and Mode7HDMA (BG mode switched mid-frame -> sky and trees above a mode-7 ground plane) are PINNED, each rendered and looked at. The RedSpace pair is EXCLUDED, and the reason is worth keeping: their HDMA is verifiably CORRECT -- the trace shows $2121 <- $00 then $2122 <- $1F, $1E, $1D, one step every 7 lines, 32 steps over 224, and the indirect variant dereferences its pointer to the identical gradient, which is direct evidence criterion 1's indirect-mode bank register works -- but the demos draw nothing but the backdrop, so every pixel is palette index 0 and an index-domain hash cannot see the effect at all. Covered instead by tests::hdma::hdma_writes_a_different_backdrop_colour_on_each_line, which runs without a fetched ROM. Noted on W7-16, which owns making colour-domain output reachable. 17 goldens green, every previously-pinned hash byte-identical.

tickets.title: S-DSP: echo, gaussian interpolation, ADSR/GAIN
acceptance: gaussian interpolation filter, ADSR and GAIN envelopes, echo (with its ARAM buffer and FIR filter), pitch modulation and noise
SPC timing suites pass; BRR decoding is sample-exact (FR-CORE-036)
audio RMS comparison against a reference for a designated SPC set
notes: BLOCK CORRECTED 2026-09-15, NOT CLEARED. The recorded blocker was "behind W7-18 (the SPC700 charges time per memory access)" — and W7-18 CLOSED 2026-08-27 on ruling D-3. That sentence had been false for two and a half weeks and nobody re-read it; it was found by auditing the board, not by working the ticket. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE TODAY, measured by the local gate on 2026-09-15: the four blargg SPC ROMs still do not report a pass. spc_dsp6 prints "Echo/basics Passed 01" — subtest 1 of many, which is the exact shape of the false-green that reopened this ticket on 2026-08-27 — spc_timer prints "Failed 02", spc_smp prints hashes, and spc_mem_access_times is the D-3 known-red that belongs to W7-17. So this stays BLOCKED, but on an open question rather than on a closed ticket: nobody has diagnosed whether the remaining subtests are S-DSP work (this ticket) or SPC700 timing work (W7-17's half), and that diagnosis is itself a session. Do not claim this expecting implementation work until it has been done.

W6-04b delivered a SKELETON on purpose — BRR decode plus eight-voice mixing — with sample-exactness deferred here. What it did NOT implement is named in its close note and in the dsp module doc, so this ticket's scope is already written down rather than needing rediscovery.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criterion 1 COMPLETE; criteria 2 and 3 are blocked, one on a real deadlock and one on material that does not exist. DELIVERED: Gaussian interpolation, ADSR and GAIN envelopes, echo with its ARAM ring buffer and 8-tap FIR, pitch modulation, and the noise LFSR — all wired into the mixer, not merely defined.

THE UNITY-GAIN TEST EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY. A resampling kernel whose four taps do not sum to a constant changes VOLUME WITH PITCH, so a sustained note swells or fades as it bends — the subtlest possible audio bug. The first table used a triangular-squared window and summed to 4080; the test caught it on the first run. The kernel is now built from the CUBIC B-SPLINE basis, which is a partition of unity by construction, plus an exact integer correction: fractions f and 255-f read the SAME four indices, so there are 128 independent sums and index f belongs to only one pair — which is why the correction loop runs to 128 and not 256 (running it to 256 double-corrects every pair and leaves the table worse than it started). Every fraction now sums to exactly 2048.

NAMED HONESTLY: this is a bell-shaped, low-pass kernel of the same family as the hardware's, NOT the S-DSP's exact 512-entry ROM table. Reproducing that byte-for-byte belongs with the sample-exactness work (FR-CORE-036), and the module doc says so rather than letting the constant's name imply more than it delivers.

THE ECHO BUFFER IS ARAM, and the model expresses that rather than hiding it in a private buffer — a game that miscomputes ESA/EDL really can have its echo overwrite its own samples, and a test asserts the ring buffer starts at ESA*256 and does not touch memory below it. $6C bit 5 disables WRITES while still reading, which is how games freeze an echo tail without clearing it; tested in both directions.

PMON BIT 0 DOES NOTHING, because voice 0 has no predecessor to be modulated by. A model that wrapped to voice 7 would sound plausible and be wrong, so there is a test that runs an identical voice with and without PMON bit 0 and requires bit-identical output.

CRITERION 2 IS BLOCKED ON A REAL DEADLOCK, and the diagnosis carries good news with it. gilyon's spctest.sfc was run: the HLE BOOT HANDSHAKE COMPLETES WITH A REAL COMMERCIAL-STYLE ROM (boot state reaches Running and the APU executes uploaded code at $0306-$0309), which is the first end-to-end validation of W6-04b's HLE. But the two processors then deadlock — the 65816 spins at $00:818E and the SPC700 loops between $0306 and $0309, each waiting on a port value the other never writes — so test_num never leaves 0 across 40,000,000 instructions. That is a post-boot port-protocol bug, not a DSP one, and it belongs to the CPU<->APU ports rather than to this ticket. RECOMMEND filing it against W6-04b's area.

CRITERION 3 HAS NO MATERIAL. It asks for 'audio RMS comparison against a reference for a designated SPC set'. No SPC set is designated anywhere in the board, tests/rom-manifest.toml or docs/TESTING.md, and no reference audio exists to compare against. RECOMMEND: designate the set and its reference, or amend the criterion — as written it cannot be satisfied by any amount of implementation work.

FINDING FROM W7-09 (2026-08-20): THE S-DSP IS WIRED TO NOTHING. Verified three ways: (1) `grep` for `.mix(` across crates/rf-snes/src finds calls ONLY in tests/dsp.rs and tests/apu_ports.rs -- no production path mixes audio; (2) `Apu` never touches `self.dsp` except in the save-state code W7-09 just added; (3) $F3 (DSP DATA) has NO write arm in Apu::write_register at all, and its read arm returns a literal 0 with the comment 'DSP data - W6-04b'. So an SPC700 program cannot program a single DSP register, and a running machine produces no sound whatever this ticket's voices, BRR decode, echo and Gaussian interpolation do in isolation. This is the same disconnected-pipeline class as W6-03a's two VRAM buffers and W7-04's unwired $2134-$2136: every unit test passes because each unit is correct, and nothing assembles them. Whoever unblocks this ticket should treat 'the DSP register map at $F2/$F3 plus mixing into the audio output' as part of the work, and add an end-to-end test that runs SPC700 code which programs a voice and asserts non-silence -- a unit test on Dsp cannot catch a missing connection.

RE-DERIVED 2026-08-20, and the diagnosis is now MUCH sharper -- the old one ('a post-boot port-protocol bug, belongs to W6-04b') was true but not actionable. Two distinct causes, one FIXED HERE and one identified. (1) FIXED: THE IPL HAND-OVER NEVER ECHOED. The CPU's upload loop is `STA $2140` then `CMP $2140 / BNE` -- it spins until the counter comes back, and the jump signal is no exception. BootAction::Run carried no echo, so control passed to the uploaded program while the 65816 waited for a byte that would never arrive. Read straight out of spctest's own code: ROM $8180 is `STX $2142 / STZ $2141 / INC A / INC A / STA $2140 / CMP $2140 / BNE`, and ARAM $0300 is `MOV $F4,#$00 / MOV $F1,#$00 / CMP $F5,#$01 / BNE` -- the SPC waits for port 1 to become 1, the CPU waits for its echo. BootAction::Run now carries `echo` and the caller writes it before handing over. (2) STILL BLOCKING, AND IT IS A TIMING BUG: SnesBus::catch_up_apu computes `spc_cycles = apu_debt / 21` and then runs that many ITERATIONS OF ONE INSTRUCTION EACH. Instructions are not one cycle. The APU therefore outruns the CPU by 2-5x, and traced directly: on the first `$2140` read after hand-over the SPC has ALREADY executed `MOV $F4,#$00` on 34 master cycles of debt (1 SPC cycle) when that instruction costs 5, so it clobbers the echo before the CPU can see it. THE ROOT FIX IS A PER-OPCODE CYCLE TABLE FOR THE SPC700, which has none at all: Spc700::step returns Result<(), u8> and ops.rs counts nothing. That is squarely this ticket's criterion 2 ('SPC timing suites pass') and is the next piece of work here.

ROOT BLOCKER FIXED 2026-08-21, and GILYON CPUTEST NOW PASSES: test_num=0x0649/0x0649 with the ROM writing its own "Success" after 6.7M instructions. That is the ROM whose port handshake the previous note traced to this bug, and it decides its own verdict, so it is a far stronger signal than any unit test. THE BUG, exactly as that note predicted: the SPC700 had NO per-opcode cycle table. Apu::step charged a flat 2 cycles per instruction (its comment called cycle counts "the cycle-accurate executor’s business"), and SnesBus::catch_up_apu computed a CYCLE budget then spent it as INSTRUCTIONS — so the APU ran 2-5x fast and clobbered port echoes before the 65816 could read them.

THE TABLE IS DERIVED FROM THE VECTORS, NOT TRANSCRIBED — crates/rf-snes/src/apu/spc700/timing.rs. Each SingleStepTests case carries a per-cycle bus-event array, so cycles.len() IS that execution’s cost. Across 256 opcodes x 1000 cases: 228 fixed, 28 variable, and the variance is ALWAYS exactly +2 — those 28 being precisely the Bcc, BBS/BBC, CBNE and DBNZ forms. Writing 256 numbers from memory is how a plausible-but-subtly-wrong emulator gets made, so spc700_cycle_table_matches_the_vectors RE-DERIVES the table from the same data and fails if one entry drifts; table and oracle cannot disagree silently. It also pins the two facts the table’s SHAPE depends on: exactly which opcodes vary, and that taken always costs +2. Branch outcomes are read from the single ops::branch helper every conditional branch routes through — the one place that knows — rather than reconstructed from a PC delta, which would need per-instruction lengths. A HALTED core still costs ONE cycle: charging zero is what froze the clock in W7-15’s investigation, since WAI waits for an interrupt that only arrives when cycles are spent. Overspend carries into the next catch-up so the APU cannot drift ahead one rounding error at a time.

STILL OPEN, and this ticket stays BLOCKED. Criterion 1 is the DSP work and is untouched: gaussian interpolation, ADSR/GAIN envelopes, echo with its ARAM buffer and FIR filter, pitch modulation and noise. Criterion 2 is now HALF met — the SPC timing suites pass (spc700 vectors 2/2, gilyon Success) but BRR sample-exactness (FR-CORE-036) is unverified. Criterion 3 needs an audio RMS comparison against a reference for a DESIGNATED SPC set, and no such set is designated or fetched — check that it exists and is licence-clear BEFORE claiming, the way W9-06’s note demands, or this stalls the way W7-05/W7-08/W7-11 did on artifacts that did not exist.

CORRECTION 2026-08-21, to the note above that I wrote hours earlier: "criterion 1 is the DSP work and is untouched" IS FALSE, and I asserted it without reading the code — I took dsp.rs’s module doc at its word. ALL FIVE features criterion 1 names ARE implemented and wired into Dsp::mix: the Gaussian interpolation kernel (with a unity-gain test), ADSR/GAIN envelopes, echo (ARAM ring buffer, 8-tap FIR, feedback, per-channel volume, FLG bit-5 write-disable), pitch modulation (including the voice-0 exception PMON bit 0 requires) and the noise LFSR. crates/rf-snes/src/tests/dsp.rs carries 14 tests over them. The dsp.rs module doc was STALE — it still described W6-04b’s skeleton scope — and has been corrected. This is the FOURTH stale second-source-of-truth found in one session (shape.rs, plugin.wit, example-mode7, now this), and the first where the stale doc propagated into the PLAN: W7-08’s notes repeated the absence as fact and scoped the remaining work around it.

SO WHERE W7-08 ACTUALLY STANDS: criterion 1 appears MET (implemented + unit-tested), though nobody has verified those numbers against hardware. Criterion 2 is HALF met — the SPC timing suites now pass (spc700 vectors 2/2, gilyon Success) but BRR SAMPLE-EXACTNESS (FR-CORE-036) is unverified. Criterion 3 is the one that would settle both: an audio RMS comparison against a reference for a DESIGNATED SPC set, and no such set is designated or fetched. IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED IS NOT VERIFIED AGAINST THE MACHINE — that distinction is the whole remaining content of this ticket, and it is why criterion 3 should be checked for an obtainable, licence-clear reference set BEFORE anyone claims this.

SCOPE AMENDMENT + RULING (Brad, 2026-08-21): criterion 3 is AMENDED. It asked for 'audio RMS comparison against a reference for a designated SPC set'; that reference audio DOES NOT EXIST and cannot be sourced — SPC files are commercial game-music rips, no canonical hardware rendering is published, and generating one from another emulator would prove AGREEMENT WITH THAT EMULATOR, not correctness. Criterion 3 now reads: the designated SPC set is blargg's recovered SPC test ROMs and the verdict is the ROMs' own. THE SET, and this FINISHES A '[thin]' FLAG tests/rom-manifest.toml has carried since W0 (see its Known-gaps header: 'blargg SPC timing ... canonical blargg.org home is dead, names gitlab.com/higan/snes-test-roms as a [thin] candidate mirror; the exact ROM path/filename inside it was not located this session'). It is blargg-spc-6/ at commit 26e8aa91e0d3b90b901e7e693bc4a8244b391d7b: spc_dsp6.sfc, spc_smp.sfc, spc_timer.sfc, spc_mem_access_times.sfc. Same repository that already supplies gilyon/, whose cputest gave this ticket its strongest signal to date. Repo license NONE, so the same no-license-grant-fetch-only posture as the other 81 artifacts applies. Fetched and hashed rather than assumed live. WHY THIS IS A BETTER ORACLE THAN THE CRITERION IT REPLACES: a self-verdicting ROM decides pass/fail itself, where an RMS threshold is a number someone picks. spc_dsp6.sfc also attacks criterion 2's still-unverified BRR sample-exactness (FR-CORE-036). THE HONEST LIMIT, quoted from byuu in the set's own README rather than paraphrased: 'passing these tests are not a proof of correctness as such. What they are, to me, is a proof of correctness of blargg's DSP core.' So this verifies against the reference IMPLEMENTATION, not against silicon. That is still a large step up from 'implemented and unit-tested', which the note above correctly calls the whole remaining content of this ticket. write_scope gains crates/rf-harness/** and tests/** to reach the manifest.

PROGRESS 2026-08-21, AND A MUCH SHARPER BLOCKER — STILL BLOCKED, NOT DONE. WHAT IS FINISHED: the designation. All four blargg SPC ROMs are pinned in tests/rom-manifest.toml by sha256 at stable raw URLs (commit 26e8aa91), fetched and hash-verified, and the manifest's '[thin]' Known-gaps entry that had stood since W0 is closed with the path it was missing. crates/rf-snes/tests/blargg_spc.rs is the acceptance test criterion 3 now designates. WHAT IS NOT: it is KNOWN-RED, deliberately — written before the thing it tests works so the ticket has an oracle instead of an opinion. THE FINDING, and it is stronger than the one already on this ticket: spc_dsp6.sfc boots, prints 'Running tests:' then 'Echo/basics', and NEVER ADVANCES — byte-identical screen at 20M, 40M and 60M instructions while the frame counter keeps climbing, so the 65816 runs and the test does not. CAUSE, confirmed in code: Apu::write_register has NO 0xF3 arm at all and its read arm is a literal `0xF3 => 0`. $F2/$F3 are the ONLY path from an SPC700 program to a DSP register, so no game and no test ROM can program one and every read-back is zero. W7-09 found this statically and it was recorded here; AN OUTSIDE ROM HAS NOW CONFIRMED IT INDEPENDENTLY and named the exact test that dies, which is a materially stronger claim than a grep. DO NOT ASSUME ONE CAUSE COVERS FOUR: all four ROMs stall on their own first test — spc_dsp6 'Echo/basics', spc_smp 'CPU Instructions/Edge arith', spc_timer 'timer read vs write', spc_mem_access_times 'mem access times'. The $F2/$F3 gap explains spc_dsp6 directly and is a PLAUSIBLE common cause for the rest, but that has not been traced, and spc_smp stalling inside a CPU-instruction test is exactly the detail that turns a tidy single-cause story into a wrong one. Isolate each before believing one fix covers four. WHAT UNBLOCKING NEEDS: a 128-byte S-DSP register file plus the $F2/$F3 plumbing. Dsp holds structured state (voices, noise, echo, a few named registers) with NO register-map layer, so this is real implementation work, not a wiring one-liner — which is why it was not attempted in the same pass rather than half-done. Until it exists, criterion 1's five DSP features are unreachable from a running machine however well their unit tests pass, and criterion 2's BRR sample-exactness has no oracle. That is the same 'implemented and tested is not verified against the machine' gap this ticket's earlier notes name as its whole remaining content — now with a designated set to measure it against.

S-DSP NOW REACHABLE AND CLOCKED 2026-08-21 — and it did NOT make blargg's ROMs pass, which is why the note above said not to assume one cause covered four. SHIPPED: a 128-byte DSP register file (Dsp::regs) with read_register/write_register covering the full $00-$7F map, the $F2/$F3 plumbing in Apu (there was no 0xF3 WRITE arm at all and the read arm was a literal 0), and a 32-cycle sample clock — 1.024 MHz / 32 kHz — driving Dsp::mix from Apu::step_counted. BEING PROGRAMMABLE IS NOT THE SAME AS RUNNING: mix() was called from nothing but tests, so without the clock nothing would advance an envelope, set ENDX or move the echo buffer. Both halves are mutation-checked: reverting the $F3 read to 0 fails one test, and deleting the tick_dsp CALL (while leaving the function) fails another — the second was written only after the first version of that test passed the mutation, because it exercised tick_dsp directly and never asked whether anything called it. That is the same shape as the defect itself. Key-on resolves the sample address through the $5D DIR directory AT KEY-ON, not at SRCN-write time, because the ordinary program order is SRCN first and DIR second; out-of-range DIR/SRCN reads as zero rather than panicking. ENVX/OUTX/ENDX read live state, never the last byte written. 10 new tests; rf-snes dsp 25 passing; workspace 1627. THE REMAINING BLOCKER IS THE IPL BOOT HLE, NOT THE DSP, and it is now traced rather than guessed. Profiling spc_dsp6 at 20M instructions: the 65816 spins in a two-instruction port-wait at $00:815C/$815F (9.5M hits each) while the SPC700's PC sits at $C11F where ARAM IS ALL ZEROS — it is NOP-sliding through empty memory, $00 being a NOP. boot.is_running() is true, ipl_enabled is false, ports read apu->cpu [CC,BB,00,00] with the CPU having written counter $00 and data $20. So IplBoot::cpu_wrote took its BootState::Ready 'just run' branch — the one gated on ports_in[1]==0 when $CC lands — and jumped to an address nothing was uploaded to. NEXT STEP, and do not skip it: LOG WHAT BLARGG'S UPLOADER ACTUALLY WRITES to $2140-$2143 and in what order before changing cpu_wrote. This ticket has already spent one cycle on a plausible port-protocol theory that was true and not actionable.

BOOT HANDSHAKE FIXED 2026-08-21 — AND IT WAS NEVER THE DSP. The HLE was EDGE-TRIGGERED ON THE CPU'S STORE. blargg's uploader starts a transfer with a 16-bit STA $2140, which lands as TWO byte writes, port 0 FIRST — traced with a port logger, not assumed: 'idx=0 val=CC ports_in before [00,00,00,04]' then 'idx=1 val=01 ports_in before [CC,00,00,04]'. So IplBoot read the kind byte one instruction early, saw 0, and took the 'transfer nothing, just run' branch — jumping to $0400 with nothing uploaded there. The SPC700 then NOP-slid through empty ARAM ($00 is a NOP) at $C11F while the 65816 spun at $00:815C waiting for a counter echo that could never come. FIX: IplBoot::poll is level-triggered on the APU's clock, which is what the real IPL IS — a polling program that cannot observe a half-finished write. Polling is naturally idempotent because every accepted value advances the value being waited for. Called from BOTH Apu::step_counted and the boot branch of SnesBus::catch_up_apu, and the second is not optional: catch_up_apu deliberately does NOT call step_counted while the handshake still owns the machine, so polling only in step_counted left the handshake frozen forever — caught by re-running the trace rather than by assuming the first call site was enough. CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: the handshake now completes one APU tick AFTER the final port write, so a CPU that halts on the very next instruction never sees it. The game-shaped-init test grew a `LDA $2140` before its STP for exactly that reason; real init code always goes on to do something. VERIFIED: upload runs to completion (Transferring 0,1,2,3... storing $20,$45,$63,$68 with correct echoes), the SPC executes blargg's code, and there are 9,009 port-state changes in 8M instructions — both processors live and conversing. gilyon cputest STILL PASSES and the PeterLemon goldens still pass, checked because a boot-model change could plausibly break them. 2 new tests, mutation-checked: re-introducing edge-triggering fails them. workspace 1629. CAUSE 3 IS OPEN AND IS NOT YET CHARACTERISED. All four ROMs still print only their FIRST test name, unchanged at 40M/80M/120M/160M/200M instructions. That rules OUT a dead SPC, a failed upload and a stalled handshake; it does NOT say why the first test never completes. DO NOT ASSUME CAUSE 3 IS ONE BUG OR THE SAME BUG IN ALL FOUR. NEXT STEP: PC-histogram the SPC700 inside the uploaded program and find what it is waiting on — the same technique that found cause 2. Trace first; every cause so far has been something other than the plausible one.

CAUSE 3 IDENTIFIED 2026-08-21 — AND IT IS NOT A BUG, IT IS THE IPL RULING. With causes 1 and 2 fixed the SPC700 sits at exactly ONE PC forever: $0495, in all four ROMs, for all 10,000,000 sampled instructions (distinct SPC PCs: 1). The uploaded code there reads MOV A,!$FFC0 / CMP A,#$CD / BNE $0495 / JMP !$FFC0 — it reads IPL ROM byte 0 as DATA, spins forever unless it is $CD, and then EXECUTES the IPL. It reads $EF, because IPL_STUB is [0xEF; 64] — ours, per law 5 and Brad's 2026-08-20 ruling extending it to 'not in a fetch list either'. apu/mod.rs's OWN DOC PREDICTED THIS AND GOT THE POPULATION WRONG: it said 'a program that reads IPL bytes as data sees our stub ... No commercial title is known to do that.' The commercial half is still true. But TEST ROMs do it, and test ROMs are the things that verify this emulator. Corrected in place (RF-L-11). WHAT SHIPPED: Apu::set_ipl_rom, the 'user supplies it' door the ruling explicitly left open. NO BYTES WERE ADDED — nothing is shipped, fetched or embedded. Point RF_SPC_IPL_ROM at a 64-byte dump of your own console's IPL and the suite runs; without one it SKIPS rather than fails, because a missing artifact is not a defect and that is the posture every other artifact-gated suite here takes. 3 new tests; workspace 1631. W7-08 STAYS BLOCKED AND HERE IS THE HONEST REASON: criterion 3 cannot be VERIFIED in this environment, because verifying it needs a Nintendo boot ROM this project will never contain. That is no longer an unknown — it is a consequence of a ruling, and the ruling is the right one. A DECISION IS AVAILABLE IF BRAD WANTS ONE, NOT TAKEN HERE: a CLEAN-ROOM IPL — writing the documented boot ROM ourselves in SPC700 assembly — would be our code rather than Nintendo's bytes, and blargg only compares the FIRST byte before jumping, so functional equivalence rather than byte equivalence is what it actually needs. The risk is obvious and is why it is not being taken unilaterally: a faithful reimplementation of a 64-byte ROM plausibly converges on identical bytes, which is precisely the line law 5 draws. Brad's call.

THE BLOCKER IS SOLVED 2026-08-23 — WITHOUT A BOOT ROM, AND WITHOUT THE CLEAN-ROOM ASSEMBLY BRAD HAD AUTHORISED. The ticket stays OPEN, but for a completely different and far better reason: the ROMs now RUN and REPORT REAL ACCURACY VERDICTS instead of hanging. BRAD'S RULING 2026-08-23 was 'we dont want ipl stored in github, if you can download one from online to test with that is good. and i accept the risks'. Downloading Nintendo's copyrighted firmware was DECLINED — that is the infringing act itself, not a risk to accept on someone's behalf. Clean-room assembly was authorised instead. It then turned out to be UNNECESSARY, which verifying the mechanism first is what revealed. WHAT THE ROMS ACTUALLY NEED, measured rather than assumed: (1) $FFC0 to read $CD, and (2) the JMP !$FFC0 to do something. Probing with a marked IPL showed ipl_enabled=true at the check (so the window IS banked in — the worry that handover banked it out was unfounded) and that byte 0 = $CD alone gets PAST the spin loop, after which the ROM executes whatever is there. THE SOLUTION IS ONE CONSTANT AND ONE HLE HOOK. IPL_STUB byte 0 is $CD — a COMPATIBILITY CONSTANT programs read as data, not borrowed code, and incidentally just the opcode for MOV X,#imm, which any boot ROM setting up a stack pointer begins with. Apu::reenter_ipl HLEs the jump-back: a real boot ROM re-runs its handshake on re-entry, so this re-arms IplBoot to Ready, republishes $AA/$BB and halts the SPC700 until BootAction::Run hands it back. NO NINTENDO BYTES, NO DOWNLOAD, AND NO 64 BYTES OF CLEAN-ROOM ASSEMBLY whose faithful reimplementation would plausibly have converged on the original anyway — which is exactly the law 5 risk Brad was accepting. It also EXTENDS his 2026-08-20 HLE ruling to the one case it did not anticipate rather than reversing it. RF_SPC_IPL_ROM still overrides the stub for anyone with a real dump; nothing requires it. WHAT THE ORACLE NOW SAYS, and this is the deliverable: spc_dsp6 'Running tests: Echo/basics Failed 03'; spc_smp 'E0 AB34EA3A E4 05599DAA ED 442B1C4D Passed 01'; spc_timer 'timer read vs write 1111111222'; spc_mem_access_times 'E6 -- -- R1 E7 -- -- R0 ... EB -- -- R0'. Those are ACCURACY results, not infrastructure failures — spc_dsp6 ran the echo test and judged it wrong, spc_smp passed one group and printed hashes for three more. This is the first external oracle this project's S-DSP and SPC timing have ever had. WHY THE TICKET STAYS OPEN, honestly: criterion 2 wants the SPC timing suites to PASS and criterion 3 wants the designated set green. They run and report; they report failures. Closing on 'the ROMs execute' would be exactly the ceremonial-green this project keeps catching. The remaining work is DSP and timing ACCURACY — starting with the echo unit and the envelope rates, which dsp.rs's own doc already admits are modelled as a proportional step rather than the hardware rate table. That is now measurable for the first time. workspace 1645 passing; ten-command gate + docs-gate green.

THREE REAL DSP BUGS FIXED 2026-08-23, each caught by the oracle and each VERIFIED AGAINST A SOURCE rather than reasoned about. (1) ECHO BUFFER AT EDL=0 was 16 bytes on the written-down assumption of 'a 4-sample minimum'. It is FOUR bytes — one stereo sample. SNESdev/sneslab: 'when EDL=0, the buffer is 4 bytes (1 sample) rather than 0'. A unit test had the wrong number baked into it with that same assumption as its comment. (2) THE FIR FILTER was computed as sum-of-eight-taps then one >>7 then one clamp. The hardware sequence is: >>6 PER TAP; taps 0-6 CLIP BY WRAPPING at 16 bits while tap 7 CLAMPS; and the result is masked & 0xFFFE because the echo buffer is 15-bit left-aligned. Three separate differences, none of them visible without the reference. Tap ORDER was already right — FIR[0]/$0F multiplies the oldest sample, FIR[7]/$7F the newest. (3) ENVX AND OUTX ARE NOT READ-ONLY. They were modelled as computed-live with writes ignored, and I had written a test ASSERTING that, reasoning that returning a written value 'would be a convincing lie: a program polling ENVX for an envelope to decay would spin forever'. That reasoning was wrong. SNESdev: 'VxENVX is technically writable and not intended to be written to. The S-DSP updates this register once per sample.' Both halves matter — the write sticks, AND the next sample lands on it, which is what stops a poller spinning. They are now ordinary register-file storage that Dsp::mix overwrites once per sample. THE ROM IS WHAT CAUGHT IT: spc_dsp6's very first check writes $88 to $08 and reads it straight back; it read 00 and the ROM gave up. It now reads 88, and the test progresses from 8 DSP reads to 24. WHY spc_dsp6 STILL SAYS 'Failed 03', now understood rather than guessed. Tracing every $F2/$F3 access shows the failing check writes $88 to ENVX and then COUNTS HOW MANY READS SURVIVE before the DSP overwrites it: 4, then 1, then 1, then 0. It is measuring WHERE INSIDE THE 32-CYCLE SAMPLE the DSP writes voice 0's ENVX. Dsp::mix updates all eight voices at once at sample granularity, so that count is an artefact of where the CPU happened to be rather than a modelled cycle. SO THE REMAINING WORK IS A CYCLE-ACCURATE S-DSP, and that is an ARCHITECTURAL change, not a bug fix. blargg's own README says his DSP is 'the first DSP emulator with cycle accuracy, properly emulating every DSP register and memory access at the exact SPC cycle it occurs at, whereas previous DSP emulators emulated these only to the nearest sample (which occurs every 32 clocks)' — this suite exists to test exactly that, which is why byuu called it invaluable. Fragments of the schedule are documented (sneslab: echo left inserted on the ring buffer at cycle 22 and written at cycle 29, right at 23 and 30, FIR coefficients read across cycles 22-25; anomie: EFB accessed at cycle 26, PMON at 27) but a COMPLETE per-cycle table was not located in this pass. NOTHING REGRESSED: 25 DSP unit tests, all 32 PeterLemon goldens, gilyon, undisbeliever and region suites green. workspace 1645 passing; ten-command gate + docs-gate green.

BLOCKED 2026-08-23 ON A DOCUMENTED PER-CYCLE SCHEDULE — Brad's call, on my recommendation. This is a DIFFERENT AND MUCH BETTER BLOCK than the one this ticket carried for weeks: it was 'no oracle exists and the ROMs hang forever'; it is now 'the oracle works, it names a specific architectural gap, and closing that gap needs a spec we do not have'. WHAT IS BANKED. Criterion 1 is met. The S-DSP is reachable ($F2/$F3 register file), clocked (32 cycles per sample), and the boot path works without any boot ROM. Three real accuracy bugs are fixed and verified against sources — the EDL=0 echo buffer size, the FIR's per-tap shift and wrap/clamp/mask sequence, and ENVX/OUTX being writable storage rather than read-only. blargg's four ROMs run and report real verdicts. WHAT REMAINS, precisely: criteria 2 and 3 need a CYCLE-ACCURATE S-DSP — a 32-step state machine placing every register and memory access at its exact SPC cycle. This is not optional polish for these ROMs; it is what they exist to test. blargg's README: his is 'the first DSP emulator with cycle accuracy, properly emulating every DSP register and memory access at the exact SPC cycle it occurs at, whereas previous DSP emulators emulated these only to the nearest sample'. The failing check measures exactly that — it writes $88 to ENVX and counts how many reads survive before the DSP lands on it. WHY IT IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN JUST HARD, and this is the honest part: I do not have the complete 32-cycle schedule. Fragments are documented (sneslab: echo left inserted at cycle 22 and written at 29, right at 23 and 30, FIR coefficients read across 22-25; anomie: EFB at 26, PMON at 27) but no full table for all eight voices was located. Without a spec, implementing this means guessing placements and using a pass/fail ROM as a search oracle — which is slow and can converge on something that passes without being right, and this project has already caught three plausible-but-wrong models this week. THE OTHER REASON IT IS BRAD'S CALL: the most likely complete source is emulator SOURCE CODE (snes_spc, ares), which is GPL. Reading it to reimplement is the same tainting question as the IPL, in a different family. NOT taken unilaterally. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT, any one of: (a) anomie's full apudsp.txt or an equivalent doc carrying the complete per-cycle table — the canonical host's certificate has expired, so a live mirror is needed; (b) a ruling that reading GPL emulator source to extract TIMING FACTS (as opposed to code) is acceptable; (c) hardware measurement, which needs a console and a capture rig; (d) amending criteria 2 and 3 to what a sample-granular DSP can honestly claim, and filing the cycle-accurate DSP as its own ticket. (d) is probably the right shape if this is ever picked up: cycle accuracy is a phase of work, not a criterion buried in an 8-point DSP ticket.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-26. The missing per-cycle schedule EXISTS and has been located: **Anomie's S-DSP Doc** (with updates by jwdonal), $Revision: 1212$, 2015-09-28 — `apudsp.txt`, its 'SOUND GENERATION' section, 'The full sample generation loop is as follows'. It gives all 32 cycles explicitly, including the three things this ticket is blocked on.

ECHO, verbatim from that source: cycle 22 'Load left channel sample from the echo buffer. Load FFC0'; cycle 23 'Load right channel sample from the echo buffer. Load FFC1 and FFC2'; cycles 24-25 load FFC3-FFC7; cycle 29 'Write left channel sample to the echo buffer, if allowed by ECENx. Load EDL - if the current echo offset is 0, apply EDL. Load ESA for future use.'; cycle 30 'Write right channel sample to the echo buffer... Increment the echo offset, and set to 0 if it exceeds the buffer length.' That EDL-applies-only-at-offset-0 detail is exactly the class of bug this ticket already fixed once by hand (the EDL=0 buffer size).
GAUSSIAN: the document specifies 4-point gaussian interpolation against a 512-entry coefficient table, with the interpolation index selecting coefficients across four adjacent BRR samples.
ADSR/GAIN: envelope updates are driven by a global counter — 'Update global counter' is cycle 29 in the loop — with per-rate periods from every sample (R=31) upward.

PROVENANCE, and it matters here: this is published documentation, which is exactly what NFR-011's clean-room standard asks for. Cite it in the doc comments the way nesdev/fullsnes are cited elsewhere. Do NOT transcribe from a bsnes or ares implementation — that is the provenance NFR-011 rules out no matter how convenient.
The oracle that made this ticket productive (blargg's SPC ROMs, running and reporting since W7-08's earlier work) is the thing that will say whether the schedule was implemented correctly.

THE DSP HALF IS DONE AND THE ORACLE SAYS SO, 2026-08-27. spc_dsp6.sfc reports 'Echo/basics Passed 01'. It had said 'Failed 03' since 2026-08-23 and was the one specific gap this ticket was blocked on. Two of the four designated ROMs now pass (spc_dsp6, spc_smp); spc_smp went from stalling in 'Edge arith' to passing without any change aimed at it. WHAT WAS BUILT: anomie's 32-cycle schedule, transcribed verbatim into a table and driven one SPC cycle at a time. Dsp::tick is the engine and Dsp::mix is a wrapper that runs 32 of them, so there is one model of a sample rather than two. The point is the prepared->visible split — ENDX prepared at S5 and readable at S7, OUTX at S6/S8, ENVX at S7/S9 — which is what the suite measures and which a sample-granular mixer cannot express at all. Two tests pin the exact cycles. Also landed from the same document: the real global counter with its rate AND offset tables replacing a proportional approximation that admitted as much in its own doc comment; ADSR as the documented pretend-GAIN decode rather than three hand-transcribed rate tables; KON/KOFF latched and polled at cycle 30 every other sample over a 64-cycle loop; the echo split across cycles 22-30; rate-gated noise. The save-state never carried the DSP register file at all — a restored state read back zeros for every register a program had written — and now carries it plus the loop position and latches. HOW THE LAST BUG WAS FOUND, because the method mattered more than the fix. The obvious suspect was CPU/DSP alignment: Apu::step_counted runs a whole instruction and only then advances the DSP, so a $F3 read is up to five cycles stale, and the failing check counts reads. That would have justified a sub-instruction bus-timing refactor of the SPC700 — days of work. It was TESTED instead: crates/rf-snes/tests/spc_dsp6_phase_probe.rs runs the ROM at all 32 starting phases. All 32 failed identically, which rules alignment out, because no alignment existed that fixed it. The real causes were three echo details read LIVE where hardware LATCHES: EDL is '----dddd' and only four bits wide (the whole byte was used, allowing a 512 KiB ring inside a 64 KiB ARAM); the ring length is latched only when the offset is 0, so a new EDL can take up to .24s to take effect; and ESA is latched at cycle 29 for the next sample. The probe is kept, now asserting that all 32 phases agree, so the disproved refactor is not reached for again. WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS A SPLIT DECISION FOR BRAD, NOT A SCOPE CALL I SHOULD TAKE. spc_timer.sfc fails in 'timer read vs write' and spc_mem_access_times.sfc in memory access timing. NEITHER IS S-DSP WORK — neither touches dsp.rs, and this ticket is titled 'S-DSP: echo, gaussian interpolation, ADSR/GAIN'. Note 22's own warning applies: DO NOT ASSUME ONE CAUSE COVERS FOUR. Critically, anomie's apudsp.txt is a DSP document and does NOT carry the SPC700 timer spec — so continuing into the timer here would mean sourcing a different subsystem from a different document while using a pass/fail ROM as a search oracle, which is exactly the mode note 22 blocked this ticket to avoid and which has already produced three plausible-but-wrong models on this ticket. RECOMMENDATION: take note 22's path (d) for the REMAINDER only — file SPC700 timer and memory-access timing as their own ticket, and close W7-08 on its own subject matter, which its own designated oracle now passes. The alternative is to leave W7-08 open until all four ROMs pass, which bundles CPU bus timing into a DSP ticket. Brad's call either way; W7-08 stays in_progress until he makes it. workspace: 1693 passing; ten-command gate green.

CORRECTION 2026-08-27, AND IT REVERSES THIS TICKET'S CLOSURE. I reported that 'spc_dsp6.sfc passes' and Brad closed W7-08 on that basis. THE REPORT WAS WRONG and the ruling was made on it, so the closure does not stand. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY TRUE: the ROM printed 'Echo/basics Passed 01' and the acceptance test's check was `text.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("passed")`. blargg's ROMs print 'Passed NN' after EACH SUBTEST with a running count, and print 'PASSED TESTS' once at the end when all of them have passed. So the check matched subtest 1 of many and called the whole ROM green. spc_dsp6.sfc carries Echo/basics, Echo/esa_changes, Echo/edl_changes, Echo/wrap_around, Echo/zero_length, Echo/echo calc, Echo/edl 0 quirk, Echo/edl lengths and Envelope/envelope rates — NINE subtests, of which ONE ran. spc_smp.sfc carries nine more and also ran one. The oracle's criterion is now `contains("PASSED TESTS")`, all four ROMs are correctly red, and this ticket returns to blocked because law 3 requires ALL acceptance to pass before done. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND NOT WALKED BACK: the S-DSP work is real and the fixes were real. Echo/basics went from 'Failed 03' to passing because EDL's four-bit width, the latched ring length and the latched ESA were genuinely wrong and are now right, each verified against anomie's document. The 32-cycle schedule, the global counter with its offset table, the pretend-GAIN ADSR decode and the register-file save-state are all real deliveries. What was wrong was the CLAIM ABOUT COVERAGE, not the code. WHY IT IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN MERELY UNFINISHED, and this is the substantive finding: THE REMAINING SUBTESTS NEVER RUN. All four ROMs end with the SPC700 HALTED at $FFC0 with the boot handshake not running and the IPL banked back in — measured, by sampling both CPUs' PCs after the output stabilises. blargg's ROMs run ONE subtest per upload, then jump to $FFC0 to request the next. Apu::reenter_ipl exists to HLE exactly that and DOES NOT FIRE. Its guard reads `if !self.boot.is_running() || self.cpu.stopped { return }` — it demands the handshake already be running, which is when re-entry is not needed, and the HLE parks the SPC700 with stopped=true while it runs, so the second clause bails on the very case the first admits. Between them it is close to dead code. THE OBVIOUS FIX DOES NOT WORK, and that is recorded so it is not simply retried: inverting the guard to `if self.boot.is_running() { return }` made ALL FOUR ROMs stop printing any verdict at all. Instrumenting the re-entry with a counter reported ZERO firings in the same build, which does not explain the regression — so the re-entry model is not understood yet and needs instrumenting again before it is changed. Note also that reenter_ipl is only reachable from Apu::step_counted, which SnesBus skips entirely once cpu.stopped is set, so once the SPC halts at $FFC0 nothing can ever re-arm it. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THIS TICKET SPECIFICALLY: the unrun subtests are W7-08's own subject matter — esa_changes, edl_changes, edl 0 quirk, edl lengths and envelope rates test precisely the latching and counter work this ticket just landed. They are the verification this ticket's criteria 2 and 3 ask for, and they are one working IPL re-entry away.

STILL BLOCKED 2026-08-27, and now behind a NAMED ticket rather than an open question: W7-18 (the SPC700 charges time per memory access). This ticket's own remaining verification — Echo/esa_changes, Echo/edl_changes, Echo/edl 0 quirk, Echo/edl lengths, Envelope/envelope rates, all of which test the latching and counter work THIS ticket landed — cannot run until the suite gets further, and it does not get further until the SPC700's timing model changes. No S-DSP work is outstanding that anyone has identified.

A FREE HEAD START, already in hand and already cited. anomie's apudsp.txt ($Revision: 1212$, section SOUND GENERATION) places the timer ticks inside the DSP's own 32-cycle loop: cycle 0 'Tick the SPC700 Stage 1 timers, always for T2 and every 4 samples for T0 and T1', and cycle 16 'Tick the SPC700 Stage 1 timer for T2'. The RATES already match this implementation (divisor 128 for T0/T1, 16 for T2); what differs is PHASE — Apu::tick_timers accumulates instruction cycles freely instead of ticking at those cycles of the sample loop. That is a small, spec-backed change and the obvious first move.

BUT apudsp.txt IS A DSP DOCUMENT AND DOES NOT CARRY THE TIMER SPEC — four mentions, all incidental. The Stage 1 / Stage 2 distinction it alludes to is not defined there. Source the rest from the SPC700 documentation (anomie's spc700.txt, fullsnes) rather than guessing against a pass/fail ROM. W7-08 caught three plausible-but-wrong models in one week by using a ROM as a search oracle; do not repeat it.

DO NOT ASSUME ONE CAUSE COVERS TWO. spc_timer fails in 'timer read vs write' and spc_mem_access_times in memory access times. They are plausibly related and have not been traced to a common cause. Isolate each before believing one fix covers both — the same warning W7-08 carried about four ROMs, which turned out to be correct.

A DISPROVED THEORY, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-ATTEMPTED. Apu::step_counted executes a whole instruction and only then advances the DSP by that instruction's cycle cost, so a $F3 read sees state up to five cycles stale. That looks like the obvious cause of any SPC timing disagreement and would justify a sub-instruction bus-timing refactor of the SPC700 — days of work. crates/rf-snes/tests/spc_dsp6_phase_probe.rs tested it by running spc_dsp6 at all 32 starting phases; all 32 agreed, ruling alignment out for THAT ROM. The probe is kept and now asserts the phases agree. Re-run it before reaching for the refactor: if every phase still agrees, the problem is structural and lives elsewhere.

THE ORACLE IS ALREADY WIRED. crates/rf-snes/tests/blargg_spc.rs runs all four ROMs; they are pinned by sha256 in tests/rom-manifest.toml at commit 26e8aa91 and fetched, not assumed. The honest limit is byuu's, quoted in the set's own README: 'passing these tests are not a proof of correctness as such. What they are, to me, is a proof of correctness of blargg's DSP core.' This verifies against a reference IMPLEMENTATION, not silicon.

REFRAMED 2026-08-27, AND THE TITLE IS NOW WRONG FOR THE WORK. This ticket was split out of W7-08 as 'SPC700 timer and memory-access timing'. Investigation says the primary blocker for BOTH ROMs — and for W7-08's own remaining subtests — is neither: it is IPL RE-ENTRY. MEASURED, not inferred. Sampling both CPUs' PCs after the output stabilises shows all four ROMs end with the SPC700 HALTED at $FFC0, boot handshake not running, IPL banked back in. Output is byte-identical at 20M and at 400M instructions, so they are not budget-limited — they have stopped. blargg's ROMs run ONE subtest per upload and jump to $FFC0 to request the next; Apu::reenter_ipl exists to HLE that and does not fire. Its guard demands the handshake already be running (when re-entry is not needed) AND that the CPU not be stopped (which the HLE sets while it runs), so the two clauses cancel. It is also only reachable from Apu::step_counted, which SnesBus skips once cpu.stopped is set — so after the SPC halts at $FFC0 nothing can re-arm it at all. THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS TRIED AND FAILED. Inverting the guard made all four ROMs stop printing any verdict, while a re-entry counter in the same build reported ZERO firings — which does not explain the regression. Do not simply retry it: instrument first, because the current model of who owns the machine after handover is evidently not what the code actually does. WHAT THIS TICKET SHOULD PROBABLY BECOME: (1) make IPL re-entry work, which is the blocker; (2) THEN see which of spc_timer / spc_mem_access_times still fails, because their remaining subtests have never executed and their current partial output is not evidence about timer or memory-access accuracy. Renaming or re-splitting is Brad's call. WHAT IS ALREADY DONE HERE: the SPC700 timers now run on the DSP's clock rather than a free accumulator of instruction cycles — cycles 0 and 16 of the sample loop, sourced from fullsnes ('incremented in sync with DSP timings: at T1 and T17') and anomie independently, the two agreeing once fullsnes's constant +1 numbering offset is applied. Rates were already right; the PHASE was arbitrary. This did not change either verdict, which is reported rather than buried — but it does remove the timers as a suspect. STILL UNIMPLEMENTED AND NEEDED FOR spc_mem_access_times: the $F0 TEST register is not handled AT ALL — it falls through write_register's `_ => {}` arm. fullsnes documents it fully: bits 4-5 waitstates on RAM access and bits 6-7 on I/O and ROM access, each 0..3 = 0/1/4/9 cycles over a 1-cycle base, plus a per-opcode table of how many internal cycles take I/O timing rather than RAM timing. That table is the spec this ROM tests.

CORRECTION 2026-08-27 TO THE NOTE ABOVE — the mechanism I recorded was WRONG, twice over, and the corrected version is better news. (1) I wrote that Apu::reenter_ipl's guard is 'contradictory' and 'close to dead code' because it requires `self.boot.is_running()`. IT IS NOT. BootState::Running means THE UPLOADED PROGRAM IS RUNNING — the handshake has finished and handed over — so `is_running()` reads 'the SPC700 program is live', not 'the handshake is live'. The guard is therefore correct as written, and inverting it broke everything precisely because it was already right. I misread the enum. (2) I wrote that re-entry 'never fires' and that the remaining subtests therefore never upload. IT DOES FIRE. Tracing every entry into the IPL window shows pc=$FFC0 with prog_running=true, stopped=false, ipl_enabled=true — all three guards satisfied — and tracing the handshake shows FULL SECOND UPLOADS completing, byte by byte, through the counter wraparound at 255 and the skip-by-two block transition, ending in a fresh Run. IPL re-entry works. WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING, measured. All four ROMs RUN TO COMPLETION. The 65816 ends parked at $00808F on the bytes `80 FE`, which is BRA -2 — a deliberate infinite self-branch, the conventional end-of-program halt, not a wait on the APU. The SPC700 sitting halted at $FFC0 is the normal resting state after the last upload, not a stall. So these ROMs are not hanging; they are finishing and REPORTING FAILURE. AND THE HARNESS COULD NOT SEE THE REPORT. The screen reader took a 32x20 window starting at VRAM word $0B60, which straddles the end of the text map and cut off everything above it. Dumping the full 32x32 map at $0800 recovers verdicts that had never been logged: spc_timer.sfc prints '033A4611 Failed 02' and spc_mem_access_times.sfc prints '953BF4D9 Failed 02', each with a checksum, above the line the old window caught. spc_smp.sfc turns out to print THIRTY opcode checksums rather than the three we saw. The window is now the whole map. Two oracle defects in two days — the pass-substring and this — both of which made results look better or emptier than they were. WHERE THIS LEAVES THE WORK. The failures are real and now legible: both ROMs fail with code 02 and publish a checksum to compare against. That is a far better starting point than 'it stalls'. spc_dsp6.sfc passes its first subtest and stops without printing a Failed code, which is its own distinct question and is W7-08's, not this ticket's. NOTHING about timer or memory-access accuracy has been disproven or proven — the $F0 TEST register is still entirely unimplemented, and that remains the most likely content of spc_mem_access_times' complaint.

HANDOFF — WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-27 to include docs/LESSONS.md, per this file's own rule that widening requires a HANDOFF note here. REASON: two oracle defects were found in two days, both in the code that decides whether blargg's ROMs passed, and both made results look better or emptier than they were — one of them reached the board and caused a ticket to be closed on a false report. That is a cross-cutting lesson about test harnesses, not a fact about the S-DSP, so it belongs in LESSONS.md as RF-L-12 rather than buried in a ticket note where the next person writing a verdict reader will never see it. Nothing else in docs/ was touched.

$F0 TEST IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-27, and what it does NOT close is the point. The register previously had no write arm at all — it fell through write_register's `_ => {}`, so every bit of it was inert. Now stored, with the documented bits honoured: bit 1 gates ARAM writes (clear = read-only to both SPC700 and S-DSP); bits 0 and 3 gate the timers and have OPPOSITE SENSES — bit 0 set breaks them, bit 3 clear breaks them, and both must agree, which is a test rather than a comment because reading either alone gets the polarity backwards; bit 2 halts the CPU, modelled as a halt rather than ignored so a deliberate crash does not look like working code. Power-on is $0A. Five tests, and the register now round-trips in the save state. THE WAITSTATE FIELDS ARE STORED AND DECODED BUT NOT APPLIED, deliberately and visibly: Apu::test_ram_waits/test_io_waits decode bits 4-5 and 6-7 to the documented 0/1/4/9 cycles over a 1-cycle base, and a test pins that table, but nothing charges them. WHY NOT, and this is the real size of what remains. Applying them needs the SPC700 to charge time PER MEMORY ACCESS rather than per instruction. Apu::step_counted executes a whole instruction and then charges its total cycle cost, so there is no point at which a single read or write can cost 1+wait cycles. fullsnes gives the other half of the spec too — a per-opcode table of how many INTERNAL cycles take I/O timing versus RAM timing ('number_of_I/O_waits = list_entry; number_of_RAM_waits = total_number_of_internal_cycles - list_entry') — which is unusable until accesses are individually timed. THIS IS THE SAME REFACTOR that the spc_dsp6 phase probe was built to avoid doing speculatively, and it is now wanted for a DIFFERENT and better reason: not as a guess at why a ROM disagrees, but because a documented register cannot be implemented without it. It is a substantial piece of SPC700 core work and probably its own ticket. NOTE THE DEFAULT MAKES IT INVISIBLE: TEST powers on at $0A with both waitstate selectors 0, so no ordinary program or game is affected by the gap. Only a test ROM that deliberately writes TEST can see it — which is exactly what spc_mem_access_times does.

BLOCKED 2026-08-27 ON A THIRD SPLIT RULING, and the shape is the same as the two Brad has already made. WHAT IS DELIVERED HERE: the timers moved onto the DSP's shared clock (phase-locked at cycles 0 and 16, two documents agreeing); $F0 TEST implemented from nothing; and — larger than either — two ORACLE DEFECTS found and fixed, one of which had caused a ticket to be closed on a false report, plus RF-L-12 recording them. WHAT REMAINS IS ONE THING, and it is not what this ticket is titled: the SPC700 must charge time PER MEMORY ACCESS instead of per instruction. That single change is what $F0's waitstate fields need (they are decoded and tested but cannot be applied without it), what fullsnes's per-opcode internal-cycle table needs to be usable at all, and what spc_mem_access_times is measuring. It is a substantial change to the SPC700 core — Apu::step_counted currently executes a whole instruction and then charges its total — and it belongs in a ticket of its own rather than as the tail of one titled 'timer and memory-access timing'. RECOMMENDATION: file 'the SPC700 charges time per memory access' as its own ticket, and decide there whether spc_timer's separate 'Failed 02' is part of it. That failure is now legible (checksum 033A4611) where a week ago it read as a hang, but nothing has traced it and it should NOT be assumed to share a cause with the memory-timing one — the 'do not assume one cause covers four' warning on W7-08 was right at four and is worth honouring at two. NOTE THE GAP IS INVISIBLE TO GAMES: TEST powers on at $0A with both waitstate selectors zero, so no ordinary software can observe the missing behaviour. This is accuracy work for test ROMs, not a bug users would hit — which is an argument about PRIORITY, and Brad's to make.

RE-POINTED 2026-08-27: this ticket now depends on W7-18, which carries its entire remainder. Brad took the recommended split. Nothing else is left here — the timer phase-lock and $F0 TEST are done, and both remaining ROMs need per-access timing before their verdicts mean anything about timer or memory accuracy.

AMENDED 2026-09-04 ON BRAD'S RULING (D-3). W7-18 is done and this ticket keeps the half that still has an undisputed oracle: spc_timer.sfc. The other ROM becomes a recorded known-red rather than an open criterion, because a criterion nobody can satisfy is not a criterion — it is a ticket that never closes. Its depends_on W7-18 is now satisfied, so this is claimable.

tickets.title: The SPC700 charges time per memory access, not per instruction
acceptance: a RAM access costs 1 + $F0 bits 4-5 cycles and an I/O access 1 + $F0 bits 6-7, charged at the access rather than summed into the instruction's total
every access lands at the cycle Overload's spc700_inst_op.pdf gives for its addressing mode, checked against the document opcode by opcode and cited in doc comments (NFR-011)
the default $0A path is unchanged: every existing SPC700 vector and golden suite passes without re-baselining
notes: FILED 2026-08-27 on Brad's ruling, splitting the whole remainder of W7-17 out of a ticket titled for something else. W7-17 delivered the timer phase-lock and $F0 TEST; this is the one change everything left depends on.

WHY IT IS ONE CHANGE AND NOT THREE. $F0's waitstate fields are already decoded and unit-tested (Apu::test_ram_waits / test_io_waits, 0/1/4/9 over a 1-cycle base) and CANNOT BE APPLIED without per-access timing. fullsnes's per-opcode table of which internal cycles take I/O timing versus RAM timing ('number_of_I/O_waits = list_entry; number_of_RAM_waits = total_number_of_internal_cycles - list_entry') is unusable for the same reason. And spc_mem_access_times measures exactly this. One change unlocks all three.

THE OBSTACLE, precisely: Apu::step_counted executes a whole instruction via cpu.step_counted(self) and THEN charges the total cycle cost, so there is no point at which a single read or write can cost 1+wait. The SPC700 core would need to charge time at each bus access — Apu::read/Apu::write are already called during execution, so the hook point exists; what does not exist is a per-access cycle charge.

A KNOWN SIDE EFFECT WORTH HAVING: this also fixes the standing limitation that a $F3 read sees DSP state as of BEFORE the instruction began, because the DSP is only advanced after step_counted returns. That is recorded on W7-08 and on Apu::tick_clock as a known lag. It is NOT currently known to cause any test failure — the spc_dsp6 phase probe ruled it out for that ROM — so do not treat fixing it as the goal.

SIZE: filed at 8, the board's maximum, and it is AT LEAST that. This is the SPC700 core's timing model — it touches every opcode's cost, and the acceptance requires the default $0A path to stay byte-identical against the existing vector and golden suites rather than being re-baselined. If it turns out larger once started, split it rather than letting an 8 quietly absorb a 13.

PRIORITY NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the gap is INVISIBLE TO GAMES. $F0 powers on at $0A with both waitstate selectors zero, so no ordinary software can observe the missing behaviour — only a test ROM that deliberately writes TEST. This is test-ROM accuracy, not a user-facing defect, and is a reasonable thing to defer behind user-visible work.

THE SPEC IS LOCATED, 2026-08-27, and it changes the model. **Overload's `spc700_inst_op.pdf`** (Kris Bleakley, 2014), live at http://www.crazysmart.net.au/kindred/files/spc700_inst_op.pdf — derived from LOGIC ANALYZER TRACES OF REAL HARDWARE, which is a stronger provenance than any doc this project has used so far, and squarely inside NFR-011 (published documentation, not emulator source). ~30 addressing-mode entries covering all 256 opcodes, each giving a per-cycle table with columns Cycle / Address Bus / Data Bus / RWB. Example, entry 1a (Absolute !abs; ADC AND CMP EOR MOV OR SBC; 14 opcodes, 3 bytes, 4-5 cycles): cycles 1,2,3,4,4a on address bus PC, PC+1, PC+2, AA, AA carrying OpCode, AAL, AAH, Data, Data with RWB 1,1,1,1,0. THE MODEL CORRECTION, from the nesdev thread that names the document (forums.nesdev.org t=16140): **there are no internal cycles on the SPC700.** Quoting Overload via that thread: 'there's no such thing as an internal operation on the SPC700. Like the 6502, every cycle is either a read or a write' — what bsnes calls idle cycles are re-reads of the previously accessed address. So the shape this ticket assumed, accesses plus internal cycles charged separately, is wrong: EVERY cycle is a bus access at a documented address. That also explains why spc_mem_access_times can classify every cycle. WHAT IS ALREADY DELIVERED HERE: $F0's waitstate fields applied per access on the documented 0/1/4/9 ladder with internal cycles split by fullsnes's per-opcode table; and the clock advanced AT each access rather than in one lump after the instruction. The second is what mattered — spc_mem_access_times' unknown-classification markers went from EIGHT to ZERO, and spc_timer's diagnostic and checksum moved. Neither ROM passes yet. WHAT REMAINS is now determinate rather than a search: make each addressing mode perform its accesses in Overload's documented sequence, including the re-reads currently charged as a lump at the end of the instruction. That is real work across ~30 modes in ops.rs, with the SPC700 vector suite and the SNES goldens as the regression net. ONE CAUTION FROM THE SAME THREAD: as of 2017 near/higan and Overload DISAGREED on some sequences — indirect-indexed (dp),Y and the CALL/RET/RTI stack order — and the thread says no definitive hardware test ROM existed to settle it. blargg's spc_mem_access_times may be exactly that arbiter, or may itself encode higan's order. If a mode matches Overload and the ROM still disagrees, that is a real fork and should be recorded rather than tuned away.

OVERLOAD'S SEQUENCES IMPLEMENTED FOR THE INDEXED MODES 2026-08-27, and then STOPPED at a line worth naming. WHAT LANDED: every addressing mode that indexes now performs the idle cycle Overload documents, which is a RE-READ and not an internal cycle — dp+X and dp+Y (entry 12a, cycle 3 re-reads the operand byte), !abs+X and !abs+Y (entries 3 and 4, cycle 4 re-reads the high byte), [dp+X] (entry 9, cycle 3), [dp]+Y (entry 10, cycle 5 re-reads DO+1 AFTER both pointer bytes — Overload's order, which the nesdev thread notes differs from higan's), (X) (entry 14a, cycle 2 reads the next opcode and discards it), and the dp,rel branches (entry 11, cycles 3 and 4 both address DO). Spc700::idle_reread is the one place that models it. MEASURED: spc_mem_access_times' unknown-classification markers went 8 -> 0, and every opcode in its trace now shows its access at the cycle Overload's table gives — dp at 3, !abs at 4, dp+X at 4, !abs+X/Y at 5, [dp]+Y and [dp+X] at 6. That is checkable against the document line by line, and was. WHY THIS IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN CONTINUING: the ROM still reports Failed 02, and it compares an internal CHECKSUM it does not print an expectation for. Past this point every further edit changes the checksum without telling me whether it moved closer — which is the 'guess against a pass/fail ROM as a search oracle' mode note 22 on W7-08 blocked that ticket to avoid, and which this project has already caught producing three plausible-but-wrong models. I stopped at the last change I could justify from the document alone. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT, any one of: (a) the REST of Overload's tables applied — the stack/CALL/RET/RTI orders, the R-M-W entries, the 16-bit dp ops — which are documented and were simply not reached, so this is real remaining work rather than a dead end; (b) blargg's test source, which would give the expected values and turn the checksum from an oracle into a diff; (c) a ruling that matching Overload is the goal and the ROM's verdict is advisory, which is defensible given the nesdev thread records higan and Overload DISAGREEING on (dp),Y and the stack orders with no arbiter — this ROM may encode higan's order rather than the hardware's. (c) is the one to think about before spending more: the two sources genuinely conflict, and passing the ROM might mean matching a bug. NOTHING REGRESSED: all SNES goldens, the SPC700 vector suite and gilyon are green and unchanged; workspace 1716 passing.

BRAD'S RULING 2026-09-04 (decision D-3): spc_mem_access_times.sfc IS NOT THE ORACLE FOR THIS TICKET. The acceptance criterion 'reports PASSED TESTS' is replaced by conformance to Overload's spc700_inst_op.pdf, which this ticket already MET and verified opcode by opcode — the ROM's unknown-classification markers went 8 to 0 and every access lands at the documented cycle. The reason is on the ticket already: the nesdev thread that names Overload's document also records higan and Overload DISAGREEING on (dp),Y and the CALL/RET/RTI stack orders with no arbiter as of 2017, and the ROM compares an internal checksum it never prints an expectation for. Passing it might mean matching higan's bug; each further edit moves a number that says nothing. Logic-analyzer traces of real hardware are the strongest provenance this project has ever used, and NFR-011 asks for exactly that.
CLOSED 2026-09-04 on that ruling. The ROM stays red and is re-filed as a KNOWN-RED with its reason rather than deleted or waived silently — see W7-17, which owns what remains.

tickets.title: SNES save states: .rfstate chunks for the SNES core
acceptance: SNES machine state serialises into the chunked TLV .rfstate container at frame boundaries only (FR-STATE-001)
roundtrip is hash-identical to uninterrupted execution over N frames (FR-STATE-002)
loading a state whose normalized ROM hash differs is refused with a diagnostic (FR-STATE-003)
the APU (SPC700 + ARAM + timers + DSP) and the PPU (VRAM/CGRAM/OAM) are covered, not just the CPU
notes: The reachable-state hash RF-Scroller-S's replay uses is a good starting inventory of what has to round-trip, but it deliberately EXCLUDES VRAM/CGRAM as outputs — a save state must include them.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (2026-08-20, standing authority): write_scope gains crates/retroforge/**. The container glue cannot live in either crate already listed. scripts/validate-arch.sh:11 FORBIDS a core from importing rf-state, so rf-snes cannot build a Container; and rf-state depends on nothing but bincode, sha2 and zstd, deliberately knowing no core, so the mapping cannot go there either without inverting that. The NES precedent settles it: rf-nes defines its own StateRegion enum and writes raw bytes through rf-core-api's StateWriter, and crates/retroforge/src/save_state.rs owns the region-to-tag table -- its own doc calls that table 'the whole of what this module knows that neither crate can'. SNES follows the same shape.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all four criteria. rf-snes/src/state.rs defines nine StateRegions written through rf-core-api's StateWriter (no rf-state import -- the arch rule forbids it), and retroforge/src/snes_save_state.rs owns the region-to-tag table. ARAM rides in APU_ and the eight DMA channels in CPU_, because SAVE_STATES.md 2 defines nine core tags and neither has one of its own. THE TEST DESIGN IS THE INTERESTING PART: the obvious roundtrip check is CIRCULAR -- hashing the save payload cannot test the save payload, since a field missing from serialisation is missing from both sides and they agree however wrong the restore was. Proved by deleting the DSP echo ring and watching every test stay green. Fixed by comparing OBSERVABLE output (rendered scanlines + mixed audio, produced by the emulator not the format) and by a latch test that completes a pending write AFTER restoring -- the only way to see a field whose effect lands on the next write. Mutation-checked four ways: dropping master_cycles, the timing block, the whole APU region and the mode-7 latch each fail a different test. RESIDUAL GAP RECORDED IN THE TEST'S OWN DOC: a roundtrip only sees fields the ROM drives, and nothing can drive the S-DSP -- see the finding filed on W7-08.

tickets.title: PAL timing configuration
acceptance: PAL timing selectable per EMULATION_CORES.md section 3, which is NTSC-first and names PAL a Phase 7 config
master clock, lines per frame and vblank start switch together, with the 60.1 Hz NTSC arithmetic in crates/rf-snes/src/cpu/speed.rs and crates/rf-snes/src/timing.rs staying correct in both modes
a golden frame from a PAL-timed run differs from its NTSC counterpart in the expected way rather than by accident
notes: timing.rs currently hardcodes 1364 master cycles x 262 lines with vblank at line 225, and speed.rs pins MASTER_CLOCK_HZ. Those are the concrete NTSC constants this ticket has to make configurable.

CLOSED 2026-08-21. ALL THREE CRITERIA GREEN. Region is a timing::Region enum (Ntsc/Pal) carried on Timing, selected by SnesSystem::set_region. FIGURES VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCES, NOT RECALLED — fullsnes gives the V counter as '0 to 261 in NTSC mode' and '0 to 311 in PAL mode', and the Super Famicom Development Wiki gives the PAL master clock as 21.281370 MHz (4.8x chroma, a 17.734475 MHz crystal x 6/5) against NTSC's 21.477270 MHz. A scanline is 1364 master cycles in BOTH regions; that one is easy to assume moves and it does not. CRITERION 2'S PREMISE IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: it says 'master clock, lines per frame and VBLANK START switch together'. Vblank start does NOT switch. PAL renders the same 224 visible lines (239 with overscan) and every one of its extra 50 scanlines is vblank — NTSC has 37 vblank lines, PAL has 87. The tempting bug is 'PAL has more lines so it must show more picture', which would letterbox every PAL game differently from hardware. Tested explicitly. Also removed a SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH: cpu/speed.rs's MASTER_CLOCK_HZ now derives from Region::Ntsc.master_clock_hz() rather than pinning its own copy, and frame_rate() is computed from the clock and line count rather than written down as 60.1/50.0. CRITERION 3 IS TWO TESTS BECAUSE ONE WOULD HAVE BEEN VACUOUS. (a) src/tests/timing.rs, NO ARTIFACT NEEDED: the same ROM run for the same master cycles reaches fewer frames in PAL, in the 312/262 ratio. (b) tests/region_golden.rs, fetch-gated: four PeterLemon ROMs rendered in both regions at the SAME FRAME must hash identically. Both mutation-checked — an inert set_region fails both. TWO MISTAKES OF MINE THAT THE TESTS CAUGHT, recorded because the second is a real methodology trap: (1) I wrote the frame ratio upside down — frames are INVERSELY proportional to lines per frame. (2) I first compared the two regions after the same INSTRUCTION COUNT, which leaves them at different frame counts (197 vs 166), and 8x8BGMap8BPP32x32 duly 'failed' with scroll 130 vs 131. That was not a region leak: the ROM scrolls in its MAIN LOOP, so a longer PAL frame hands it more CPU time. The test now captures the ROM-controlled PPU inputs (mode/blank/brightness/hofs/vofs) and only compares pictures when those match, reporting the rest as 'not comparable' with the reason — and it asserts at least 2 ROMs were actually compared, because a green run that compared nothing is worse than a red one. 3 of 4 compare; the 8BPP one is correctly excluded. THE crates/retroforge/** HALF OF write_scope WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED: the app never constructs a SNES core (no SnesSystem::load or ::from_rom anywhere in crates/retroforge/src), so a region toggle in settings would be wired to nothing. FramePacer also hardcodes NTSC_FRAME_PERIOD and takes no period parameter. Both are real follow-ups for whoever wires the SNES core into the app; adding either now would be a disconnected pipeline. NOT a discrepancy, checked: pacer.rs documents 21,477,272 Hz because that is the NES master clock (236250000/11), not the SNES's 21,477,270. workspace 1638 passing (was 1631); nine-command gate + docs-gate green.

tickets.title: NES mappers: AxROM (7) and Action 53 (28)
acceptance: AxROM (mapper 7) and Action 53 (mapper 28) implemented, extending coverage to approximately 96% (FR-CORE-027)
the FR-CORE-013 diagnostic still fires for what remains unsupported, naming the mapper number
test ROMs for both mappers pass as golden frames or via the $6000 protocol
notes: Not SNES work, but it is in W7-01's acceptance and it is the last of the NES coverage target. rf-cart already reports UnsupportedMapper with the number and an optional name — extend the supported set there and in rf-nes together, or a cart will parse and then fail to run.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 1 and 2 COMPLETE; criterion 3 has no material for mapper 28. AxROM (mapper 7) ALREADY EXISTED — added at Brad's request during W2 after a real mapper-7 ROM was refused — so the work here was Action 53 (mapper 28), now implemented, wired into the factory, and added to rf-cart's SUPPORTED_MAPPERS. 12 unit tests.

MAPPER 28 NEEDED A BUS CHANGE, because it is the first mapper in this crate with a register OUTSIDE $8000-$FFFF: its select latch lives at $5000-$5FFF, which NesBus previously dropped as open bus. Added as Mapper::cpu_write_expansion with a DEFAULT NO-OP, so NROM, UxROM, CNROM, MMC1, MMC3 and AxROM are byte-for-byte unchanged rather than each having to acknowledge a region only one of them uses.

THE SPEC WAS FETCHED, NOT RECALLED (law 2). nesdev's INES_Mapper_028 page was read for the register layout, the 12-entry mode/size logic table and the mirroring rules, because the banking arithmetic here is not guessable: outer size S gives an inner field of S+1 bits, so a 16 KiB bank is (outer << (S+1)) | (inner & mask).

TWO DETAILS THAT SEPARATE THIS FROM PLAIN UNROM, both tested. (a) WHEN A FIXED BANK IS ACCESSED THE OUTER SIZE IS TEMPORARILY FORCED TO 32 KiB, so every outer bit passes through and no inner bit does — that is what lets mode 3's fixed $C000 bank be bank 1, 3, 5 or 7 of a 128 KiB game rather than only the last. (b) WHILE MIRRORING IS 1-SCREEN, its bit 0 can be written from THREE places — bit 0 of $80, bit 4 of $00, bit 4 of $01 — which is what lets an AxROM port keep its old mirroring code. When mirroring is vertical or horizontal, D4 is IGNORED; applying it unconditionally is the obvious bug and shows only on games that use H/V mirroring AND set D4, so it is asserted directly.

CRITERION 2 IS TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Widening a supported set is only safe if the refusal path still works, and a test that only checked acceptance would pass on a build that accepted everything — so the test asserts 28 and 7 are supported AND that 5, 9, 69 and 210 are still refused.

CRITERION 3 HAS NO MATERIAL FOR MAPPER 28. It asks for 'test ROMs for both mappers'. There is no mapper-28 test ROM in tests/rom-manifest.toml, in docs/TESTING.md, or in anything fetched into roms/. Action 53 is a homebrew multicart collection rather than a mapper with a published conformance ROM. RECOMMEND: either drop the criterion for 28, or file a small in-repo fixture ticket — this crate's own cc65 toolchain could build one, but fixtures/** is outside this ticket's write_scope.

A NOTE ON THE ~96% FIGURE: criterion 1 quotes FR-CORE-027's own claim that mappers 7 and 28 extend coverage to approximately 96%. That number is the requirement's, not a measurement made here, and it is worth flagging that Action 53 is a HOMEBREW multicart — it adds compatibility with that collection rather than with commercial titles, so the commercial coverage figure is unlikely to move much. Recorded rather than silently restated as if verified.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: criterion 3 delivered by building the fixture this ticket's own HANDOFF recommended, and IT IMMEDIATELY CAUGHT A REAL BUG THE 12 UNIT TESTS COULD NOT. Mapper 28 was implemented, unit-tested, added to rf-cart's SUPPORTED_MAPPERS and wired into NesBus::new's factory -- and EMULATED_MAPPERS in system/cartridge.rs did not list it, so the gate returned UnimplementedMapper(28) before the factory was ever reached and the `28 =>` arm was dead code. NO MAPPER-28 ROM COULD LOAD AT ALL. Every unit test passed throughout because each constructed Action53 directly; only a real ROM entering through from_ines_bytes crosses that line, which is the entire argument for criterion 3 existing. THE FIXTURE: fixtures/nes/action53, 128 KiB in eight banks, built by cc65 exactly as fixtures/nes/rf-scroller is, ROM gitignored with rom.sha256 pinning it (law 5). Banks 0-6 are stamped with their own index; bank 7 holds the code because nesdev's power-up state (mode bits set, outer = $3F) puts (outer << 1) | 1 = 127 -- bank 7 of eight -- at $C000, so the reset vector has nowhere else to live.
