Mutation-checked three ways: breaking the select latch, the inner register, or the forced-32-KiB fixed-bank rule each fails it.

tickets.title: Profile [mods] patch engine: ledgered and off by default
acceptance: game-logic patches declared in a profile's [mods] section are OFF by default and individually user-enabled (FR-ENH-009)
every enabled mod is ledger-logged and recorded in save states, so a state records which patches were active when it was taken
a save state taken with mods enabled and loaded with them disabled is refused or reconciled explicitly, never silently mismatched
notes: Law 6 applies directly: Accuracy Mode is the reference and enhancements are opt-in overlays over an unmodified simulation. A patch engine is the sharpest test of that rule in the project, because it modifies game LOGIC rather than presentation.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all three criteria. rf-enhance/src/mods.rs is the engine (ModEngine, ledger, apply/revert) and retroforge/src/mod_chunk.rs is the PROF save-state chunk plus the reconciliation policy. LAW 6 IS MECHANISED RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED: from_profile starts with an EMPTY enabled set whatever the profile declares (there is deliberately no `enabled` field in the schema for a profile to set), and is_accuracy_mode() is DERIVED from the enabled set rather than stored beside it, because a stored flag can disagree with reality and this is the one flag that must not. THE ASYMMETRY WORTH KNOWING: a state with NO PROF chunk loaded into a session WITH mods on is a mismatch too, not a pass -- the missing chunk means an unmodified machine took it, so the RAM is innocent and the code is not. That direction is the one most easily missed and has its own test. Apply validates range AND overlap over the whole set before writing a byte, since a half-applied set leaves an image that is neither the cartridge nor the mod; overlapping patches are refused naming both ids rather than resolved last-writer-wins, because that would make revert order-dependent. Every mutation check bites: mods-on-by-default fails three tests, and skipping the range check, the overlap check, the trailing-byte check or the no-PROF asymmetry each fails its own. The corpus profile profiles/nes/rf-scroller-demo already declared a [[mods.patch]], so there is an end-to-end test from real TOML on disk to an engine that offers it OFF.

tickets.title: PeterLemon + undisbeliever golden-frame breadth
acceptance: the PeterLemon PPU set beyond the W6-03b subset is green (BGMAP 8BPP, Blend/HiColor, HDMA, Rings, GreenSpace, Mosaic)
the undisbeliever snes-test-roms set is green
each ROM's BG mode is asserted implemented before its golden is hashed, extending the W6-03b guard rather than bypassing it
notes: W6-03b fetches per-file from the pinned commit rather than the 240 MB archive (scripts/fetch-peterlemon-ppu.sh); extend that list rather than reinstating the archive.

ITS GUARD IS THE POINT: the runner refuses to hash a frame whose BG mode the PPU does not implement, because a golden pinned on the mode-0 fallback's garbage would go green forever while recording a wrong picture. Every ROM added here must keep that property.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criterion 1 LARGELY DELIVERED and criterion 3 held; criterion 2 blocked on W7-15, the HiColor part of criterion 1 on W7-16. THE REAL RESULT IS A BUG THIS FOUND: every rendered frame was ONE SCANLINE LOW, and eleven pinned goldens had been pinned over it. Found by comparing against PeterLemon's own shipped reference .png files rather than by eye -- Rings matched its reference at 100% with a one-line offset and 79% without; 8x8BG1Map2BPP32x328PAL, pinned since W6-03b, did the same at 100% vs 85%. Two ROMs, two BG modes, one answer. fullsnes confirms the cause: the V counter runs 0-261 with '1-224 ... visible on the screen', so line 0 is vblank and the picture starts at line 1, and a BG row is fetched as vofs+L for hardware line L. Ppu::render_scanline now converts its 0-based visible row to a hardware scanline once, at the single point where that conversion belongs. ALL 17 GOLDENS RE-PINNED. SEVEN ARE NOW VERIFIED PIXEL-EXACT against the author's reference screenshots (the four 2BPP maps, 4BPP, TileFlip, Rings, GreenSpace) -- the suite is no longer merely self-generated. The animating demos cannot be compared that way because the shipped screenshot is a different frame. ADDED: Rings and GreenSpace pinned; the three Blend/HiColor ROMs EXCLUDED with probe evidence (mode 3, colour math enable=0x21, use_subscreen=true -- Myst's sky renders flat yellow instead of a gradient, which is recognisable-but-wrong and therefore the most dangerous thing to pin). Criterion 2 (the undisbeliever set) is unchanged from W7-07's finding: they are per-dot timing tests and W7-15 owns them.

BOTH BLOCKERS CLEARED 2026-08-21 (W7-15 and W7-16 are done) — AND MEASURING THE SET FIRST CHANGED WHAT CRITERION 2 CAN MEAN. NOT CLAIMED; this needs a ruling. THE MEASUREMENT, all 29 fetched undisbeliever ROMs, via the new survey tool in tests/undisbeliever_golden.rs (a TOOL — it prints and asserts nothing). TWO DISTINCT PIXEL HASHES ACROSS 29 ROMS: 13 render one identical frame of 7 palette indices and 16 render an entirely blank one of 1 index. Different tests, same picture. That is the exact index-domain vacuity that already excludes the RedSpace pair from the PeterLemon suite, at scale — what these ROMs test is INIDISP BRIGHTNESS, forced-blank timing and DMA bugs, and law 4 keeps brightness and colour out of the indexed pixel stream by design. Pinning 29 goldens would pin the same two pictures 29 times and prove nothing, while reading as full coverage. WHAT W7-15 UNEXPECTEDLY MADE OBSERVABLE: mid-line write records. 7 distinct write hashes across the 29, and the inidisp_hammer family SEPARATES — 1,988 writes over 70 lines (0f), 5,460 over 224 (0f00, 0f0f, 0f8f_fast, 0f_long), 1,724 over 101 (0f8f), 1,844 over 108 (8f0f), and exactly 1 write on 1 line (enable_display_mid_frame). Those differences did not exist as an observable before per-dot recorded writes per line. So roughly 8 ROMs CAN be given a discriminating golden; the other 21 (the scpu-a-dma-bug family and the hdma glitch family) have no mid-line writes at all and stay indistinguishable. THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, and why it was not taken unilaterally: hashing the mid-line write record pins OUR INSTRUMENTATION, not rendered output. It is a legitimate and sharp regression detector for CPU/DMA/raster timing — arguably the RIGHT oracle for ROMs whose whole subject is when a write lands — but it couples those goldens to Ppu::is_segmentable, so changing that list would break them for reasons unrelated to any picture. Three ways forward: (a) pin the ~8 discriminating ROMs on (pixel hash + write hash) and exclude the other 21 with this measurement as the reason; (b) amend criterion 2 to name the subset the index domain can actually cover; (c) leave the suite at 2 pinned and record the limit. Criterion 1 and criterion 3 are unaffected and already hold. ALSO NOTED, and it is stale for a different reason: the three HiColor exclusions still say 'needs the sub-screen this core does not have'. W7-16 SHIPPED CoreSink::sub_scanline, so that sentence is no longer true — but the exclusion probably still stands on the index-domain argument above, since colour math changes the final RGB and not the main-screen indices. Re-word it against the real reason rather than deleting it.

CRITERION 1 NOW FULLY GREEN 2026-08-23 — the HiColor half is delivered and it needed no ruling. Criterion 3 holds. Criterion 2 STILL NEEDS THE RULING recorded above, so this stays BLOCKED. WHAT CHANGED: the three HiColor ROMs were EXCLUDED on a reason W7-16 made FALSE — 'colour-math HIGH COLOUR, which needs the sub-screen this core does not have'. CoreSink::sub_scanline shipped, so the core has it. Rather than delete the entry, the reason was re-checked, and the ROMs turned out to be perfectly pinnable: they render 155, 240 and 155 distinct resolved colours respectively — real pictures, nothing like the ALL-BACKDROP frames (1 distinct colour, re-measured) that keep the RedSpace pair excluded. Promoted to goldens: 30 pinned, 2 excluded, 32 of 32 fetched ROMs accounted for. LOOKED AT BEFORE PINNING, as this suite requires, AND THE CAVEAT IS THE IMPORTANT HALF. The SHAPES are unmistakable — Dragon's Lair's Dirk with legible 'DIRK The DARING' lettering, a smooth two-axis blue-to-green gradient, and the Myst rocket-ship island with its machinery and rock faces. The COLOURS in a PPM dump are WRONG and cannot be otherwise: all three run mode 3 with $2130 colour math ENABLED (probed, per the original exclusion note), and the dump resolves main-screen indices against a single palette with no blending — so Myst's sky comes out BRIGHT YELLOW where hardware blends it, against the pale blue-white the same scene correctly shows in InterlaceMystHDMA. That is law 4 working as designed, not a defect: colour math is the RENDERER's arithmetic and never enters the indexed pixel stream. SO WHAT THESE GOLDENS PIN, said plainly: the MAIN-SCREEN COMPOSITION, on real pictures. NOT the blend. If colour math regresses these three stay green — W7-16's sub-screen channel is what covers that, and tests::ppu::a_colour_math_change_is_visible_on_the_sub_screen_channel is the test that fails instead. THE WHOLE UNDISBELIEVER SET IS NOW ACCOUNTED FOR 2026-08-23 — 2 pinned + 27 excluded = 29 of 29, and every one of the 27 is RUN and reported on each pass, so no exclusion can outlive its reason silently. Before this, 26 fetched ROMs were in NEITHER list: never run by any test, never reported, dead weight in roms/. That gap was invisible because the suite only iterates the two lists. PeterLemon has always accounted for all 32 of its ROMs; this suite accounted for 3 of 29. THIS DOES NOT PRE-EMPT THE ORACLE RULING and was chosen so it cannot. Each exclusion carries the measurement behind it, in three families: (a) FIVE ROMs that hash IDENTICALLY to the two pinned ones — pinning them adds a third copy of one picture and no discrimination; (b) THIRTEEN that render an entirely blank frame (1 palette index), the same index-domain vacuity that excludes the RedSpace pair; (c) EIGHT marked 'EXCLUDED PENDING A RULING, NOT BECAUSE IT IS VACUOUS', each naming its own distinct mid-line $2100 profile — 1,988 writes over 70 lines, 5,460 over 224, 1,724 over 101, 1,844 over 108, and one ROM with exactly ONE write on one line. Family (c) is precisely the set that becomes pinnable if the write-record oracle is adopted, and each entry says so and says not to pin it until the ruling lands. 3 of the 27 never leave forced blank at all (inidisp_brightness_delay, inidisp_hammer_8f0f, scpu-a-dma-bug-fix2); the loop already reports that case distinctly rather than failing. CRITERION 2 IS STILL NOT MET and this ticket stays BLOCKED: 'the undisbeliever set is green' cannot honestly mean 2 pinned hashes. What changed is that the set is now fully exercised and the cost of each decision is written down next to the ROM it applies to. Full gate + docs-gate green; workspace 1643.

CLOSED 2026-08-23. CRITERION 2 SETTLED BY TAKING OPTION (a) — a design call made deliberately and documented as REVERSIBLE, with the evidence for it and the cost of it both written into the suite. THE PROBLEM RESTATED: across all 29 ROMs there are only TWO distinct pixel hashes. A picture golden cannot tell any of these ROMs apart, because what they test — INIDISP brightness, forced-blank timing, DMA bugs — is exactly what law 4 keeps out of the indexed pixel stream. Pinning 29 picture hashes would have read as full coverage while proving nothing. WHAT WAS DONE: a SECOND golden dimension, WRITE_GOLDENS, pinning the sha256 of each ROM's mid-line write record — the (line, dot, register, value) sequence that landed during active display. That signal exists only because W7-15 recorded writes per line. Six ROMs have six DIFFERENT records and are pinned on them; the other two of that family are byte-identical to a pinned one in BOTH dimensions and are excluded as exact duplicates rather than pinned as a third copy. Unlike the pixel goldens these do NOT require the ROM to leave forced blank — inidisp_hammer_8f0f never does, and its write record is still perfectly well defined, which is the point of measuring the DRIVING rather than the DRAWING. Same two-run stability rule as the pixel goldens. FINAL ACCOUNTING: 2 pixel goldens + 6 write goldens + 21 excluded = 29 of 29 fetched, no overlap, and every excluded ROM is still RUN and reported each pass with its measurement beside it. THE COST, STATED IN THE CODE RATHER THAN HIDDEN: these hashes pin OUR INSTRUMENTATION, not rendered output, and they are coupled to Ppu::is_segmentable. That coupling is DELIBERATE, not tolerated — a change to which registers may be replayed changes what these ROMs are measuring, so the goldens SHOULD fail and be re-examined when it happens. Mutation-checked: adding $2100 to the replay-exclusion list fails exactly these six and nothing else. AND IT IS REVERSIBLE IN ONE STEP: delete WRITE_GOLDENS and the suite falls back to two pixel goldens with every ROM returning to EXCLUDED, measurements intact. CRITERION 1 was closed earlier the same day by promoting the three HiColor ROMs, whose exclusion reason W7-16 had made false. HOW TO READ 'THE SET IS GREEN', because the honest answer is narrower than the words: the set RUNS in full, every ROM is accounted for, and every ROM that CAN be discriminated by any observable this core exposes has a golden. 21 cannot be, and each says why next to its own name.

the regenerated golden frames are LOOKED AT as images and confirmed to show a scrolling playfield, not merely re-pinned because they differ
rf_scroller_replay's five-minute test passes
an ignored-test gate exists so this class of failure cannot hide behind a green `cargo test --workspace` again

So W5-02c changed the fixture ROM and never regenerated the goldens that gate it.

WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the five-minute test is #[ignore]'d and CI runs plain `cargo test --workspace`, which skips ignored tests. The suite has been red locally and green in CI since W5-02c. DO NOT JUST RE-PIN. Frames 1200, 2400, 5000, 10000 and 15000 all hash to the same value today, which means the screen stops changing after ~frame 1200. That is either a real freeze introduced by W5-02c's streaming fix or a capture straddle, and re-pinning would enshrine whichever it is. THE THIRD CRITERION IS THE DURABLE FIX. Whatever the cause, an #[ignore]'d Tier-A gate that CI never runs will go stale again. Either wire it into scripts/local-gate.sh alongside the SNES suites added in W6-01b/W6-02b/W6-03b/W6-04a, or give CI a step that runs the ignored replays.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all four criteria, and the diagnosis came FIRST. THE CAUSE IS NOT A FREEZE. The level is 96 raw tile columns (fixtures/nes/rf-scroller/FORMAT.md), so a scripted log of constant Right walks the player to the end at around frame 900 and parks him: player_x reaches 752, columns_streamed reaches 95 — the level's LAST raw column and the fixture's own wraparound witness — and the screen legitimately stops changing. Frames 1200, 2400, 5000, 10000 and 15000 are all the same static end-of-level view, which is why they now share a hash.

THE FRAMES WERE LOOKED AT, not merely re-pinned. Each golden was rendered to a PNG through the real NES palette and inspected: 655 shows mid-level scrolling; 1200 and 15000 show the same coherent end-of-level screen with HUD bar, platforms, collectibles and ground. A self-generated golden proves only that behaviour stopped changing, so re-pinning without looking would have enshrined whatever was there — exactly the trap W6-03b built its mode-assertion guard to avoid on the SNES side.

FIVE IDENTICAL HASHES ARE COVERAGE, NOT WASTE — worth stating because they look alarming. Spread over four minutes of emulated time, they prove the emulator produces a bit-identical frame from identical state indefinitely: any drift at all (an uninitialised byte, an accumulating counter leaking into video, a mis-scheduled DMA) breaks them. A new test, the_static_goldens_are_the_level_end_not_a_freeze, pins the REASON alongside them so 'the screen stopped changing' can never again be confused with 'the game froze'.

THE DURABLE FIX IS THE POINT OF THIS TICKET. This suite was red since W5-02c and green in CI the entire time, because it is #[ignore]'d and CI runs plain `cargo test --workspace`, which skips ignored tests. BOTH five-minute replays (NES and SNES) are now wired into scripts/local-gate.sh, and docs/TESTING.md has a new 'Hidden gates' section naming the whole class with this incident as its worked example and one rule: if you add an #[ignore]'d test that gates behaviour, add it to local-gate.sh IN THE SAME COMMIT. A gate nothing runs is not a gate.

tickets.title: Per-dot SNES PPU timing (unblocks the undisbeliever set)
acceptance: the SNES PPU composes per DOT rather than per scanline, with mid-line register writes taking effect at their H-position (EMULATION_CORES.md section 3.3's deferred 'per-dot upgrade path')
the undisbeliever hdma-2100-glitch, hdma-21ff-glitch and hdmaen_latch_test ROMs leave forced blank and produce stable golden frames
RotZoom, Perspective and the ten BGMAP goldens are unchanged, proving the upgrade did not disturb what already worked
notes: FILED BY W8-01 BECAUSE IT BLOCKS TWO OPEN TICKETS: W7-07's criterion 4 and W7-05's, both of which name undisbeliever ROMs.

EVIDENCE ALREADY GATHERED (W7-07): all 18 undisbeliever DMA/HDMA ROMs were extracted and run. Every one EXECUTES — PC advances, frames progress — but none leaves forced blank within 12,000,000 instructions; hdmaen_latch_test is still on frame 0 at that point. They are per-DOT timing tests (mid-scanline $2100/$21FF writes during HDMA), and section 3.3 states the v1 PPU is 'scanline-based ... per-dot deferred'. So this is the deferred upgrade, not a bug hunt.

W7-07 ALREADY BUILT HALF THE FOUNDATION: Ppu::line_state latches the mode-7 matrix, BG mode and per-layer scroll once per visible line. Per-dot means latching at finer granularity, or recording writes with their H-position as 3.3 describes — read that code before designing.

THE THIRD CRITERION IS THE GUARD. A per-dot rewrite is exactly the kind of change that fixes one suite and silently breaks another, so the existing goldens are part of the acceptance rather than something to re-pin afterwards.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 2 and 3 DELIVERED; criterion 1 (per-dot composition) NOT started. THIS TICKET'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE RESULT. Its own note said 'this is the deferred upgrade, not a bug hunt'. It was a bug hunt. Cpu::step returned immediately while `stopped` (WAI/STP) without touching the bus, so a halted step cost ZERO master cycles -- and WAI waits for an interrupt, every interrupt this machine raises comes from the raster, and the raster only moves when master cycles are spent. The CPU waited for a vblank that could never arrive. Measured before the fix: hdmaen_latch_test ran 3,000,000 instructions and advanced the clock by 6,840 master cycles, still on frame 0, still in forced blank. Charging one internal CPU cycle (speed::FAST) per halted step makes 17 of the 20 ROMs leave forced blank and render their test screens. Two tickets (W7-05 and W7-07, both closed) recorded the symptom and read it as a per-dot rendering limit; it was a frozen clock. CRITERION 3 HOLDS: all 17 PeterLemon goldens and 198 unit tests are unchanged. CRITERION 2 delivered with two ROMs pinned and one excluded -- and the pinning itself measures what is left: hdma-2100-glitch and hdma-21ff-glitch hash IDENTICALLY, because they differ only in the per-dot behaviour of a mid-scanline $2100/$21FF write, which a scanline-composed PPU cannot express. When criterion 1 lands those two hashes MUST diverge; that is the cheapest available measure of the remaining work. hdmaen_latch_test is excluded: it now leaves forced blank but renders a frame that is entirely palette index 0, the same index-domain vacuity that excludes GreenSpace and RedSpace.

CRITERION 1 ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED 2026-08-21 — the ATTEMPT IS THE DELIVERABLE, because it narrows the remaining work from "build per-dot" to one verification step. Design tried: SEGMENTATION AT WRITE BOUNDARIES rather than rewriting bg/obj/mode7 into per-dot fetchers. Register state only changes where a write happens, so a line split at its write boundaries and composed segment-by-segment yields exactly what a dot-by-dot composer would, while leaving the fetchers (and the 17 goldens criterion 3 protects) alone. Plumbing was ONE call site — bus.rs already holds `timing`, so write_register_at(offset, value, timing.dot()) was the whole wiring; write_register stayed as a dot-0 forwarder so ~50 existing test call sites kept their meaning.

WHY IT WAS REVERTED, and it is not a bug in the segmentation: RotZoom.sfc’s pinned golden CHANGES under per-dot. Isolated properly rather than guessed — disabling segmentation alone (keeping every other edit) returned RotZoom to 6ebfb8ce exactly, which ruled out the more suspicious-looking change (a forced_blank LineState latch) and pinned the cause on segmentation. HDMA is not the trigger: system.rs runs hdma_run_line() BEFORE latch_line(), which clears the buffer, so RotZoom’s segmenting writes are CPU writes during VISIBLE time — exactly the writes per-dot semantics say should take effect mid-line. Composition was also verified IDEMPOTENT, so repeated composition is not the cause either. The new frame is therefore plausibly MORE correct than the pinned one. But criterion 3 says RotZoom must be unchanged, and this suite pins a golden only after the frame was rendered to a PNG and LOOKED AT — a standard that changed three of four outcomes when W7-05 applied it. Shipping it would assert correctness nobody has checked, on the most accuracy-critical path in the emulator.

TO FINISH CRITERION 1, in order: (1) re-apply segmentation (the design above; it took ~80 lines in ppu/mod.rs plus one bus line); (2) LOOK at RotZoom’s per-dot frame — `RF_GOLDEN_DUMP=1 cargo test --release -p rf-snes --test peterlemon_golden -- --ignored` now emits a correctly-headed PPM; (3) if it is right, re-pin RotZoom and AMEND CRITERION 3, which cannot hold as written — "RotZoom unchanged" is unsatisfiable for any ROM that writes registers mid-line, which is precisely the class per-dot exists to render correctly. Criterion 2 (the two glitch ROMs diverging) remains the cheapest ROM-level measure and was NOT reached, since it needs segmentation live.

SIDE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: LineState does NOT latch $2100, so forced_blank composes from the LIVE register — a mid-frame write retroactively blanks lines the beam already passed. Latching it was verified GOLDEN-SAFE (all 3 golden tests pass with it in), but it was reverted with the rest because a lone semantic change with no failing test to justify it is scope creep on an abandoned attempt. Re-apply it with per-dot, where it is REQUIRED: replaying blank-at-dot-128 against an already-blank state yields a wholly blank line.

INVESTIGATED 2026-08-21 (second pass) — AND IT SUPERSEDES TWO CLAIMS I MADE ABOVE. The earlier note said the per-dot RotZoom frame is "plausibly MORE correct than the pinned one" and that criterion 3 is "unsatisfiable as written". BOTH LOOK WRONG. EVIDENCE. Re-applied the segmentation on a scratch branch and diffed every golden: 31 of 32 ROMs are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and RotZoom differs by 105 of 57,344 pixels (0.2%) — all of them on ROW 0 ALONE, one span from x=26 to the right edge. A change confined to the FIRST VISIBLE LINE is not what a genuine mid-line effect looks like; it is what FRAME-SETUP WRITES LANDING ON LINE 0 looks like.

THE TRACE CONFIRMS IT. Logging every write the implementation treated as mid-line: $2104 OAMDATA 16,307 writes, $2122 CGDATA 19,455 at a single dot, $210D BG1HOFS 9,839 — and $211C/$211D (M7B/M7C, RotZoom’s OWN Mode 7 matrix) at dots 1, 2 and 3. Bulk data-port transfers to OAM and CGRAM are what a game does during VBLANK or forced blank, not mid-visible-line, and thousands of writes clustered at dots 1-3 are line/frame SETUP. THE DEFECT: timing.dot() at the moment of a CPU write does not distinguish "dot N of the visible line being composed" from "somewhere in vblank", so setup writes get low dot values, are recorded as mid-line, and split line 0. The pinned golden 6ebfb8ce is RIGHT; the per-dot frame is WRONG. DO NOT RE-PIN ROTZOOM.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE REMAINING WORK. The segmentation DESIGN is sound — the composition machinery works and 31 unchanged ROMs prove it is inert when it should be. What is missing is WRITE ATTRIBUTION: a write must be tagged with (LINE, dot) and vblank/forced-blank writes excluded, rather than trusting a bare dot(). That is a smaller and sharper problem than "build per-dot", and it is the actual next step. AND CRITERION 3 IS PROBABLY FINE AS WRITTEN: if RotZoom’s only change came from the attribution bug, then with correct attribution RotZoom should be UNCHANGED and "RotZoom, Perspective and the ten BGMAP goldens are unchanged" becomes satisfiable. Do not amend it on my earlier say-so — fix attribution first and re-measure. No human needs to look at a frame for this ticket after all.

CLOSED 2026-08-21. CRITERION 1 DELIVERED; 3 GREEN; 2 SUBSTANTIALLY MET WITH ONE HONEST GAP NAMED BELOW. THE PREDICTION IN THE NOTE ABOVE HELD: with correct attribution RotZoom is UNCHANGED, and criterion 3 did not need amending. All 32 PeterLemon goldens, both undisbeliever goldens, gilyon and the region goldens are green. WHAT SHIPPED. (a) Timing::mid_line_position — a write counts as mid-line only when the beam is on a VISIBLE line (line 0 is vblank) and inside the drawn dots; hblank writes belong to the next line, which latch_line already carries. (b) Ppu::write_register_at records (dot, addr, value) per hardware line. (c) compose_line_segmented splits a line at its write dots and composes each segment — segmentation, not a per-dot fetcher, so bg/obj/mode7 and the goldens protecting them are untouched. A line with no writes composes exactly as before, which is why this is inert on 32 of 32 goldens. TWO THINGS THE FIRST ATTEMPT DID NOT KNOW, both found by measuring rather than reasoning. (1) HDMA WRITES ARE NOT MID-LINE. hdma_transfer_unit goes through the same bus write path, and hdma_run_line is driven from the frame loop at whatever dot the CPU reached — so every HDMA write was splitting the very line it was meant to SET UP. StarWars, a Mode 7 perspective demo driven almost entirely by HDMA, turned its starfield into a regular grid of dashes. Fixed with a hdma_in_progress flag; mutation-checked — removing it fails StarWars's golden. (2) DATA PORTS MUST NEVER BE REPLAYED. OAM/VRAM/CGRAM writes are MEMORY writes that have already landed and each auto-increments its address register; replaying one writes again at a second address and composes the rest of the line against corrupted memory. Ppu::is_segmentable excludes $2102-$2104, $2116-$2119 and $2121-$2122. That is also where the traffic is — 16,307 OAMDATA and 19,455 CGDATA writes in one frame. A DESIGN CORRECTION MADE MID-IMPLEMENTATION, worth recording because the obvious route was wrong: segmentation needs to REWIND registers a mid-line write changed, and LineState latches only a subset (scroll, mode 7, windows, colour math, mosaic) — $212C is not in it, so the whole line took the post-write value and no split happened. WIDENING LineState FIXED THAT AND BROKE STARWARS, because LineState is latched for EVERY line, so widening it changes how every line composes and stopped HDMA writes reaching lines through the live registers. That is a real semantic change and smuggling it in under this ticket would be exactly the 'fixes one suite, silently breaks another' failure criterion 3 exists to prevent. Replaced with PpuRegs: a full register snapshot captured ONLY for a line that actually receives a mid-line write, and only just before the first one lands. Lines without one are untouched. CRITERION 2, HONESTLY: hdma-2100-glitch and hdma-21ff-glitch leave forced blank and hold stable pinned goldens. hdmaen_latch_test leaves forced blank too but renders an ENTIRELY index-0 frame, so its hash cannot tell a correct blank screen from a PPU that drew nothing — it stays EXCLUDED with that reason, pre-existing and already covered without a ROM by tests::hdma::enabling_a_channel_mid_frame_does_not_transfer_until_the_next_init. AND THE THING THAT DID NOT HAPPEN, said plainly: an earlier note called the two glitch ROMs DIVERGING 'the cheapest ROM-level measure'. THEY STILL HASH IDENTICALLY. The reason is understood rather than mysterious — their glitch is driven by HDMA writes to $2100, and this model treats HDMA as line setup because hdma_run_line does not fire at a real hblank dot. Modelling that needs HDMA scheduled at its true H-position, which is beyond segmentation and is the honest next step if those two ROMs are ever to discriminate. 7 new tests, every one mutation-checked. workspace 1643 passing (was 1638); nine-command gate + docs-gate green; peterlemon, undisbeliever, gilyon and region ignored suites all green.

tickets.title: rf-core-api: a sub-screen channel so colour math can reach a renderer
acceptance: CoreSink can carry a sub-screen scanline and a per-pixel colour-math mode alongside the accuracy-exact main screen, without displacing it (the W1-05a ruling)
rf-snes emits it, and a golden or A-B test can detect a colour-math change — which no existing test can today
the NES path and every existing CoreSink implementor keep compiling and behaving identically, proven rather than assumed
PpuPixel::dropped_by_limit is either given a real carrier by the same mechanism or removed, with the decision recorded
notes: FILED BY W8-01. Found during W7-05: colour math ($2130-$2132) produces an RGB value that need not exist anywhere in CGRAM, but cores emit INDEXED pixels (law 4) — so a blended colour cannot travel through PpuPixel at all, and the golden-frame hash (palette indices only) could not see it if it did. W7-05 therefore delivered clip-to-black on the indexed path (black IS index 0) and left the add/sub/half arithmetic implemented but unreachable.

THE SAME QUESTION HAS NOW COME UP TWICE. W6-03a found that PpuPixel::dropped_by_limit is dead on BOTH the NES and SNES paths: its doc retains it 'for cores that can express a suppressed sprite without displacing a real pixel', but the one-pixel-per-x sink makes that impossible everywhere. Both features want the same thing — a second, parallel channel — so they should be answered together rather than twice.

THE CONSTRAINT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: rf_core_api::video's W1-05a ruling says video_scanline is accuracy-exact and nothing may displace it. OverlayPixel/overlay_scanline is the existing precedent for a parallel channel; extend that shape rather than fattening PpuPixel.

PER-LINE CGRAM IS THE SAME PROBLEM, FOUND BY W7-07 (2026-08-20). PeterLemon's RedSpaceHDMA drives $2121/$2122 from HDMA to paint a different BACKDROP COLOUR on every scanline -- verified correct by trace ($1F, $1E, $1D ... one step every 7 lines, 32 steps over 224). It is unpinnable as a golden for exactly this ticket's reason: the frame is 100% palette index 0, so an index-domain hash cannot see it, and a renderer handed one palette snapshot per frame cannot draw it either. Whatever mechanism this ticket adds for colour math should be checked against this case too -- per-line CGRAM is not a test-only concern, it is how real games do sunsets and water. Both RedSpace ROMs are already fetched and sit in EXCLUDED in tests/peterlemon_golden.rs, so they are available as the acceptance evidence.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all four criteria. CoreSink gains a THIRD channel, sub_scanline(y, &[SubPixel], fixed_color), modelled exactly on overlay_scanline and defaulted to a no-op -- which is what satisfies criterion 3 by construction: all ten existing implementors compile unedited and the 17 PeterLemon goldens are unchanged. SubPixel carries palette_index + layer + ColorMathOp + a `fixed` flag; the fixed colour ($2132) rides once per LINE because it is a register, and an HDMA-written one. LAW 4 SURVIVES: the core says WHETHER and WHICH operation applies (that is hardware state -- $2130's prevent mode against the colour window, $2131's per-layer enable and its add/subtract/half bits) and the renderer performs the arithmetic, so cores still emit indices only. CRITERION 2's test is the one the ticket said could not exist: flipping $2131 from add to subtract now changes an observable, and the same test asserts the MAIN screen is byte-identical across the flip -- the W1-05a ruling, checked rather than trusted. Mutation-checked both ways. FOUND ON THE WAY: $212D (TS, the sub-screen layer designation) was not handled AT ALL, so a game that set it was configuring a screen nothing composed. CRITERION 4: dropped_by_limit REMOVED from PpuPixel (85 references across 20 files). It was false at every construction site on both cores, its only reader hashed a constant byte per pixel into the mode-invariant digest, and rf_debugger::oam deliberately computes dropped sprites from OAM instead -- its doc says so. Its real carrier, OverlayPixel via overlay_scanline, already existed. NOTE FOR WHOEVER WIRES THE SNES CORE UP: rf-snes implements no EmulatorCore and drives no CoreSink at any point -- frames are pulled directly via SnesSystem::render_scanline, unlike rf-nes which calls sink.video_scanline. So 'rf-snes emits it' means the data is available through render_sub_scanline; there is no sink call to add it to yet. That gap is not this ticket's and is worth its own. ALSO: rf-cache's canvas chunk format carries NO version field, so removing dropped_by_limit from its WirePixel makes older chunks fail to decode -- acceptable only because a canvas chunk is regenerable and a decode error is already handled as a miss.

tickets.title: Rewind
acceptance: rewind per SAVE_STATES.md section 4 and FRONTEND_UI.md section 5 (FR-STATE-008), with a ring of periodic states and a configurable depth
rewinding N seconds and replaying forward reaches state hash-identical to never having rewound
the memory and CPU cost of the ring is measured and recorded, not estimated
notes: The determinism suite is the natural oracle: a rewind that is not hash-identical is a save-state bug wearing a different hat.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all three criteria. crates/rf-state/src/rewind.rs implements SAVE_STATES.md section 4's ring of delta-compressed snapshots (XOR against previous + zstd) with a configurable interval and depth, OFF by default because section 4 is explicit that the memory cost is real. zstd was already an rf-state dependency and is already in TECH_STACK as 'State/canvas/cache compression' — no new dependency.

THE DELTA DIRECTION IS THE DESIGN DECISION, and it is not obvious from section 4's one sentence. The obvious reading — each snapshot XOR'd against its predecessor, reconstructed FORWARD from a base — DOES NOT SURVIVE RING EVICTION: once the base is dropped every delta chained off it is unreadable, and the ring would need periodic full snapshots to recover. This stores the deltas the other way round: the ring keeps the most recent state uncompressed, each entry is the XOR between one snapshot and the NEXT, and because XOR is its own inverse a rewind walks BACKWARDS from the live state (older = newer XOR delta). Evicting the oldest entry then costs nothing but depth — no base to lose, no full snapshot to schedule.

CRITERION 2 IS THE ACCEPTANCE IN EXECUTABLE FORM. A reference machine runs 300 frames straight through; a second runs the same inputs, rewinds 100 frames, and replays forward from the snapshot it landed on. The two are compared BYTE FOR BYTE. A rewind that lands somewhere plausible but not identical is exactly the bug worth catching, and only that comparison catches it. The test machine is state-shaped rather than a counter on purpose — the ring's whole premise is that consecutive states differ in a small fraction of their bytes, and a counter would not exercise it.

CRITERION 3 IS MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED, which is what it asked for. RewindRing tracks its own compressed size and exposes it next to what the same snapshots would cost whole; the test asserts an order-of-magnitude saving and PRINTS the real figure. Measured here: 64 snapshots of a 4 KiB machine cost 4,608 bytes compressed against 266,760 uncompressed — 57.9x. That is the number a UI can show, and it is the claim the XOR-then-compress design rests on: compressing raw states instead would spend the same CPU for a far larger ring.

TWO SMALLER THINGS WORTH KNOWING. push() is CHEAP WHEN DISABLED and returns immediately, so callers invoke it unconditionally rather than branching at every call site — and a test asserts the disabled ring retains nothing and reports zero bytes. And a state whose LENGTH changes (it should not, but a core could grow a chunk) falls back to storing the older state whole, so the ring degrades in SIZE rather than in correctness; that path has its own test.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE: the input-replay half of section 4's 'rewind replays inputs from nearest snapshot'. RewindRing lands the caller on the nearest retained snapshot and stops, because replaying inputs needs a machine and rf-state owns no machine — the caller does. FRONTEND_UI.md section 5's hold-key scrub with a ghost timeline is likewise UI work and belongs with the front end, not the container crate.

tickets.title: Video recording + screenshot polish
acceptance: video recording (FR-FE-007) writes a playable file whose frame count matches the frames emitted
screenshots capture the indexed frame through the same palette path the renderer uses, so a screenshot matches what was on screen
both are exercised by a test that inspects the OUTPUT rather than asserting the call was made
notes: W5-04's lesson applies directly: a capture path that looked correct wrote alpha 0 for palette index 0 and produced a white PNG. LOOK AT THE OUTPUT.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all three criteria. Video recording lands as APNG via a new rf_renderer::png::encode_apng, with crates/retroforge/src/recording.rs accumulating frames and encoding on stop. Screenshots already resolved through the renderer's own palette path (rf_renderer::original_rgba_from_indexed), so criterion 2 was met by existing code and is now PROVEN rather than assumed — see the frame-zero test below.

THE BACKEND DECISION FRONTEND_UI.md SECTION 5 LEFT OPEN IS TAKEN, AND IT IS APNG. That document said 'ffmpeg sidecar or gstreamer TBD at W8 planning'. Both are large: a sidecar makes recording depend on an external binary being installed and on shelling out; gstreamer is a substantial native dependency with a licence review attached (NFR-011). APNG needs neither, because it is PNG plus three chunk types — so it reuses this workspace's existing dependency-free stored-deflate PNG encoder wholesale. That is exactly the reasoning W3-04 already recorded when it wrote that encoder rather than adding a png/image crate, applied one step further. The result plays in browsers, in macOS Preview, and in ffmpeg/mpv.

THE HONEST COST, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: frames are stored UNCOMPRESSED, roughly width*height*4 bytes each — a 64x64 30-frame sample is 495 KB. This is a format for clips and bug reports, not hour-long captures. Recorder::estimated_bytes reports the size as it accrues and Recorder::with_limit lets a UI stop BEFORE filling a disk rather than after, counting what it refused so the recording can be reported as cut.

CRITERION 3 SAID INSPECT THE OUTPUT, SO EVERY TEST DOES. The frame count is read back out of the file's own acTL chunk rather than from the encoder's bookkeeping — which would pass even on a malformed file. The chunk ORDER is asserted as a literal sequence (IHDR, acTL, fcTL, IDAT, fcTL, fdAT, ..., IEND) because acTL must precede the first IDAT and frame 0's pixels must live in IDAT rather than fdAT; get it wrong and a viewer shows ONE FRAME, which looks like 'recording captured one frame' rather than like a broken file. The fcTL/fdAT sequence numbers are checked to be one gapless shared sequence, since a decoder rejects a gap. And a sample APNG was written and fed to an EXTERNAL decoder (macOS sips) which accepted it at 64x64, then rendered and looked at — W5-04's white-PNG lesson applied.

ONE TEST TIES THE TWO HALVES TOGETHER: frame 0 of a recording must encode byte-identical IDAT to the still screenshot of the same image. That is what makes 'a screenshot matches what was on screen' and 'a recording matches what was on screen' the SAME guarantee rather than two separate hopes.

TWO DELIBERATE CHOICES WORTH KNOWING. (a) The file extension is .png, not .apng: an APNG IS a PNG, and every non-APNG decoder shows its first frame rather than refusing the file — naming it .apng would break that graceful degradation with tools that dispatch on extension. (b) A frame whose geometry disagrees with the recording's is REFUSED and counted, never scaled or padded: a recording that silently changed size mid-file would produce a broken APNG, and guessing at a resize is not this module's decision to make.

NOT WIRED TO A UI BUTTON YET. Recorder is a tested, self-contained unit; hooking it to a hotkey and a status line is shell work of the same kind W8-04 (gamepad navigation and the accessibility pass) is about, and belongs with it rather than half-done here. FR-FE-007's 'either pipeline' is already satisfied structurally: the shell resolves both the accuracy-exact and enhanced frames every capture, and Recorder takes whichever it is handed, so the choice stays with the UI.

tickets.title: Gamepad UI navigation + accessibility pass
acceptance: every UI surface is reachable and operable with a gamepad alone (FRONTEND_UI.md section 4)
an accessibility pass against FRONTEND_UI.md section 6: focus order, contrast, and text alternatives
the egui_kittest harness asserts accessibility NODES, not pixels
notes: W4-09's finding is a prerequisite, not a detail: at the harness's default window size every panel rendered ZERO accessible nodes, so the assertions would have been vacuous — it needs 1600x1000. And neither a bare ui.label NOR a hover-sensed egui::Label contributes a node; selectable_label does.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: the navigation MODEL and the accessibility harness are complete and tested; wiring them through every existing surface of app.rs is the remainder. DELIVERED: crates/retroforge/src/ui_nav.rs (11 unit tests) and crates/retroforge/tests/gamepad_nav.rs (5 accessibility-tree tests).

IT DRIVES EGUI'S FOCUS SYSTEM RATHER THAN REPLACING IT, and that is the design decision. egui already has focus with a defined order, Tab/Shift+Tab traversal, arrow movement and Enter/Space activation — and crucially THAT focus is what AccessKit reports, so it is what a screen reader and the headless harness both see. A parallel focus model would have been more code, would NOT have appeared in the accessibility tree, and would have drifted from keyboard behaviour the first time either changed. So NavAction translates to egui::Event and hands over.

BACK AND MENU DELIBERATELY PRODUCE NO KEY EVENT. They are decisions about which window is open, not focus movement, and forging an Escape keypress would ALSO reach any widget that handles Escape itself. Asserted, so nobody 'fixes' it into a forged key later.

AUTO-REPEAT IS THE PART THAT NEEDED CARE, and each failure mode has its own test. Repeating every frame while held makes a list uncontrollable; repeating from the FIRST frame makes a single tap jump two entries. Hence one event on press, silence until a 400 ms delay, then one per 90 ms. Activation does NOT repeat — the difference between scrolling a list and launching thirty games. And a pad DISCONNECTED mid-hold clears the held direction, or the UI scrolls forever with no hardware attached.
BOTH THE D-PAD AND THE LEFT STICK NAVIGATE. A stick-only pad and a d-pad-only pad are both real hardware, and treating either as second-class makes the UI unreachable on it.

CRITERION 3 ASSERTS NODES, AND W4-09'S TWO TRAPS ARE GUARDED EXPLICITLY. (1) The harness runs at 1600x1000 because at the default size every panel renders ZERO accessible nodes and the assertions would be written against an empty tree — the label test therefore also requires at least three interactive nodes to exist, so it cannot pass vacuously. (2) Neither a bare ui.label NOR a hover-sensed egui::Label contributes a node, so the fixture uses selectable_label; a plain label can be reached by neither a gamepad nor a screen reader. The reachability test walks the whole focus order and requires EVERY entry to be visited, because an order that skips one is exactly the bug that makes a surface unreachable — checking a single step would miss it.

WHAT REMAINS: app.rs's own surfaces are not yet routed through GamepadNav. That is mechanical — feed PadEvents in, push events_for() into RawInput, and audit each panel's widgets for labels — but it touches every window in a 2,600-line file and is better done as its own pass than half-finished here. The two hard parts, the input model and a harness that can PROVE reachability rather than assert a call was made, are done. FRONTEND_UI.md section 6's contrast and UI-scale items are also outstanding: they are theme work, not navigation, and were not started.

CLOSED 2026-08-21. The remaining pass is done. app.rs now routes pad input through GamepadNav, and FRONTEND_UI §6’s theme half (crates/retroforge/src/accessibility.rs) is built — both were what the earlier HANDOFF listed as outstanding. THE CORRECTNESS TRAP IN THE WIRING: PadBackend::poll DRAINS. The obvious implementation — leave PadRouter::poll alone and add a second backend.poll() for the UI — hands each consumer roughly HALF the events, giving a d-pad that moves the menu on some presses and the game on others. Events are taken ONCE and fanned out to PadRouter::apply and GamepadNav. PadRouter::apply was already pub, so rf-input needed no change. Auto-repeat ticks on WALL-CLOCK, not per-frame: repeat measured in frames speeds up on a 144 Hz display and crawls on a slow one. Nav actions go into egui RawInput rather than a bespoke focus model, because egui’s focus is what AccessKit reports — so a gamepad driving it is visible to a screen reader AND the headless harness.

A DEFAULT `cargo build` DOES NOT TYPE-CHECK THIS WIRING. The block is #[cfg(feature = "gamepad")], which CI leaves off so the runner needs no evdev/udev — so the seven-item gate passes over it entirely. A green default build reported success while SKIPPING the change, and hid a real error (PadBackend not in scope). VERIFY WITH `--features gamepad`: both `cargo build` and `cargo clippy -p retroforge --features gamepad --all-targets -- -D warnings` were run and are green. Anyone touching this block must do the same.

§6 CONTRAST IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. accessibility.rs implements WCAG 2.1’s real formula including the sRGB gamma expansion that is commonly skipped — skipping it INFLATES every ratio, i.e. flatters the palette, which is the wrong direction to be wrong in. Three of the nine tests exist to stop this being decoration: the published anchors (21:1 black-on-white, 1:1 self), a KNOWN THIRD-PARTY value (#767676 on white ≈ 4.54:1) so the transcription is checked against something other than its own extremes, and an anti-vacuity test that high-contrast is MEASURABLY better than default — without which shipping the same palette twice would pass everything. High contrast is OFF BY DEFAULT: an accommodation imposed on everyone is the same mistake as a default-on enhancement (law 6). ui_scale handles NaN explicitly because NaN SURVIVES clamp, and a NaN pixels_per_point renders nothing — leaving no way to open settings and undo it.

RF-L-10 FIXED HERE, and it was in scope after all: crates/retroforge/tests/** is inside crates/retroforge/**. mode_invariant_corpus.rs’s evidence directory now takes a std::process::id() suffix. PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL FAILURE MODE rather than reasoned about: two deliberately CONCURRENT runs of that suite both pass 6/6, and that pairing is exactly what produced the empty replay-slice.rfreplay before. The bug cost four red runs in one session, including the two stop-hook failures that could not be reproduced afterwards.

tickets.title: SNES widescreen per-BG-layer policies
acceptance: per-BG-layer widescreen policies on the bsnes-hd model, declared per profile
Accuracy Mode is unaffected and a fresh install renders 4:3 (law 6)
a layer whose policy would reveal unrendered content is identified and handled explicitly rather than showing garbage at the edges
notes: The third criterion is the whole difficulty: widescreen shows what the hardware never drew, so each layer needs a declared policy (extend, repeat, letterbox) rather than a global switch.

SCOPE AMENDMENT + SPEC CORRECTION (2026-08-20, standing authority). (a) write_scope gains crates/rf-profiles/** because criterion 1 says the policies are 'declared per profile' and the schema has no place for them: GAME_PROFILES.md 2 has only a single global `widescreen = none|stitched|decoded`. (b) THE POLICY NAMES IN THIS TICKET'S NOTE ARE NOT bsnes-hd's. The note guesses 'extend, repeat, letterbox'; the criterion says 'on the bsnes-hd model', so its README was read (law 2). The real per-BG options are off / on / '< xy' or '> xy' (scanline-conditional) / autoHor / autoHor&Ver (the DEFAULT) / crop / cropAuto / disable, and sprites have their own clip / safe (default) / unsafe / disable. Implemented to the real model. THE AUTO POLICIES ARE CRITERION 3's MECHANISM, which is why this matters: 'autoHor' disables widescreen when the background spans full width with horizontal position 0 -- that is a HUD or a static full-screen image, and widening it reveals nothing the hardware ever drew. bsnes-hd also states plainly that 'Objects/Sprites will not be visible correctly in the widescreen areas', which is why its sprite default is 'safe' (render only if partially inside the classic 4:3 area) rather than 'on'.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all three criteria. rf-enhance/src/widescreen.rs holds the policies and the decision; rf-profiles gains an optional [widescreen] table. CRITERION 3 WAS ALREADY SOLVED BY THE EMULATOR THE CRITERION NAMES, which is why reading bsnes-hd's README beat guessing: its `autoHor` / `autoHor&Ver` policies disable widescreen for a background that 'spans full width with horizontal position 0', because such a layer is a HUD or a static image and the columns past 256 hold VRAM the hardware never drew. That is a DETECTION rather than a declaration, which is what makes it safe as the default for profiles nobody has hand-tuned -- and it is bsnes-hd's default too, so it is ours. Sprites default to `safe` (draw only if partly inside the classic area) because bsnes-hd states plainly that 'Objects/Sprites will not be visible correctly in the widescreen areas': OAM gives a sprite one X in a 256-wide space, so there is no such thing as a sprite meant to be out there. LAW 6 IS STRUCTURAL: WidescreenPolicies::default() is DISABLED, decide_all returns narrow for every layer when disabled so a caller cannot forget to check, and A PROFILE CANNOT ENABLE WIDESCREEN -- there is deliberately no `enabled` field in the schema, exactly as [mods] has no way for a profile to switch itself on. An unknown policy name is REFUSED rather than defaulted, including 'letterbox' from this ticket's own note, since silently reading a typo as 'off' hands the author a 4:3 layer and no reason why. Mutation-checked three ways.

tickets.title: HUD separation (profile-driven + heuristic)
acceptance: HUD separation per FR-ENH-007, driven by a profile declaration and by a heuristic where none is declared
the heuristic's inputs are the ScrollWrite and HDMA events EMULATION_CORES.md section 3.2 names, not pixel guessing
a false positive is visible in the ledger rather than silently altering the picture
notes: Depends on W7-07 because HDMA is what makes most split-screen HUDs work, and section 3.2 says those events feed this directly.

CLOSED 2026-08-21: all three criteria. rf-enhance/src/hud.rs. THE FRAMING THAT MADE IT TRACTABLE: a split-screen HUD is not a picture, it is a SCROLL DISCONTINUITY -- the game writes one scroll value for the status bar and another for the playfield part-way down the frame. That is why criterion 2 forbids pixel guessing and names ScrollWrite + HDMA: those events ARE the phenomenon, and pixels are only its consequence. scroll_tracker::compute_bands already turned those events into bands and left ScanlineBand::is_hud permanently false; this module is what fills it in, so no new event plumbing was needed. CRITERION 3 IS THE TRUST LADDER, NOT A NEW MECHANISM: D-004's Shadow is the default everywhere and means detect-and-record, never act, so a fresh install cannot have a HUD false positive alter the picture -- the verdict goes to the report card and Verdict::acted says which happened rather than leaving a caller to infer it. THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS, each mutation-checked: (a) EDGE BANDS ONLY -- a mid-screen scroll split is parallax or a water effect, and pinning one would freeze the wrong half of the picture; (b) THREE STABLE FRAMES before naming a HUD, because one frame of 'this band did not scroll' is just a paused game and would grow a HUD on every pause; (c) A PROFILE DECLARATION WINS OUTRIGHT AND ACTS WITHOUT THE LADDER (it is a human statement, not a heuristic), but the heuristic still RUNS and a disagreement is recorded -- being wrong here, where somebody checked, predicts being wrong on the next game where nobody wrote a profile. Also removed a dead guard the mutation run exposed: `std::ptr::eq(candidate, playfield)` could never fire, since a band cannot have a scroll different from its own.

tickets.title: Profile-declared loading fast-forward
acceptance: fast-forward during profile-declared loading windows (FR-ENH-008), off by default and ledger-logged
the emulated machine's state is IDENTICAL to running at normal speed — fast-forward changes wall-clock time only, never simulation
a determinism double-run with fast-forward enabled matches one without it
notes: The second and third criteria are the ones that matter: a fast-forward that changes emulated state is a determinism bug (law 4), not a feature.

CLOSED 2026-08-20: all three criteria. crates/rf-enhance/src/loading.rs decides pacing from a profile's [loading].wait_loops (PC + condition), OFF by default (law 6), with every window ledgered by the profile author's own label rather than by an address.

IT CANNOT ALTER SIMULATION BECAUSE IT IS GIVEN NO WAY TO. FR-ENH-008 says fast-forward must disable frame pacing 'without altering simulation', and a fast-forward that changed emulated state would be a determinism bug (law 4) rather than a feature. So FastForward owns no machine: it takes a READ-ONLY probe and returns a Pacing decision. That makes the constraint close to structural — but almost is not a test, so the acceptance is proved by driving a real deterministic machine through identical input twice, once enabled and once not, and requiring the two to end BYTE-IDENTICAL. A test that only compared pacing decisions would pass on an implementation that also poked memory.

THE DETERMINISM TEST CAUGHT A REAL SEMANTIC BUG ON ITS FIRST RUN, and it was the exact one this module's own doc had predicted. `until = { addr, equals }` reads 'wait UNTIL addr equals this', so the wait is in progress while the address does NOT hold that value. The first implementation compared with == and therefore flagged EXACTLY ONE frame: the one the wait finished on. The test reported 1 unpaced frame instead of 30, and that single frame was the LAST rather than the first. The module doc already said 'a game will also pass through [the PC] on the frame the wait ENDS' — it turned out to be describing the bug rather than guarding against it, which is why the fix carries that story in the code.

THE ANTI-VACUITY GUARD MATTERS HERE MORE THAN USUAL. 'Enabled and disabled runs match' is trivially true if the enabled run never fast-forwarded — so the test also asserts the enabled run had a non-zero unpaced count and the disabled run had zero. Without that, the whole criterion could pass on a feature that did nothing.

PC ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, which is why the profile schema carries both. The same address is reached once per loop iteration whether the wait has one frame left or a thousand, and the game passes through it on the frame the wait ends. Tested in all three directions: at the PC with the condition unmet (waiting), at the PC with it met (over), and elsewhere with it unmet (not waiting).

A PLAYER TOGGLING MID-LOAD IS THE OBVIOUS REAL CASE, so it has its own test: enabling at frame 10 and disabling at frame 20 must still produce a machine identical to never enabling it, and the ledger must stay BALANCED — disabling mid-window closes the open entry, because a ledger that says a window opened and never closed is worse than no ledger.

tickets.title: Smooth-camera and room-stitching experiments
acceptance: profile-gated entity interpolation (smooth camera) and room-stitching for top-down profiles (ROADMAP P8)
both are opt-in overlays with honesty-contract UI labels, and Accuracy Mode shows neither
each ships with the A-B test ROADMAP P8's exit criteria require
notes: ROADMAP P8's exit criteria are explicit that EACH feature ships with its own golden/A-B tests, per-game override knobs and honesty-contract labels — that is acceptance, not decoration.

CLOSED 2026-08-21: all three criteria. rf-enhance/src/experiments.rs. THE TWO FEATURES SHARE ONE PROBLEM AND DIFFER ON THE ANSWER: both show the player something the hardware never produced, but smooth camera INVENTS positions between the game's own updates while room stitching REVEALS pixels the game really made, just earlier. They therefore carry different HonestyLabels with an explicit `invents` flag rather than one shared 'enhanced' badge, and a test asserts the two disagree on it -- blurring that distinction is the exact dishonesty law 6 exists to prevent. P8's THREE EXIT CRITERIA ARE MET BY MECHANISMS THAT ALREADY EXISTED, which is why this is 8 points of care rather than 8 points of new machinery: per-game override knobs are TrustLadder::pin (FR-ENH-011 already says 'profiles may pin states', and a second override mechanism would just be a second thing to disagree with the first); the labels are carried BY the feature so a surface that forgets to show one is a visible omission; and each A-B test asserts BOTH that the feature is inert when ungated (law 6) AND that it changes something when gated (anti-vacuity, since 'inert' otherwise passes for 'working'). DETAILS WORTH KEEPING: interpolation is fixed-point (alpha 0..=255, integer lerp) not f32, because a replay that reproduces only on the same FPU does not reproduce; the first frame returns None rather than an invented origin, since treating a missing previous frame as (0,0) slams the camera to the corner; and rooms are kept in a BTreeMap keyed by SceneId rather than merged into one plane, because two top-down rooms both start at (0,0) and one plane would overlay them -- the ordered map also gives a map view a stable order so its own golden can exist. SceneId gained Ord for that. Mutation-checked four ways.

tickets.title: AI upscaling cache + replacement pack format
acceptance: the offline pack pipeline and cache per FR-AI-001/002/003/004, cache-keyed so a pack is reproducible from its inputs
animation-set grouping and the pack manifest format per ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME.md section 6
a pack that does not match its declared inputs is REFUSED with a diagnostic rather than partially applied
notes: The third criterion is the honesty contract in mechanical form: a half-applied replacement pack is worse than none, because the player cannot tell which pixels are the game's.

HANDOFF 2026-08-20: criteria 2 and 3 COMPLETE, criterion 1 PARTIAL — the cache-key and reproducibility half is delivered; the inference half needs a model runtime that is a TECH_STACK decision. DELIVERED: crates/rf-ai/src/pack.rs (the replacement-pack manifest, the FR-AI-002 (rom, asset, model, settings) key, and all-or-nothing validation) and crates/rf-ai/src/animation.rs (section 6's sprite grouping). 20 tests. rf-ai was a 15-line stub before this.

ONE FORMAT FOR AI PACKS AND ARTIST PACKS, because section 6 and FR-AI-004 both insist on it. Nothing in PackManifest is AI-specific: what produced the pixels is ONE FIELD (model_id), so an artist pack and a model pack validate through the same path and cache side by side under different keys. A test asserts exactly that.

THE PALETTE IS PART OF AN ASSET'S IDENTITY. Section 6 says matching is hash-based like Mesen HD packs rather than fuzzy, and asset_hash therefore covers indexed pixels AND the palette they are indexed against — the same tile bytes under two palettes are two different pictures. Keying on pixels alone produces the classic HD-pack artefact where a recoloured enemy wears its sibling's skin. Lengths are hashed too, so two different splits of the same bytes cannot collide.

SETTINGS ORDER MUST NOT MATTER, or the cache misses for a reason no user could understand: two callers setting the same options in different sequences must hit the SAME entry. Hence a BTreeMap and a test. The key's digest is a HASH rather than a concatenation — concatenating four hex strings makes paths long enough to hit filesystem limits, and lets a field containing the separator forge another key.

CRITERION 3 IS THE HONESTY CONTRACT IN MECHANICAL FORM, and it is ALL-OR-NOTHING. A pack that does not match its declared inputs is refused WHOLE, because a half-applied pack is worse than none: the player can no longer tell which pixels are the game's, which is the exact thing the contract exists to prevent. Validation also collects EVERY fault rather than returning the first, so a pack author fixes them in one pass instead of one per run, and each diagnostic names both sides (the running ROM and the pack's) so it can be acted on.

SECTION 6'S GROUPING NEEDS BOTH SIGNALS, AND NEITHER ALONE WOULD DO. OAM tile id groups a sprite with itself across frames but also groups unrelated sprites that reuse a tile (shared blanks, repeated UI glyphs); adjacency-in-time catches 'this replaced that', which is what an animation IS, but alone would chain two entities that pass through the same pixel. The motivation is concrete: upscaling each frame of a walk cycle independently gives eight subtly different characters that flicker between one another in motion — invisible in a screenshot, glaring in play.

A DETAIL THAT WOULD HAVE SILENTLY GROUPED NOTHING: the position test needs SLACK. A walking character moves a pixel or two per frame, so a zero tolerance would split every walk cycle into single-frame sets — grouping nothing while appearing to work, and producing exactly the per-frame packs the feature exists to avoid. POSITION_TOLERANCE is 8, with tests on both sides of the boundary. Set ids are derived from their MEMBERS rather than discovery order, because a set that renamed itself between runs would break the reproducibility criterion 1 asks for.

WHAT CRITERION 1 STILL OWES, AND WHY IT IS NOT HERE. 'The offline pack pipeline' needs a local ONNX runtime (ROADMAP P8 names ort) to actually produce upscaled pixels. That is a docs/TECH_STACK.md row plus an NFR-011 licence review plus a model artifact — a dependency decision on the scale of the wgpu and egui rows, not something to take inside a ticket whose write_scope is crates/rf-ai/**. Everything AROUND the model is done and tested: the contract assets are keyed by, the format the output lands in, the grouping that makes the output coherent, and the refusal that keeps a bad pack from being half-applied. RECOMMEND filing the ort/model decision as its own ticket.

RULING (Brad, 2026-08-20, in response to the unattended loop’s four blocking questions). ADD `ort` AND DO THE INFERENCE. Criterion 1’s inference half is authorised: add the docs/TECH_STACK.md row for the ONNX runtime, run the NFR-011 licence pass on it and its tree, and make the offline pack pipeline actually produce upscaled pixels. write_scope is widened to docs/TECH_STACK.md for the row. Constraints that do NOT move: law 6 (Accuracy Mode is the reference — upscaling is an opt-in overlay, never the default), no model weights in git (fetch-and-pin like the ROM and vector fetchers, gitignored, CI has no artifacts), and the all-or-nothing pack refusal already delivered stays. If the runtime turns out to need a model artifact with a licence that fails NFR-011, STOP and record it rather than shipping the row anyway.

DESIGN: docs/design/AI_UPSCALING.md (written 2026-08-21). §4 resolves a question neither this ticket nor ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME §6 had addressed: float ONNX inference is NOT bit-reproducible across runtime versions or execution providers, so model_id alone does not pin output pixels. The pipeline folds Upscaler::provenance() into the settings map under the RESERVED key rf.provenance (a caller who supplies it is REFUSED), so a runtime change changes the KEY rather than changing the pixels behind an unchanged one. What is guaranteed is stated exactly, and what is NOT — that two machines produce identical pixels from the same model — is stated too.

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: ALL THREE CRITERIA NOW COMPLETE; criterion 1's inference half delivered per Brad's ruling. ort 2.0.0-rc.13 adopted behind rf-ai's OFF-BY-DEFAULT `onnx` feature (TECH_STACK row added). NFR-011 pass done and it changed the shape of the dependency: ort's DEFAULT features (download-binaries + tls-native) resolve 73 crates including webpki-root-certs under CDLA-Permissive-2.0, which is NOT on deny.toml's allowlist and would have needed a per-crate exception — and deny.toml is OUTSIDE this write_scope. With default-features=false + load-dynamic the tree is 20 crates and `cargo deny --all-features check licenses` passes with NO allowlist change. NOTE the --all-features part: plain `cargo deny list` omits optional deps and does not see ort at all, so checking without it proves nothing. BRAD'S STOP CONDITION DID NOT TRIGGER, because NO MODEL IS SHIPPED, NAMED OR FETCHED — the pipeline is model-agnostic (model_id is caller-supplied), so the weights choice is left open rather than made silently. Whoever adopts specific weights records their licence status; the rom-manifest precedent (LicenseStatus::NoLicenseGrantFetchOnly) is the mechanism. rf-ai: 41 tests default, 44 with --features onnx; workspace 1495 passing.

BLOCKED/OUT OF SCOPE (follow-up ticket recommended). (1) THE ONNX PATH AGAINST A REAL MODEL IS UNPROVEN BY AUTOMATION. An #[ignore]'d inference test needs a scripts/local-gate.sh row and a docs/evidence/local-gate.json row, and BOTH files are outside this write_scope; so is scripts/** for a runtime/weights fetcher. What IS proven without a runtime: that a missing dylib is an error rather than a process abort, and that a model whose output shape disagrees with the declared scale is refused. (2) docs/MODULE_DESIGN.md documents rf-ai's public API surface and lives at docs/ root, not docs/design/**, so the four new public modules are not recorded there — and rf-ai's own lib.rs module doc points readers at it. (3) sheet_of puts NO BOUND on sheet width, so a large animation set produces one inference call sized by input alone; that is the most likely way the one-call coherence guarantee meets a real model that will not accept it.

tickets.title: Translation and accessibility overlays
acceptance: translation and accessibility overlays driven by profile declarations
overlays are opt-in, ledger-logged, and absent in Accuracy Mode
text an overlay replaces is identifiable in the ledger, so a player can always tell what was changed
notes: Same honesty contract as every other enhancement: the player must be able to tell what is the game and what is ours.

SCOPE BLOCKER found 2026-08-21 while orienting (ticket was claimed, then released unworked so W8-11 could take lowest-id order). Criterion 1 says overlays are "driven by profile declarations", but this write_scope is crates/rf-enhance/** + profiles/** and the PROFILE SCHEMA lives in crates/rf-profiles/src/schema.rs. Profile has NO serde(deny_unknown_fields), so a [translation] table in a profile TOML is SILENTLY IGNORED rather than rejected — an in-scope example profile would look right and do nothing. Wiring it needs one Option<Translation> field on Profile plus the struct, i.e. crates/rf-profiles/**, which is OUT OF SCOPE; GAME_PROFILES.md §2 (docs/design/**) documents the table and is also out of scope. Precedent says do not take this unattended: W8-11-era note records "amending scope to add docs/** is a one-line ruling; it was not taken unattended". RECOMMEND asking Brad to add crates/rf-profiles/** + docs/design/** to this write_scope, or splitting the schema field into its own ticket. Everything else — the overlay engine, the ledger, the Accuracy-Mode absence and criterion 3’s replaced-text identifiability — is fully in scope.

SCOPE AMENDED 2026-08-21 ON BRAD'S RULING: `crates/rf-profiles/**` and `docs/design/**` added, in response to the scope blocker recorded in the note above. Criterion 1 requires overlays "driven by profile declarations" and the profile schema lives in crates/rf-profiles/src/schema.rs; GAME_PROFILES.md §2 (docs/design/**) is where the table is specified. Same one-line-ruling shape as the earlier `docs/**` amendment on another ticket. Recorded as vetoable.

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: ALL THREE CRITERIA COMPLETE. rf-profiles gains `[text]` (regions + entries) and rf-enhance gains overlay.rs; 13 tests. CRITERION 3 DROVE THE SCHEMA: the ledger carries the ORIGINAL STRING VERBATIM, which is why TextEntry::original is stored as text rather than a hash — a ledger naming only the region would satisfy a careless reading and still leave the player unable to read what the game actually said. LAW 6 IS STRUCTURAL, not disciplinary: [text] has NO `enabled` key (same as [widescreen] and [mods]), and Overlays::resolve returns Unchanged WITHOUT consulting the table when the mode is Off, so a caller cannot forget to check first. A SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH WAS FOUND AND FIXED: adding the serde struct was NOT enough — `retroforge-tool profile validate` still warned `unknown key text` because rf-profiles/src/shape.rs keeps its own key tree for FR-PROF-004. Profile has no deny_unknown_fields, so a table missing from shape.rs deserialises fine and merely warns. Both are now in step; keep them so.

WHY THE EXAMPLE IS IN rf-scroller-DEMO AND NOT THE REAL PROFILE: RF-Scroller DRAWS NO TEXT. init_video() fills HUD rows 0-1 with solid tiles ($0C, and $0B which is sprite-0’s opaque BG collision partner) and the fixture has no glyph set at all. Declaring [text] on profiles/nes/rf-scroller would mean inventing strings the ROM never renders — a profile lying about what a game says is exactly what this feature’s honesty contract exists to prevent. The demo profile already carries a placeholder identity and is the honest home until a fixture with real glyphs exists.

OUT OF SCOPE / follow-up. (1) NO RENDERER OR UI WIRING: Overlays::resolve is a pure function; nothing draws the replaced text and no surface shows TEXT_OVERLAY_LABEL yet (crates/rf-renderer/** and crates/retroforge/** are outside this write_scope). (2) NO TRUST-LADDER INTEGRATION: TEXT_OVERLAY is defined as a heuristic name but Overlays does not consult TrustLadder — unlike hud.rs, this feature is profile-DECLARED rather than heuristically detected, so there is no detection to ladder; revisit if text detection (ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME §6’s later AI capability) ever lands. (3) NO GLYPH RENDERING: replacement strings are returned as text, not rasterised — fitting a longer translation into a fixed-width HUD box is a real unsolved problem this ticket does not address.

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: ALL THREE CRITERIA COMPLETE. wasmtime 47.0.4 adopted (TECH_STACK row; the row had said 46 — 48.0.0 needs Rust 1.95 and this workspace pins 1.94). crates/rf-plugin-sdk/wit/plugin.wit is the WIT world, src/component.rs the host; 42 tests in the crate (was 16). NFR-011: default features resolve 244 crates including ittapi/ittapi-sys at GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-3-Clause and the icu_*/zerovec family at Unicode-3.0. With default-features=false + runtime,cranelift,component-model,std the tree is 114 and both are gone — cargo deny --all-features check licenses passes with NO allowlist change, which mattered because deny.toml is outside this write_scope. icu_properties@2.2.0 IS in the workspace graph but pre-dates this ticket (W1-06 frontend stack; confirmed by re-resolving with the dep stashed).

THE SANDBOX IS THE LINKER, and NOTHING IS STUBBED. A host interface is linked iff the manifest grants it; an ungranted import is a MISSING import. No no-op stubs, because a stub is exactly criterion 3’s failure mode — the plugin runs, does nothing, reports success. Three refusals with distinct diagnostics: CapabilitiesNotGranted (lists EVERY ungranted one at once; the author’s manifest), CapabilityNotImplemented (names it; OURS — their manifest is correct), UnknownImport (deny-by-default covers the unknown case).

TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN REVIEW WHERE SHIPPED CODE CONTRADICTED ITS OWN DOCS — same species as W8-12’s shape.rs finding, and the THIRD second-source-of-truth in this project that no compiler checks. (1) plugin.wit was read by NOTHING while the module doc claimed the exhaustive match caught WIT-vs-enum drift; it does not — the match covers Capabilities-field-vs-enum only. Now include_str!’d as WIT_WORLD with four drift tests INCLUDING an interface COUNT (without the count, an interface added to the WIT and not the enum still passes). (2) link_granted registered an EMPTY INSTANCE for the five unimplemented capabilities, three lines under a comment saying that would "make the capability appear granted while doing nothing". Now Capability::is_implemented() + a distinct CapabilityNotImplemented refused by name. Before this, instantiate() — the tier’s ONLY execution path — had no test at all; all six component tests hit check_imports.

SCOPE/SPEC NOTE: criterion 1 cites PLUGINS.md §1, which is a TIER TABLE and specifies NO world. The WIT world’s shape — one interface per capability, and the single `on-frame` export — is therefore a W9-03 DESIGN DECISION, not a pre-existing requirement implemented; recorded as new §1.1 rather than claimed as conformance. IMPLEMENTED host-side: read-memory, write-memory (ledgered — §2’s mod boundary), frame-events, scanline-events. DECLARED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED: read-ppu, draw-overlay, replace-layers, input-bindings, filesystem — each needs renderer/input/cache plumbing outside rf-plugin-sdk, and each is refused BY NAME. No app-shell wiring: nothing loads a component at runtime yet (crates/retroforge/** is outside this write_scope).

tickets.title: Community distribution format for packs, profiles and mods
acceptance: a distribution format carrying packs, profiles and mods with REQUIRED licence metadata (FR-PROF-005/006/007)
no ROM data can be embedded: an archive containing any is refused with a diagnostic, tested with a deliberately poisoned archive
an intake CI check that a third-party submission passes or fails on its own merits
notes: 'Community-safe: no ROM data, license metadata required' is ROADMAP P9's phrasing and is a hard requirement rather than a guideline — CLAUDE.md law 5 is the project-side counterpart.
The poisoned-archive test is the acceptance that matters: a format that merely DOCUMENTS the rule will eventually carry a ROM.
DESIGN: docs/design/DISTRIBUTION.md (written 2026-08-21).

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: ALL THREE CRITERIA COMPLETE. crates/rf-enhance/src/distribution.rs (16 unit tests), tests/intake_poisoned_bundle.rs (5 on-disk tests), bin/rf-intake.rs, docs/design/DISTRIBUTION.md. THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION, and the obvious one is BACKWARDS: the ALLOWLIST over member kinds is the guard; sniff_rom is only the DIAGNOSTIC. A denylist of ROM signatures cannot work — renaming game.nes to data.bin defeats an extension check and a headerless dump (most SNES ROMs) defeats a magic-byte check. A bundle may carry ONLY profile/pack-manifest/pack-image/mod-patch/license/readme; there is deliberately NO `other`/`data` variant. An arbitrary blob is refused for being UNCLASSIFIABLE, not for resembling a ROM. Both run on every member, because the sniffer catches the one case the allowlist cannot: a ROM LABELLED as a legitimate pack-image.

WHAT PASSING DOES NOT MEAN, and a test asserts the wording: intake CANNOT prove a bundle contains no ROM data — a submitter can base64 a ROM into a readme. IntakeReport::summary() states exactly what a pass establishes (no member declared an uncarried kind; nothing matched a ROM signature) and says it is NOT proof. An ACCEPTED reading as "verified ROM-free" would be the same overclaim this project refuses everywhere else. LICENCE: three outcomes, and the split between the last two is the easy-to-miss half of FR-PROF-007 — absent is MissingLicense, recognised-and-unacceptable is DeniedLicense WITH THE REASON (NC/ND/GFDL/GPL/SSPL), and anything else is UnknownLicense, REFUSED rather than assumed permissive.

OUT OF SCOPE / follow-up. (1) NOTHING INVOKES rf-intake IN CI — .github/** is outside this write_scope, so FR-PROF-007’s "nothing activates without passing" is currently a property of the CODE PATH, not of the repository’s automation. The check is AVAILABLE, not ENFORCED. Wire `rf-intake <dir>` into ci.yml; exit codes are 0 accepted / 1 refused / 2 unreadable. (2) NO ARCHIVE CONTAINER: a bundle is a directory; .zip vs .tar.zst is a packaging decision for its own ticket and the intake rules are identical either way. (3) NO SIGNATURE OR AUTHORSHIP VERIFICATION: `provenance` is a required STRING and nothing checks that it is true.
