The third criterion needs a real pack: check one is obtainable and licence-clear BEFORE claiming, or this stalls exactly like W7-05, W7-08 and W7-11 did on artifacts that did not exist.

PRE-CLAIM CHECK RUN 2026-08-21, AS THIS TICKET'S OWN NOTE DEMANDS — AND IT FAILED. Criterion 3 wants "a real community pack imported end to end in a test", but docs/SCOPE.md's game-aware row lists "third-party assets as gate fixtures" in the OUT column, and community HD packs are derived works keyed to copyrighted games with no clear licence (FR-PROF-007/NFR-011 deny unlicensed content; law 5 forbids ROM bytes). W8-11 hit the identical wall and recorded it. This write_scope is crates/rf-enhance/** only, so the fetch-and-pin manifest path (rf-harness + tests/rom-manifest.toml, which has a LicenseStatus::NoLicenseGrantFetchOnly category for exactly this) is also unavailable in-ticket.

RULING (Brad, 2026-08-21): DO CRITERIA 1 AND 2, BLOCK CRITERION 3 pending a licence-clear artifact — same shape W8-10 sat in before the ort ruling. Import + apply and the PARTIAL reporting are both fully inside this write_scope; criterion 3 is not, and is recorded rather than faked against a pack we authored ourselves.

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: CRITERIA 1 AND 2 COMPLETE, CRITERION 3 BLOCKED (Brad's ruling above). rf-enhance/src/hdpack.rs gains import()/Import/Unsatisfied; 27 hdpack tests (7 new). CRITERION 2 TURNED ON ONE JUDGEMENT: a partial pack is REPORTED, NOT REFUSED. Refusing outright throws away work the author did do; what is forbidden is applying it QUIETLY. A pack that half-applies without saying so breaks the honesty contract in the most confusing way possible — some tiles change, some do not, and the player cannot tell which was intended. Import::Partial keeps usable rules usable and names every gap. EVERY GAP NAMES THE TILE, not just the file: an author with 400 rules needs to know WHICH. Three kinds — MissingImage, UnevaluatedCondition (W8-11 ledgers the condition NAME; this names the affected TILE, which is what is actionable) and RegionOutOfBounds (reported with BOTH sizes). This is the CONSUMER of W8-11's identity, not a second implementation: matching still goes through HdPack::lookup, and a test asserts the default-tile fallback still works after import.

CRITERION 3 REMAINS BLOCKED AND IS NOT DONE: no real community pack was imported end to end. To unblock, EITHER designate a licence-clear HD pack as a fetch-only artifact (tests/rom-manifest.toml already has LicenseStatus::NoLicenseGrantFetchOnly for exactly this posture — but reaching it means widening write_scope to crates/rf-harness/** + tests/**), OR amend what criterion 3 accepts as proof. Do NOT satisfy it with a pack we authored ourselves; that would prove the importer against its own author rather than against a pack from the wild, which is the entire point of the criterion.

SCOPE AMENDMENT + RULING (Brad, 2026-08-21, third pass): write_scope gains crates/rf-harness/** and tests/** so criterion 3 can be satisfied the way this project already handles every other unlicensed test artifact — a pinned-commit fetch, never a vendored copy. RESEARCH THAT PRECEDED THE RULING, because the ticket's own note demanded it: NO LICENCE-CLEAR COMMUNITY HD PACK EXISTS. Every pack in the wild is a derived work of copyrighted commercial game art; TasticHacks/Contra80s, AxlRocks/Megaman-Super and ModernRetroDesign/ZII-mesen all report NO LICENSE on GitHub. Mesen itself is GPLv3 but that covers the emulator, not packs. So 'find a licence-clear pack' had no candidate and the choice was really between a fetch-only pin and amending the criterion. ALSO CORRECTED: the earlier pre-claim note cited docs/SCOPE.md's 'third-party assets as gate fixtures' OUT entry, but that sits on the ENHANCEMENT (GAME-AWARE) row. W9-06 is on the ASSET REPLACEMENT row, whose OUT column is empty and whose Later column literally reads 'Mesen hires.txt import'. The distinction that does survive is real and worth stating: the 81 artifacts already fetched at license_status=no-license-grant-fetch-only are hardware-conformance test ROMs, not commercial game art. Brad ruled that the fetch-only posture — fetch-from-origin only, never vendored/mirrored/re-hosted, dest under gitignored roms/ — carries over. CHOSEN ARTIFACT: AxlRocks/Megaman-Super at commit be6f9c23335666aaface41d4598a299a09ab110b (2022-12-14, repo inactive since). Checked before pinning rather than after: hires.txt is 774 KB of 106 with 7,412 lines, 302 lines, 89 refs, 708 , 17 and 2 . (THOSE FIRST FIGURES WERE COUNTED WRONG WHEN THIS NOTE WAS WRITTEN and are corrected here: the first count matched only tags at line START and so missed every condition-prefixed line — which is the entire population and 1,373 of the lines. The parser's real totals are 7,349 tile rules, 301 conditions.) Contra80s was the obvious first candidate and was REJECTED on inspection — it contains no hires.txt at all, only a README and 47 MB of promo banners.

CLOSED 2026-08-21 (third pass). ALL THREE CRITERIA GREEN. Criterion 3 is satisfied by crates/rf-enhance/tests/mesen_hdpack_real.rs importing AxlRocks/Megaman-Super @ be6f9c2 end to end: 7,349 tile rules, 301 conditions, 89 images, ZERO missing images, ZERO out-of-bounds regions, reported as PARTIAL with 3,655 NAMED gaps. FOUR THINGS A PACK FROM THE WILD FOUND THAT OUR OWN FIXTURES COULD NOT — which is the entire argument for this criterion existing. (1) A REAL DEFECT: <tile> carries NINE fields, not the seven the published spec documents, on all 7,349 rules. parse_hires required EQUALITY and rejected the whole real-world corpus at line 487. Checked against Mesen's own HdPackLoader.cpp rather than guessed: it reads tokens positionally and never checks that none remain, so `need(n)` is now a MINIMUM. Being stricter than the reference implementation is a defect in a compatibility importer, not rigour. (2) AN HONESTY VIOLATION criterion 2 forbids: the parser's catch-all arm silently dropped <background> (702 uses), <bgm> (17) and <patch> (2). HdPack::unsupported now counts them and import() reports them as Unsatisfied::UnsupportedDirective. Not implementing them is correct per SCOPE.md; dropping them QUIETLY was not. (3) A duplicate <condition> declaration (Wily03ScreenChecker1D) that no hand-written fixture would have contained. (4) 63 commented-out <tile> lines using '#', which the parser skips correctly by accident since they do not start with '<'. MANIFEST CHANGE, and why it was necessary rather than convenient: GitArtifact.subpath became subpaths: Vec<String>. Cone mode natively takes N directories and always includes root files; the pack's images sit in root + Submerged/ + Cutscenes/. Fetching only the root would have made the importer report 20 tiles as MissingImage for a gap OUR FETCH created — manufacturing exactly the silent-degradation finding this ticket exists to prevent. One existing entry migrated; validate() now rejects an empty list, because empty would degrade to a root-only checkout that SUCCEEDS while missing most of the artifact. DELIBERATELY NOT FETCHED: Backdrops/, which only <background> references — unimplemented, so the images would be dead weight and the directive is reported instead. Implementing backgrounds means adding that subpath in the same commit. BLIND SPOT, STATED SO THE NEXT PASS DOES NOT ASSUME OTHERWISE: criterion 3's proof needs the network and is #[ignore]'d, so the nine-command gate does NOT cover it — run `cargo run -p rf-harness --bin fetch-test-roms -- mesen-hdpack-megaman-super` then `cargo test -p rf-enhance --test mesen_hdpack_real -- --ignored`. That is the same hole that hid two real defects in the SNES hires path earlier the same day (W7-06). Gate green, workspace 1617 passing.

tickets.title: Documentation site
acceptance: a documentation site built from docs/ in CI, so it cannot drift from the repository
the site covers the profile format, the pack format and the plugin SDK — the three things a third party needs
every code sample in the site is compiled or executed by CI
notes: ROADMAP P9's exit criterion is 'a third party ships a profile + pack + script without touching Rust or asking us questions'. That is the real acceptance for this ticket, and the third criterion above is how it stops being aspirational.

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: ALL THREE CRITERIA COMPLETE. docs/site/ (mdBook: book.toml, SUMMARY.md, 4 chapters), .github/workflows/docs.yml, .github/scripts/verify-doc-samples.mjs. CRITERION 3 DROVE THE DESIGN: the site contains NO COPIED SAMPLES. Every one is an {{#include}} of a file CI already builds — W9-04’s plugin examples, the profile retroforge-tool validates, anchored sections of the design docs. ONE COPY means drift is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE rather than merely detected, which is stronger than compiling a second copy and discovering later that the two disagree.

LINE RANGES WERE THE FIRST DESIGN AND THEY ARE WRONG: a range shifts silently when the source doc is edited. Writing the verifier caught exactly that in my own draft — plugins.md cited lines 243:255 of a 204-line file. Every include is now a NAMED ANCHOR (<!-- ANCHOR: name --> in the source docs), and a missing anchor is an ERROR because mdBook would otherwise emit the WHOLE FILE, which reads as a formatting slip rather than a broken reference. The verifier was NEGATIVE-TESTED, not just run green: it correctly rejects an inline `rust` block, a nonexistent anchor, and a chapter SUMMARY.md never links.

Also note the verifier lives at .github/scripts/ rather than scripts/ (this project’s conventional home for validators) purely because scripts/** is outside this write_scope; worth moving when a ticket owns both.

NOT DONE: no publishing step. docs.yml uploads the built book as an artifact; it does not deploy to Pages or anywhere else. That needs a repository settings decision (Pages source, custom domain) that is not a code change.

tickets.title: Second and third game profiles
acceptance: two further game profiles beyond the first, each exercising a decoder family the first does not
each ships with the evidence its claims rest on, to the standard docs/design/GAME_PROFILES.md sets
both load without warnings and are covered by the profile-corpus test
notes: The point is breadth of FORMAT coverage, not count: two profiles of the same shape prove less than one that forces a second decoder family into existence. Pick them for what they exercise.

HANDOFF (2026-08-20, unattended loop): NOT STARTED — criterion 1 is unbuildable inside write_scope. Criterion 1 asks for profiles 'each exercising a decoder family the first does not'. Decoder families are implemented in crates/rf-enhance/src/decode/ and EXACTLY ONE exists: metatile_screens (decode/mod.rs:38 is the only `pub mod`; metatile_screens.rs:165 returns UnknownFamily for anything else). GAME_PROFILES.md §2 names room_grid, tilemap_direct and custom, but none is implemented — profiles/snes/example-mode7 already declares kind = 'room_grid' and decodes nothing, which is the vacuous artifact this criterion must not produce more of. write_scope is profiles/** + crates/rf-profiles/**, so neither a new family nor a new fixture ROM (fixtures/**) can be added here. Criterion 2 ('ships with the evidence its claims rest on') compounds it: the only ROMs this repo can cite first-party evidence for are its own fixtures, and both are metatile scrollers — the same family. Criterion 3 IS satisfiable: crates/rf-profiles/tests/example_profiles.rs is the corpus test and already walks profiles/{nes,snes}. To unblock, one of: (a) widen write_scope to crates/rf-enhance/** + fixtures/** and accept that this ticket now implements a decoder family and the fixture that exercises it (probably better as its own ticket, e.g. 'implement room_grid + its fixture', with W9-08 depending on it); or (b) rule on whether profiles for real commercial titles belong in /profiles at all — that is a law-5 and clean-room-provenance question for Brad, and it decides whether criterion 2 can ever be met by anything but our own fixtures.

RULING (Brad, 2026-08-20, in response to the unattended loop’s four blocking questions). BOTH options taken. (a) write_scope is widened to crates/rf-enhance/** and fixtures/**: implement the `room_grid` decoder family — which profiles/snes/example-mode7 has declared since W4-02 while decoding nothing — and author the fixture that exercises it, so criterion 1’s "a decoder family the first does not" becomes satisfiable at all. (b) Profiles for real, documented commercial titles ARE permitted, citing published documentation (DataCrystal and similar). Law 5 still binds absolutely: NO ROM BYTES IN GIT, and no copyrighted title hardcoded in engine code — a profile is data under /profiles, never a name baked into a crate. Every claim still needs its FR-PROF-003 source citation, and clean-room-from-documentation (NFR-011) remains the standard: transcribed-from-disassembly is not acceptable provenance no matter how convenient.

HANDOFF 2026-08-21: ALL THREE CRITERIA COMPLETE, on Brad's ruling. Delivered: the room_grid decoder family (crates/rf-enhance/src/decode/room_grid.rs, 11 unit tests), RoomGridSpec in the schema AND shape.rs, two authored fixtures with PUBLISHED CONSTRUCTION RULES (fixtures/nes/rf-rooms, fixtures/snes/rf-rooms-flat), two profiles, and 4 end-to-end tests. room_grid is deliberately a DIFFERENT SHAPE from metatile_screens, not a second stream decoder: a 2-D grid of fixed-size rooms with an optional indirection table, so ONE ROOM CAN APPEAR IN MANY CELLS. That reuse is what metatile_screens cannot express at all, and it is how room games fit on a cartridge. The two profiles cover BOTH HALVES — indexed (reuse) and unindexed — with a test asserting they genuinely differ, because two profiles of the same shape would satisfy the criterion’s letter while proving one thing.

THE END-TO-END TEST IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, because criterion 3 alone would NOT have caught the rot this ticket exists to fix: profiles/snes/example-mode7 declared kind = "room_grid" from W4-02 until 2026-08-21 while configuring NOTHING, and it LOADED CLEANLY the whole time. Loading is not exercising. crates/rf-enhance/tests/room_grid_profiles.rs reads each profile from disk, resolves a Spec, and actually decodes its fixture bytes — bytes REBUILT from the published rule rather than read from a file, so a change to generate.md turns the test red instead of silently agreeing with it.

TWO HONESTY CALLS. (1) example-mode7’s [decode] section is REMOVED, not filled in: once room_grid existed the declaration stopped being inert and became a live falsehood (spec_from_profile would refuse it with MissingSpec), there is no Mode 7 fixture with room data behind it, and inventing offsets to satisfy the schema would be inventing facts. A test asserts the ABSENCE so a future edit cannot quietly re-add an unbacked declaration. (2) [[identity]] stays a PLACEHOLDER in both new profiles even though real hashes were computed and are recorded in comments: these fixtures are LEVEL DATA, not bootable ROMs, so putting a level image’s hash into a field meaning "the ROM this profile matches" would be a false claim wearing the costume of a precise one.

OUT OF SCOPE / follow-up. (1) GAME_PROFILES.md §2 still does not document the [decode.room_grid] table — docs/design/** is outside this write_scope, so RoomGridSpec’s doc comment and room_grid.rs’s module doc ARE the specification for now. Worth writing into §2. (2) NO COMMERCIAL-TITLE PROFILE was authored. Brad’s ruling permits them from published documentation, but every claim needs an FR-PROF-003 citation the loader enforces, and verifying real addresses against DataCrystal-class sources was not done here — shipping unverified addresses would be worse than shipping none. The permission stands unused. (3) NEITHER FIXTURE IS A RUNNABLE ROM: the family is a pure function of ROM bytes, so building a bootable image to test it would add a cc65 dependency to prove nothing extra. RF-Scroller/RF-Scroller-S remain the runnable fixtures.

the persistent bottom bar carries only what docs/design/FRONTEND_UI.md §3.2 specifies (mode badge · FPS · A/V sync · profile chip) plus transport; every other control moves to the Esc overlay or a View menu
the window size is one pub const that main.rs and the regression test both read, so the test cannot go stale when the size changes
crate::accessibility::Palette drives egui through ctx.set_visuals, and ui_scale drives the zoom factor — the module is currently orphaned and its WCAG tests prove nothing about what renders
the permanently disabled 'Switch mode (W4-05)' button is removed from the overlay menu or made live

acceptance: the Enhance workspace presents §3.3's three tabs — Compare, Features, Map — in an egui_dock DockArea whose tab type lives in the retroforge crate

rf-debugger's DebugTab does NOT gain Enhance/Author variants: that would put upper-layer concepts into a lower-layer crate and into PersistedLayout, which is versioned and already has files in users' config dirs
Compare's controls (off/split/blink, divider, both-buffer screenshot) move OUT of the bottom-bar Enhance menu and into the Compare tab; there is one route to them, not two
Map renders the stitched canvas with fog for unvisited cells (FR-ENH-004) and says plainly when nothing has been stitched yet, rather than showing a blank rectangle
nothing clips at app::WINDOW_SIZE (tests/hud_fits.rs), the new surface is covered by tests/renders.rs, and any non-ASCII it draws joins app::PROPORTIONAL_GLYPHS so tests/glyphs_render.rs checks it
what is NOT built is written into docs/design/FRONTEND_UI.md §3.3 with the reason, not left for the next reader to discover
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-25, before any code was written. The two notes this replaces were both wrong, and the error propagated into acceptance criterion 2, three W10-01/W10-03 commit messages and docs/STATUS.md.

WRONG #1: 'egui_dock is confined to debug_dock.rs by an explicit layer rule.' It is not. debug_dock.rs's own module doc says it is 'the one module in this crate (BESIDES crate::app) allowed to depend on egui_dock' — app.rs is explicitly permitted — and scripts/validate-arch.sh enforces nothing about egui_dock at all (it enforces core-crate imports, rf-core-api purity, direct core access, the determinism lint and the one-wgpu invariant). There was never a rule here to break.

WRONG #2: 'this is the ROOT CAUSE of W10-01's symptom.' It was when filed, and it no longer is. W10-01 moved every window toggle out of the bar into the View and Enhance menus, and W10-03 deleted the Library window outright. No HUD pressure remains for docking to relieve.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT is §2 conformance — 'Workspaces (dockable, per-game layout persisted): Debug / Enhance / Author' — a real but much weaker reason than defect repair, and it should be weighed as such rather than inherited from a dead root cause.

THE REAL CONSTRAINT, found by reading rather than assumed: rf_debugger::layout::DebugTab is a LOWER-layer type. Giving it Enhance/Author variants would make rf-debugger carry enhancement and authoring concepts, and would put non-debug tabs into PersistedLayout, which has a LAYOUT_FORMAT_VERSION and existing files in users' config dirs. A second dock host in app.rs with its own tab enum avoids all of that, at the cost of a second persisted layout.

SCOPE FINDING: enhance_window is 94 lines and implements only the FEATURES third of §3.3's [Compare][Features][Map]. Compare lives in a bottom-bar menu; Map does not exist as a tab (the ultrawide camera is a View-menu toggle). Docking what exists would dock one third of a specified workspace, so 'build §3.3's three tabs' is probably the more valuable ticket and 'dock it' the container question. Brad's call — he splits bundled tickets.

SCOPE, decided with Brad 2026-08-25: build §3.3's CONTENT (the three tabs), because that is where the user-visible value is — Compare is currently buried in a bottom-bar menu and Map does not exist as a surface at all. Docking is the container, not the point.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, and this is a data problem rather than a UI one: §3.3's 'live player marker' and 'original-viewport outline' need the canvas-space position of the CURRENT viewport, and that never reaches the UI thread — CoreEvent::CanvasSnapshot carries only rf_enhance::stitcher::Canvas, and UltrawideRender carries rgba/size/reduction. tickets.title: Every surface that can overflow can be scrolled, and says so
acceptance: every dock pane and window whose content can exceed its container is inside a ScrollArea; the audit is written down, naming the surfaces checked and the ones deliberately left alone
a surface deliberately without a ScrollArea says why in a comment (a fixed-size image or a fixed row count cannot overflow; unbounded prose or a growing list can)
there is a check that would catch a NEW unscrollable overflow, or a written statement of why no such check is practical — not silence
notes: Brad, looking at the rendered Enhance workspace 2026-08-25: 'I did not see in that image a scroll bar to scroll for things that need to scroll'. He was right twice over.

FIRST: crates/retroforge/src/enhance_dock.rs shipped in W10-02 with ZERO ScrollAreas, so all three §3.3 tabs clipped their content with no way to reach it — the profile inspector was cut off mid-list. Fixed in the same session; this ticket is the rest of the audit, not that fix.

SECOND, and the more interesting half: egui's DEFAULT scroll style is `floating` — a thin bar that fades in only on hover. A pane full of content it cannot show then looks identical to a pane whose content simply ends. app::apply_theme now sets ScrollStyle::solid() app-wide, so a scrollbar is a visible readout of how much you are not looking at, rather than a control you have to already suspect exists.

AUDIT SO FAR (measured, not guessed). debug_dock.rs: 6 of 11 pane functions contain a ScrollArea. The five that do not are pattern_ui and palette_ui (fixed-size images, cannot overflow), memory_rows_ui (called from memory_ui, which has one), event_timeline_ui (allocate_exact_size of row_height * TIMELINE_ROWS.len() — bounded vertically, but its WIDTH is computed and may exceed a narrow pane, so horizontal scroll is the open question), and audio_ui (unverified — per-channel scopes plus controls). app.rs windows are unaudited: settings_window, author_window, states_modal and layers_debug_window have not been checked.

WHY A TEST IS HARD, stated rather than hidden: an accessibility-tree walk cannot distinguish 'clipped and unreachable' from 'scrolled out of view but reachable' — egui reports laid-out rects for ScrollArea children even when scrolled off screen, so a probe on the Controls window reported 31 'clipped' nodes that were all perfectly reachable. tickets.title: The Map tab renders the canvas it says is missing
acceptance: with a stitched canvas in existence, §3.3's Map tab shows it — it does not depend on the View-menu camera toggle having been flipped first

the canvas-snapshot request is driven by whether the Map tab is VISIBLE, on the same 'closed panels cost nothing' principle debug_dock uses for SetEventMask, so an unopened Map tab still costs no per-frame clone
'nothing stitched yet' is shown only when the canvas is genuinely empty, and that case is distinguishable from 'the map is not being fed'
photographed in tests/capture_tour.rs with a canvas that exists, so the fix is visible rather than asserted
notes: FOUND BY THE SCREENSHOT TOUR, 2026-08-26, and by nothing else. tests/capture_tour.rs photographed the Enhance workspace at frame 308 of a live RF-Scroller session: the Map tab read 'Nothing stitched yet — play for a moment and the map fills in.' The canvas DID exist — the same tour's ultrawide shot at frame 1200 shows a fully stitched level.

CAUSE: EnhanceCtx::map_texture is app.rs's self.ultrawide_texture, and that is only populated while camera == CameraToggle::Ultrawide, because maybe_request_canvas_snapshot returns early otherwise. So the Map tab is inert unless the user has separately flipped View > Camera to Ultrawide, and nothing on the tab says so. A surface that is blank for a reason the user cannot see is the exact failure W10-02's own map_ui doc claims to avoid ('every empty case says WHICH empty case it is') — it enumerated three cases and missed this fourth one.

The honest fix is to make the Map tab a CONSUMER of the canvas in its own right rather than a passenger on the camera toggle: request snapshots when the tab is visible, throttled the same way, and keep the camera toggle for what it is (which view fills the play area).

COST NOTE, from W3-03a's precedent: snapshots are not free — CanvasAccumulator::current_canvas clones the whole stitched canvas, 'tens of MB/s for a level of any real size' — which is why the existing code throttles to one per CANVAS_SNAPSHOT_REFRESH_INTERVAL repaints. Driving it from tab visibility must keep that throttle, not drop it.

This is the headline of the RF-Scroller demo and one of the four differentiators in VISION §3. It being library-only is the single largest gap between what the docs claim and what a user can do.

SCOPE DISCOVERY 2026-08-26, before code. This is not 'wire up an existing feature' — THE PIXEL PRODUCER DOES NOT EXIST. `SceneLayer::DecodedLevel` has no renderer anywhere: scene_graph.rs's own module doc says no producer exists for it, `enhanced_view::compose_ultrawide` carries an `unreachable!` for any layer that is not `StitchedCanvas`, and the only thing in the repo that renders a decoded level is `authoring::preview_text`, which draws ASCII. level_view_demo.rs asserts on the SceneGraph's SHAPE and never produces a pixel, which is why this looked finished.

TRACTABLE, though. `DecodedLevel` carries `metatiles` (column-major ids) plus `metatile_tiles` (CHR tile ids per metatile), and `rf_debugger::pattern` already has `decode_tile` and `tile_to_rgba`. The producer belongs in `crate::enhanced_view` — ARCHITECTURE §3 names it the SceneGraph -> CompositeLayer mediator, handle resolution is explicitly OUTSIDE rf-enhance, and retroforge is a layer that may depend on rf-debugger (rf-enhance may not).

THE DATA PROBLEM, and the design chosen for it. `LevelSession::scene` needs a `&dyn Fn(u32) -> u8` CPU peek and the entity-table bytes, and only the core thread can produce those without touching core state. But rendering needs the GPU, which is the UI thread's. Resolution: the profile declares WHICH addresses matter, so the app computes that address list once and asks the core for exactly those values per frame — a bounded probe rather than shipping RAM. Keeps the peek on the core thread, the composite on the UI thread, and costs nothing while the feature is off.

Both live in rf-snes. W11-13 delivered the width; this delivers the mask, the core's use of it, and the path to the user. THE PATH THAT DID NOT EXIST: Enhance toggle -> EnhanceActions::widescreen_set -> RetroForgeApp::set_widescreen (reads the matched profile's [widescreen] policies) -> CoreCommand::SetWidescreen(WidescreenRequest) -> core thread decides PER FRAME against live layer geometry -> EmuStepper::set_widescreen -> SnesCore -> Ppu::render_scanline_masked. Before this, the 'widescreen_decoded' checkbox set a field that round-tripped to disk and changed nothing anyone could see, and WidescreenPolicies was referenced by nothing in crates/retroforge/src. DECIDED EVERY FRAME, not once at toggle time: the `auto` policy asks where a layer is scrolled to, and that changes as the player moves. Deciding once would freeze a HUD's verdict onto a scrolling layer or the reverse. REFUSALS ARE SURFACED (criterion 2). A layer the policy declines keeps its 4:3 width — Ppu::WidenMask carries the decision INTO the renderer, so a declined layer is simply absent from the margins rather than smeared or repeated — and its reason is sent back as CoreEvent::WidescreenDecisions and printed under the toggle that caused it. bsnes-hd's lesson is that widening the wrong layer looks like a bug in the GAME; a user not told why just sees a narrower picture than they asked for. OFF IS OFF (law 6): width <= WIDTH means SnesCore never reaches the widening path at all, and the test asserts the frame returns to 256 when the toggle is cleared — not merely that it stops growing. PART (b): profiles/snes/rf-scroller-s/profile.toml, the FIRST profile any bootable SNES ROM has had. Legitimate in-repo work — our own fixture, built from source in-tree with published rules, so every policy is checkable rather than believed. Explicitly not W11-06's commercial titles. It asserts the app's frame goes 256 -> 400 -> 256 and that at least one layer comes back refused WITH a reason. All four SNES golden suites unchanged including the #[ignore]d ones. workspace 1703 passing; ten-command gate + docs-gate green.

An HD pack replaces each 8x8 tile with a `HdPack::scale`-times version, so the composited frame is scale times larger than 256x240 — and `rf_renderer::FrameBuffer` is hardcoded to exactly 256x240. The pack machinery is complete (parse_hires, write_hires, lookup by tile+palette, PackBuilder, and mesen_hdpack_real.rs against a real pack); what is missing is a frame big enough to draw the result into.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-27 — the recorded blocker is gone and the status was simply stale. This ticket was blocked on 'rf_renderer::FrameBuffer is hardcoded to exactly 256x240', so an HD pack's scale-times-larger composite had nowhere to be drawn. W11-08 added FrameBuffer::with_size, and W11-03 proved it live by resizing the buffer when decoded widescreen turns on. Both dependencies (W11-03, W11-08) are done. The pack machinery was already complete — parse_hires, write_hires, lookup by tile+palette, PackBuilder, and mesen_hdpack_real.rs against a real pack — so what is left is the same shape W11-03 turned out to be: a path from a UI action to the running core, plus the honesty half (provenance and refused tiles reported, not silently skipped).

HANDOFF — WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-27 to include crates/rf-nes/**, per plan.json's rule that widening needs a note here. WHAT FOR, and it is deliberately the SMALL version: two READ-ONLY accessors, `Ppu::chr()` and the scroll state, mirroring the existing `vram()`/`palette()`/`oam()` borrows exactly — the same 'a borrow cannot have a side effect, so the guarantee is structural' property those three already document. WHY ANY CORE CHANGE AT ALL: an HD pack rule is keyed on TileData + palette. The app ALREADY receives nametable VRAM, palette RAM and OAM every frame (W4-06d), and for a CHR-ROM game the tile index IS the nametable byte — so most of tile identity is already in hand. What is missing is CHR (for CHR-RAM games, where TileData is the tile's BYTES) and the scroll position (to map a screen cell to a nametable cell). WHY NOT THE BIGGER DESIGN: the obvious alternative is a per-tile observation stream out of the PPU, which is what `hdpack::TileObservation` was shaped for. That would be real core surgery in a dot-accurate renderer and would have to cost nothing when packs are off. Two borrows the app reads when it needs them is smaller, cheaper and cannot perturb anything — including A12 edge timing, which is exactly why `Ppu::vram`'s doc calls non-observing the load-bearing property.

STAGE 1 OF 2 DONE 2026-08-27 — the NES PPU reports the tiles it drew, and that was the enabling half. `Ppu::set_tile_capture` / `Ppu::drawn_tiles` yield a Vec<DrawnTile> {x: i16, y: u16, tile: u8, base: u16, palette: u8} per frame, recorded at reload_shift_registers — the one place the tile index and its attribute bits exist together with the scroll state that positions them. Plus Ppu::chr()/chr_is_ram() as non-observing borrows for CHR-RAM packs. Pay-for-use, not serialised, three tests. THE DESIGN DECISION, so it is not revisited cheaply: the obvious route is a frame-end scroll snapshot, which needs NO core change because the app already gets nametable VRAM and palette RAM every frame and a CHR-ROM tile index IS the nametable byte. It is WRONG for any game that changes scroll mid-frame — nearly every status bar — and shipping it would be W9-08's vacuous artifact. Do not 'simplify' back to it. POSITIONING, already solved and easy to get wrong again: a reloaded tile enters the LOW byte of a 16-bit shifter whose HIGH bits feed output, so it appears at pixel dot+7, not dot-1. Dots 329/337 prefetch the NEXT scanline's pixels 0 and 8. Fine X shifts left and the first tile is reported at a NEGATIVE x rather than clipped, because a pack must draw its partly-visible left column. A test asserts the tile INDEX at two rows, which is the only thing that catches a whole-tile offset on a repeating background. STAGE 2, WHAT IS LEFT: (a) plumb drawn_tiles + chr to the app, pay-for-use like the level probe — off unless a pack is loaded, since a Vec of ~7680 tiles per frame is not something to clone unconditionally; (b) import a pack in the app: parse_hires is done, but the PNGs need decoding and retroforge already has `image = 0.25` for it — hdpack deliberately decodes no pixels and takes ImageInfo dimensions from the caller; (c) composite: output is 256*scale x 240*scale, each DrawnTile either blits its replacement or upscales the original cell; (d) the honesty half, criterion 2 — Import::summary() and Import::unsatisfied() already exist and must reach the UI, not a log; (e) the end-to-end test through RetroForgeApp. NOTE ON SPRITES: this stage reports BACKGROUND tiles only. Mesen packs also replace sprite tiles, and sprites.rs has the tile index at fetch time in the same shape. Whether stage 2 covers sprites or declares the limit is a decision that should be MADE rather than discovered — a pack whose sprites silently do not apply is the half-applied confusion Import::summary exists to prevent.

DONE 2026-08-27. A Mesen HD pack reaches the running game end to end: RetroForgeApp::load_hd_pack reads a pack directory (hires.txt beside its PNGs), decodes the images, imports it, and turns on tile capture; the core thread ships this frame's placements; the app composites at the pack's scale and draws the result. THE BUG THE END-TO-END TEST CAUGHT, and it is the reason a unit test could not have: the capture window and the frame boundary did not line up. A frame's visible tiles finish at scanline 239, but this crate's only frame-boundary signal is the pre-render line wrapping to scanline 0 — twenty-two scanlines later, by which time the NEXT frame's prefetch has been recorded. A single buffer therefore handed the reader 2 or 3 tiles of the coming frame instead of the 7680 of the finished one. Fixed with a published buffer, the same settled-frame model the rest of the system uses: completed_tiles is swapped in when the pre-render line begins. Every piece was individually correct; nothing assembled them, which is this ticket's own diagnosis turned on itself. A SECOND ONE the test caught: rf-scroller, like real NES software, waits several vblanks before enabling rendering — it draws its first tile around frame 57. A test loading the pack at frame 30 finds nothing to replace and blames the plumbing. THE HONESTY HALF (criterion 2) is three separate facts in the Enhance panel, because conflating them hides the one that matters: what the pack CLAIMS (Import::summary), what could not be honoured (Import::unsatisfied — missing images, unevaluable conditions, unsupported directives), and what the last frame actually REPLACED (CompositeReport::summary). A pack can import cleanly and replace nothing, which looks identical to a broken feature without the third line. SPRITES ARE NOT COVERED, and the panel says so rather than leaving it to be discovered. Filed as W11-14 with the measurement of why it is its own ticket: sprite fetches are per-scanline so an 8-pixel sprite yields eight observations of one tile, 8x16 spans two tiles chosen from OAM byte 1, and vertical flip inverts the row — its own positioning problem, plus a sprite-priority decision the compositor does not model. NEW RUNTIME DEPENDENCY: `image` 0.25, png feature only, promoted from dev-only with a TECH_STACK section-2 record. rf_enhance::hdpack decodes no pixels by design, so the decoder lives in the one crate that already owns image I/O. cargo deny check licenses was run before and after and reports the same single pre-existing rejection (libfuzzer-sys, NCSA), so this adds no licence surface. EVIDENCE: crates/retroforge/tests/hdpack_reaches_the_app.rs drives RetroForgeApp with a real pack it writes itself, and asserts the frame grows to 512x480, that tiles were actually REPLACED rather than merely upscaled, that the pack's colour is visible in the drawn pixels, and that unloading returns to 256x240. Five compositor tests and three PPU capture tests, the load-bearing one asserting tile INDEX at two rows. workspace 1712 passing; ten-command gate green.

VISION §5's 18-month criterion is '>=10 curated game profiles'. There are FIVE: nes/rf-rooms, nes/rf-scroller, nes/rf-scroller-demo, snes/example-mode7, snes/rf-rooms-flat — and every one is against our own fixtures.

Brad ruled 2026-08-20 that profiles for real, documented commercial titles ARE permitted, citing published documentation (DataCrystal and similar). THE PERMISSION HAS NEVER BEEN USED. W9-08's handoff records why: verifying real addresses against DataCrystal-class sources was not done, and shipping unverified addresses would be worse than shipping none.
Sequenced after W11-02 deliberately: a profile whose decoded level cannot be SEEN in the app is a profile nobody can check by looking. Authoring ten of those would multiply unverifiable content.

BLOCKED 2026-08-26, and the reason is evidence rather than effort. Reaching ten profiles means five more, and the acceptance forbids 'ten of the same shape' — so they must be commercial titles, which Brad's 2026-08-20 ruling permits from published documentation. PERMITTED IS NOT VERIFIABLE. A profile's value is its decode offsets and camera addresses, and there is no way to check those without running the ROM they describe. Law 5 forbids ROM bytes in git and we hold none, so every claim in such a profile would ship untested. W9-08 refused exactly this and called the result a vacuous artifact: profiles/snes/example-mode7 declared `kind = "room_grid"` from W4-02 until 2026-08-21 while configuring NOTHING, and LOADED CLEANLY the whole time. Authoring five of those would multiply the problem by five and move a number in VISION §5.

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT, so this is a decision rather than a dead end: (a) a lawfully-obtained commercial ROM present on the developer's machine but never committed, with the profile's offsets verified against it locally and the ROM excluded by .gitignore as `roms/` already is; or (b) a ruling that a profile citing published documentation may ship with its offsets marked UNVERIFIED and a loader that says so in the UI — which is honest, but means the profile chip would start meaning 'someone wrote this down' rather than 'this was checked'; or (c) more in-repo fixtures exercising genuinely different decoder families, which is breadth but not the commercial coverage VISION §5's number is a proxy for.

A SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND WHILE INVESTIGATING, and it blocks path (a) too. `rf_profiles::schema::IdentityEntry` carries FOUR hash families (sha256, sha1, md5, crc32) and `IdentityEntry::matches` checks every family the entry specifies. `crate::level_view::find_matching_profile` — the ONLY matcher the app uses — ignores three of them: it compares `i.sha256.as_deref() == Some(normalized_sha256)` and nothing else. A profile authored from a published No-Intro CRC32, which is the realistic way to identify a commercial title one does not hold, would load fine and never match anything. The schema and the matcher have diverged, and the schema's own `matches` method is dead code as far as the app is concerned.

CORRECTION 2026-08-27: the matcher defect recorded in the note above IS FIXED, and was fixed by W11-09 (done) before this note was ever acted on. `find_matching_profile` now calls `rf_profiles::schema::IdentityEntry::matches`, which checks every hash family an entry declares, so a profile identified by a published No-Intro CRC32 matches. That half of this ticket's blocker is gone. WHAT REMAINS IS THE EVIDENCE PROBLEM, unchanged and still Brad's: reaching ten profiles means five commercial titles, his 2026-08-20 ruling permits authoring them from published documentation, and PERMITTED IS NOT VERIFIABLE — law 5 means we hold no ROM to check a decode offset against, so every claim would ship untested. W9-08 refused exactly this and called the result a vacuous artifact. THREE HONEST SHAPES: (a) accept unverified profiles and say so in each file's `sources`; (b) amend VISION §5's ten to the number that can be verified, which today means profiles for our own fixtures — rf-scroller-s now has one (W11-03), so the verifiable count is real and small; (c) leave parked until a verification route exists. My recommendation is (b): a number that means something beats a number that is met. ALSO OPEN, raised by W11-09 and never settled: whether a published RAW hash should match as well as a normalized one. No-Intro publishes hashes of the file as distributed, which for NES is often the headered one, so matching raw would make published hashes directly usable — at the cost of more than one identity per game. That trade should be decided deliberately, not by accident, and it bears directly on (a).

The NES path must come out byte-identical, and the 10k-frame determinism double-run plus the blargg/nestest goldens are what can actually show that. They are `#[ignore]`d and run from scripts/local-gate.sh, so closing this ticket means running the local gate, not just `cargo test`.

CLOSED 2026-08-26. Evidence, stated precisely rather than as 'the gate is green': (1) `alter_ego_five_minute_replay_final_hash_and_golden_frames` — FIVE EMULATED MINUTES through the modified FrameBuffer, checked against a final state hash AND golden frames, passing in release; (2) the 10k-frame determinism double-run, release, both halves; (3) rf-renderer's pre-existing exact-pixel tests (`video_scanline_writes_resolved_rgb_into_the_right_row` and the overlay pair), which assert byte offsets and values and pass unchanged; (4) workspace 1673 passing.

tickets.title: The profile matcher uses every hash family the schema declares
acceptance: a profile identified by crc32, md5 or sha1 alone matches its ROM in the app, not only one identified by normalized sha256
matching goes through rf_profiles::schema::IdentityEntry::matches rather than a second hand-written comparison, so the schema has one matcher and not two
a test loads a profile per hash family and asserts each matches, and that a wrong hash does not — the negative half matters, since a matcher that returned true always would pass the positive half
notes: FOUND 2026-08-26 while investigating whether W11-06's commercial profiles are authorable. `IdentityEntry` carries sha256, sha1, md5 AND crc32, and `IdentityEntry::matches` correctly checks every family an entry specifies. `crate::level_view::find_matching_profile` — the only matcher the app calls — compares `i.sha256.as_deref() == Some(normalized_sha256)` and ignores the other three.

SO THE SCHEMA'S OWN MATCHER IS DEAD CODE as far as the product is concerned, and a profile authored from a published No-Intro CRC32 loads cleanly and never matches anything. That is the realistic way to identify a commercial title nobody in this project holds a copy of, so the gap is not academic.

The fix needs `rf_cart::RomIdentity` rather than a bare `&str` at the call site: the app currently threads `current_game_hash: Option<String>`, which is the normalized sha256 and cannot express the other families. `RomIdentity` already carries normalized AND raw hashes for all four.

WORTH DECIDING WHILE HERE: whether a published RAW hash should match too. `RomIdentity::raw` is documented 'diagnostics only' and normalization exists so a headered and a headerless dump of the same game share an identity — but No-Intro publishes hashes of the file as distributed, which for NES is often the headered one. Matching raw as well would make published hashes usable directly; matching only normalized keeps one identity per game. This is a real trade and should be recorded, not settled by accident.

tickets.title: rf-nes implements EmulatorCore, and the shell drives it through the trait
acceptance: rf_nes implements rf_core_api::EmulatorCore — load, reset, run_frame, step, save_state, load_state, state_view, config

the NES path is byte-identical afterwards, proven the way W11-08 was: the five-minute alter_ego replay against its final hash AND golden frames, plus the 10k-frame determinism double-run, both in release

The alternative — branching `core_thread` on cartridge type and duplicating ~20 methods of behaviour — is how one shell ends up with two half-consoles: every future feature gets written twice or forgotten once. Write scope widened to include the core crates, which W11-07 as originally filed excluded, making it unbuildable as written.

FIRST OF THREE, and deliberately the NES one: it is the console the shell already works with, so this is a refactor with a known-good output to check against rather than a new console AND a new abstraction at once. RISK is the same shape as W11-08's and should be treated the same way: this is the path every frame flows through, so `cargo test` is not sufficient evidence and the ignored release suites are.

CLOSED 2026-08-27. rf_nes::core::NesCore implements all eight EmulatorCore methods plus the `peek` this ticket added, and EmuStepper holds a NesCore rather than a raw (bus, cpu) pair — all four emulation loops go through the trait.

TWO REAL REGRESSIONS, both caught by tests that already existed, both invisible without them. (1) THE CYCLE BUDGET SILENTLY GREW ~12x: the original is `4 * 29_781`, four frames of CPU cycles; the first version here wrote `4 * 341 * 262 * 4`, four frames of DOTS. A jammed core would have spun twelve times longer before reporting. (2) `Step::Scanline` STOPPED AT A FRAME BOUNDARY: a scanline step stops when a scanline is DRAINED, and the first frame after power-on ends before any visible scanline exists, so a fresh stepper returned zero for a step that had simply not got there yet. retroforge::stepper looped on `scanlines > 0` alone since W1-06.

AND A PROCESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING: the first attempt at fixing (2) SILENTLY DID NOTHING — cargo fmt had reflowed the struct literal so the search pattern missed, and the edit no-oped. It was caught only because a probe still printed rows=0. Every scripted edit in this repo should assert its replacement count; this one did not.

TRAIT ADDITION: `EmulatorCore::peek(addr) -> u8`. StateView lends raw memories, which is right for walking a region, but cannot answer 'what does the CPU see at $6000?' — that goes through the mapper, and mapping is what a bus does. Three shipped features need exactly that: the debugger's memory viewer, W11-02's level probe, W11-04's script window. Both test mocks got honest implementations consistent with their own state_view, not unimplemented!().

DELIBERATELY NOT BOXED. EmuStepper holds a concrete NesCore, not Box<dyn EmulatorCore>, because three things still have no trait expression: typed CPU registers (StateView::cpu_regs is an untyped &[u8] with no agreed encoding), an out-of-band bus WRITE for the debugger's memory editor, and APU access for channel capture. Boxing before those close would mean bypassing the trait through a downcast, which is worse than holding the concrete type honestly. W11-12 closes them, when there are two cores to be generic over.

EVIDENCE, to the W11-08 standard because this is the path every frame flows through: alter_ego_five_minute_replay_final_hash_and_golden_frames (five emulated minutes, final state hash AND golden frames, release) and the 10k-frame determinism double-run (release, both halves), plus workspace 1680 passing / 32 ignored, clippy -D warnings, validate-arch.

tickets.title: rf-snes implements EmulatorCore
acceptance: rf_snes implements rf_core_api::EmulatorCore over SnesSystem

notes: BRAD'S RULING 2026-08-26: adopt `EmulatorCore` in both cores rather than adding a second bespoke SNES path, and split the work three ways. The alternative — branching `core_thread` on cartridge type and duplicating ~20 methods of behaviour — is how one shell ends up with two half-consoles: every future feature gets written twice or forgotten once. Write scope widened to include the core crates, which W11-07 as originally filed excluded, making it unbuildable as written.

SECOND OF THREE. `rf_snes::SnesSystem` exposes load / step / run_until / render_frame / palette_rgb — no `CoreSink` anywhere in the crate. The frame shape is the real work: `render_frame(max_instructions) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, u8>` returns rows AFTER the fact, whereas `CoreSink::video_scanline` is called DURING the frame, which is what lets layer extraction, the compare path and the debugger see a frame as it is produced.
W11-08 already removed the other half of this: the display path can carry 256x224 and 512-wide hires frames now.

CLOSED 2026-08-27. rf_snes::core::SnesCore implements EmulatorCore, driven by a test with the real rf-scroller-s fixture that asserts on PIXELS — every prior SNES proof (65816/SPC700 vectors, gilyon cputest, PeterLemon goldens, Mode 7, colour math) ran through rf-harness and never through the trait the shell speaks.

THE SHAPE DIFFERENCE, which is the actual reason one shell could not drive both consoles. rf-nes PUSHES: the PPU queues completed scanlines as the CPU runs and drain_video hands them to a CoreSink MID-FRAME, which is what lets layer extraction, the compare view and the debugger watch a frame being built. rf-snes PULLS: SnesSystem::render_frame runs to a settled vblank and THEN asks Ppu::render_scanline for each visible line — deliberate since W7-06, because mid-frame register writes are normal on this machine and composing as you go would compose half-written state. The adapter runs the frame, then replays the settled picture into the sink line by line.

WHAT A SINK THEREFORE DOES NOT GET is the TIMING of those lines. For a settled-composition renderer that information does not exist to report, and it is written into the module doc rather than left for a future mid-frame-effects feature to discover.

Overlay rides alongside: `Scanline` carries `overlay` with `pixels`, and forwarding only the pixels would make the 32-per-line sprite suppression invisible to the feature built to show it. The test asserts one overlay row per video row.

peek ANSWERS FOR MEMORY AND REFUSES REGISTERS. A SNES register read can latch — $2139 advances the VRAM read address — so peek resolves through mapping::map and answers for Rom/Wram/Sram, reporting quiescent 0 for Register/Open. Routing a debugger viewer through the CPU read path would make it a participant in the simulation, which ARCHITECTURE §2 forbids: a viewer that changes what it observes is worse than one with blanks in it.

Frames are asserted at 224 OR 239 lines, not a fixed number: SETINI's overscan bit decides, and a core that always emitted 224 would silently crop an overscan game's bottom fifteen rows (W7-06). W11-08 is what made either representable — the display path was hardcoded to 256x240 until then.

tickets.title: The SNES PPU renders a caller-specified width
acceptance: Ppu::render_scanline accepts a width and composes that many dots, fetching the extra tilemap columns rather than stretching
the accuracy path is unchanged at 256: a default-width render is byte-identical to today's output, proven by the existing goldens
a test renders a wider-than-256 scanline and asserts the extra columns carry real tilemap content, not backdrop
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W11-03 ON BRAD'S RULING, 2026-08-27. W11-03's own notes had already decomposed the work into (a) a variable-width PPU, (b) a profile for the rf-scroller-s fixture, and (c) the app wiring — and identified (a) as 'the expensive half [that] belongs in rf-snes'. W11-03's write_scope covers crates/retroforge/** and crates/rf-enhance/** but NOT crates/rf-snes/**, so it could not legally do (a) at all. Filing it here keeps that write_scope honest instead of widening a 5-point ticket to cover a PPU refactor.

MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED, 2026-08-27. rf_snes::ppu::WIDTH is a `pub const WIDTH: usize = 256` and it is baked into FIXED-SIZE ARRAY TYPES across the whole PPU, not merely used as a loop bound: bg.rs has `pixels: [Option<u8>; WIDTH]` and `priority: [u8; WIDTH]`; obj.rs has `pixels: [Option<(u8, u8)>; WIDTH]`, `priority: [u8; WIDTH]` and `dropped: [Option<u8>; WIDTH]`; mod.rs allocates `vec![backdrop; WIDTH]` and iterates `0..WIDTH`; mode7.rs derives its sample count from it. Making width a runtime value means changing those array types (to Vec, or to const generics) and every construction site. That is why this is 8 points and not a parameter addition.

WHAT W11-08 DID AND DID NOT DO. W11-08 made a wider FRAME representable in the display path — rf_renderer::FrameBuffer is no longer hardcoded to NES dimensions. It did nothing about a PPU that only ever composes 256 dots. W11-03's notes record this correction explicitly ('W11-08 did not unblock it the way it appeared to'); do not re-read the earlier note and conclude otherwise.

THE TECHNIQUE is bsnes-hd's: fetch tilemap columns beyond the visible window so the widened area carries real scenery rather than a stretch or a mirror. That is also why the honesty contract matters — some layers cannot be widened correctly (a status bar, a fixed HUD, a Mode 7 floor), and rf_enhance::widescreen already models that as a per-BG policy with refusals. This ticket only has to make the WIDTH available; deciding which layers get it is W11-03's job and its engine already exists (441 lines, 8 tests, BgPolicy/LayerView/decide).

ACCURACY MODE IS THE REFERENCE (law 6). Widening is an opt-in overlay; the 256-dot path must stay byte-identical. The PeterLemon goldens and the region suites are the proof of that and must be run unchanged, not re-baselined.

AFTER THIS, W11-03 STILL NEEDS A PROFILE. widescreen::WidescreenPolicies::from_profile reads a profile's per-BG policy names, and the only SNES profile declaring any is profiles/snes/example-mode7, whose [[identity]] is all zeros and matches nothing. The one bootable SNES fixture, rf-scroller-s, has no profile. That is W11-03's part (b) and is legitimate in-repo work — our own fixture with published build rules, unlike W11-06's commercial titles whose offsets cannot be verified.

DONE 2026-08-27. Ppu::render_scanline_at(y, width) composes a caller-specified width by FETCHING the extra tilemap columns; Ppu::render_scanline(y) is now a wrapper over it at WIDTH. THE MODEL: output column x is 256-space column x - (width - 256)/2, so the extra columns sit EITHER SIDE of the picture hardware would draw. That is bsnes-hd's technique, and it works here because tilemap addressing is modular — `sx as u16` truncates a negative column to the top of the 16-bit range, which is exactly the wrap wanted, so the left margin shows the scenery genuinely to the left rather than a mirror or a stretch. Sprites keep their 256-space X and shift by the same pad, so a sprite in the middle stays in the middle; a sprite hardware would clip at the edge becomes visible, which is the honest consequence of showing more world and exactly what a per-BG policy may decline. Mode 7 needed no special handling — it is a projection, so extending the screen-x range simply projects more of the same plane. WHY A SECOND ENTRY POINT RATHER THAN CHANGING render_scanline's SIGNATURE, which is what this ticket's acceptance literally asked for: it makes criterion 2 STRUCTURAL instead of merely tested. Every accuracy caller goes through render_scanline, the pad is zero there, and every derived index reduces to the old expression — so 'byte-identical at 256' is a property of the code shape, not a claim resting on whether the right goldens were run. It also avoided touching ~20 call sites in tests that have nothing to do with widening. Same capability, less risk, stronger guarantee. MAX_WIDTH = 512, a fixed cap rather than heap buffers: the per-scanline layer arrays are hot (four backgrounds plus objects, 224 times a frame), and 512 covers both users — true-hires modes 5/6 sample 512 columns, and 16:9 at this height wants 398 (426 at 240 rows). Over-wide requests are CLAMPED, not truncated, and there is a test for it. HIRES + WIDESCREEN IS DECLINED, not half-done: a true-hires line ignores the width and composes at 256 before its own widening to 512. Combining the two is not modelled, and quietly doing part of it would be worse than saying so. EVIDENCE: all four SNES golden suites green unchanged — PeterLemon, undisbeliever, region and mirror-map, INCLUDING the #[ignore]d ones, which is the gate a plain `cargo test --workspace` does not cover. Four new tests: the centre is unmoved when widened, render_scanline_at(256) equals render_scanline, the margins are Background(0) rather than Backdrop (the only assertion that distinguishes fetching from stretching), and over-wide clamps. workspace: 1702 passing. W11-03 IS NOW UNBLOCKED for its part (a). It still needs part (b), a profile for the rf-scroller-s fixture, and note that profiles/ is outside W11-03's write_scope — raise that when claiming it.

tickets.title: HD packs replace sprite art too, not only background tiles
acceptance: the PPU reports the sprite tiles it drew, with their screen position, palette and flip
a pack rule matching a sprite tile replaces it in the running game
the Enhance panel's 'background tiles only' limitation notice is removed, because it is no longer true
notes: FILED 2026-08-27 as a DECLARED limit rather than a discovered one. W11-05 delivered background tile replacement end to end and states in the Enhance panel that sprite art will not appear. Mesen packs do replace sprite tiles, so a pack whose sprites silently did nothing would be exactly the half-applied confusion hdpack::Import::summary exists to prevent — hence saying so in the UI and filing this, rather than leaving a silent gap.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN W11-05, measured rather than guessed: sprite fetches are PER SCANLINE, not per tile. `sprites.rs`'s `run_sprite_fetch_dot` phase 7 has the bank, tile index, attribute and x for a sprite on the scanline it is being fetched FOR — so an 8-pixel-tall sprite yields eight observations of the same tile and something must collapse them to one placement at the sprite's top row. On top of that 8x16 mode spans two tiles selected from OAM byte 1 itself, and vertical flip inverts which row is which. That is its own positioning problem with its own tests, comparable in size to the background one W11-05 solved.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE: `rf_enhance::hd_render::composite` takes a flat list of `Placement`s and does not care what produced them, so sprites need no new compositing. `Ppu::set_tile_capture` already gates the whole facility pay-for-use. `EmuStepper::hd_placements` is where a sprite's TileData and palette bytes would be built, next to the background path — note sprite palettes are $3F10-relative, not $3F00.

A DECISION THIS TICKET MUST MAKE, not inherit: sprites are drawn OVER the background with priority and transparency, so a replaced sprite tile has to composite with alpha against whatever is under it. `blit` already skips fully transparent source pixels, which is most of the way there, but sprite-behind-background priority is not modelled in the composite at all and would need to be.

DONE 2026-08-27. HD packs replace sprite art, and the Enhance panel's 'background tiles only' notice is gone because it is no longer true. THE PER-SCANLINE PROBLEM, solved the way the note predicted: sprite pattern fetches happen on every scanline a sprite covers, so a naive capture records an 8-pixel sprite EIGHT times, each copy claiming a different row — a pack would draw its replacement eight times down the screen. Ppu::capture_sprite records once, at the fetch for the sprite's top row (evaluation runs a scanline ahead, so that is `scanline == y`), and a test asserts exactly one placement per sprite. 8x16 emits TWO placements because a pack replaces 8x8 art, with the bank taken from OAM byte 1's own bit 0 rather than PPUCTRL, and vertical flip swapping which half is on top. Flips are reported so the replacement can be mirrored — otherwise a character faces the wrong way. Sprites draw at OAM y + 1, which is pinned by a test because it is the classic off-by-one that puts a whole sprite layer one row high. THE PRIORITY DECISION THIS TICKET HAD TO MAKE, and it turned out not to need priority modelling at all: a replacement may only paint pixels where the ORIGINAL frame shows the same layer. The PPU already resolved priority when it drew the frame, and FrameBundle already carries PpuPixel::layer per pixel, so masking against it is free and exactly right — a sprite behind the background is masked out, and so is a background tile with a sprite standing in front of it. THAT SECOND HALF WAS A BUG IN W11-05, found while doing this: background replacements were painting over sprites. Nothing caught it because the fixture's replaced tiles happened not to overlap a sprite. A test now pins both directions. ALSO: a rule whose every pixel is masked away is reported as UNMATCHED, not replaced — counting it would overstate what the pack achieved. FrameMsg's two HD fields became one boxed HdFrame. Not tidying: clippy's large_enum_variant fired because CoreEvent travels through a channel every frame, so two inline vectors would grow it for every session whether a pack is loaded or not. EVIDENCE: 7 PPU capture tests (4 new, covering once-per-sprite, 8x16 as two tiles, vertical-flip swap, and horizontal flip reporting), 8 compositor tests (3 new, covering the layer mask in both directions, the fully-masked rule, and mirrored art), and the existing end-to-end app test still green with masking applied. workspace 1723 passing; ten-command gate green; NES and SNES suites unchanged.

It is little-endian, the order $2122 writes them in, so a viewer reading a pair back sees what the ROM wrote. ppu_regs: the SNES PPU is DECODED into typed fields, not a raw register array, so the file is rebuilt from the live fields rather than shadowed at write time — a shadow updated inside write_register would be a second copy that can silently disagree with what the renderer reads, which is the exact failure SnesBus's own doc warns about for VRAM. cpu_regs IS EMPTY BY DECISION and a test ASSERTS the emptiness, so filling it later is a deliberate change rather than something that quietly happens. It is W13-02i's (Brad's ruling 2026-09-04, D-6).

THE DECODERS LIVE IN rf-snes, NOT rf-debugger, AND THAT WAS THE REAL DESIGN QUESTION. rf-debugger may not depend on a core (validate-arch rule 3), and its NES decoders get away with it because NES CHR is JUST BYTES — two bitplanes eight bytes apart, no register state. SNES tile data is not: a pixel's value depends on the layer's bit depth (2/4/8, chosen by the BG mode) and the bitplane pairs are interleaved at +0/+8/+16/+24 words. bg::fetch_pixel's own doc calls that 'the mistake that makes graphics come out with the right shapes in scrambled colours'. Reimplementing it in rf-debugger would have been a second copy of this crate's most easily mis-transcribed knowledge, free to drift from the renderer that draws the game. EVERYTHING IN rf_snes::debug TAKES BYTE SLICES, NOT &Ppu, and that is what makes it usable at all: the debugger reads a SNAPSHOT that travelled to the UI thread on a frame message (law 4), never a live core.

CoreCommand::SetSnesDebugCapture is the switch, driven by whether a SNES-capable tab is docked AND the window is open — the same trade SetLayerExtraction already makes for its two 240 KB buffers (DEBUGGER.md section 6).

Criterion 3 asked for the same DebugTab to serve both consoles and this is how — a user does not learn two panel layouts. Opening a NES ROM after a SNES one clears the field, so the previous game's memories cannot be drawn against the new one; a test asserts that direction specifically.

DETAILS THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG IF GUESSED, each pinned by a unit test: tilemap quadrants are NOT contiguous (a 64-wide map puts its right half at +0x400 and a 64x64 map's bottom-left at +0x800, so a viewer ignoring it shows the same quadrant four times); CGRAM is BGR555 with BLUE in the high bits and scales by *255/31 so full scale is 255 and not 248; OAM's high table supplies X's ninth bit and the size select two bits per sprite, four sprites to a byte, and X is a SIGNED 9-bit value so 0x110 means -240 — a decoder stopping at 512 bytes would put every sprite past x=255 on the wrong side of the screen; and palette index 0 is transparent on every SNES layer, so the CHR page draws it as backdrop rather than as palette entry 0.

tickets.title: The SNES CPU trace is diffable against a reference emulator
acceptance: SNES CPU trace lines follow bsnes conventions — bank:addr, m/x-aware disassembly (DEBUGGER.md §2, bar B-9)
one formatter serves both the on-screen trace viewer and any golden diff, the way rf_nes::trace::format_trace_line already does for the NES
a golden trace fixture pins the format so it cannot drift silently
notes: FILED BY W13-01, 2026-09-03. The NES half of §2 is met by rf_nes::trace::format_trace_line and shared with the nestest golden diff; the SNES half does not exist. m/x-awareness is the part that makes this more than string formatting — operand width depends on processor-status bits, so the disassembler needs the machine's state, not just the bytes.
HANDOFF 2026-09-04: write_scope widened to the tests trees, retroforge/src/stepper.rs (the shared trace path lives there) and DEBUGGER.md — the same reasons the sibling tickets recorded.

DONE 2026-09-04. A 65C816 disassembler had to be written: none existed. All 256 opcodes with their addressing modes, transcribed from the W65C816S opcode matrix and cross-checked against fullsnes (NFR-011), in rf_snes::trace with the table in its own file so the matrix is readable as a matrix. There are NO illegal opcodes on this chip, which is why there is no `illegal` flag here and rf_nes::trace has one; WDM ($42) is the single reserved slot and behaves as a two-byte NOP.

WHY THE DISASSEMBLER TAKES P AND e AND NOT JUST BYTES: on a 6502 'LDA #$12' is always two bytes; on a 65816 it is two or THREE by the M flag, and LDX by X. A width guess does not merely misprint an operand — it reports the wrong instruction LENGTH, and every following line of the trace starts mid-instruction. Emulation mode pins both widths to 8 whatever P holds, which is why `e` is a parameter too: a trace taken before the first XCE would otherwise read every immediate as 16-bit.

A LATENT HANG WAS FOUND AND FIXED, AND IT IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING. latch_and_advance_frame_traced took EVERY exit through nes_bus(), which is None on a SNES session: the deadline compared 0 against a budget (always true) and the frame check compared 0 against self.frames (never true on a fresh stepper). BOTH exits were dead and the loop ran forever. It was pre-existing — nothing had traced a SNES session, so nothing reached it — and this ticket's test is what exposed it, by hanging for 600 seconds. Per law 8 the run was killed and the loop found BEFORE anything was re-run. Fixed with an instruction counter that advances on every path whatever the console, plus switching the frame check to self.frames, which is incremented from StepResult::frame_complete and is therefore the one frame count that exists for both consoles. Noted while there: the old check compared the NES bus's own counter against `start` taken from self.frames — two different counters that were only ever equal by coincidence.

A TEST ASSERTION OF MINE WAS WRONG IN AN INFORMATIVE WAY: I asserted the flag string contains M or m. A 65816 comes out of reset AS A 6502, so the first traced line of any SNES session is an EMULATION-mode line, where bit 5 is unused and bit 4 is B rather than X — format_flags renders that as 'nv-BdIzc' deliberately, because printing M and X there would describe registers the chip does not have in that mode. The assertion now checks the field's shape and accepts either mode.

EVIDENCE: 9 tests in rf-snes/tests/trace_format.rs, including criterion 3's GOLDEN LINE pinned byte for byte, the m/x width cases in both directions, emulation-mode forcing, SEP/REP always being one operand byte however the widths stand, a branch target relative to the NEXT instruction and staying in bank, long addressing printing six hex digits, block move printing SOURCE-first though it ENCODES destination-first (the classic block-move bug), and a completeness sweep over all 256 entries. Plus an app-level test that a real SNES fixture produces bank:addr lines through the shared path — criterion 2. Workspace 1775 passing / 0 failed / 33 ignored, up from 1765.

tickets.title: The SNES core emits no CoreEvent at all
acceptance: SnesCore emits the CoreEvent variants its hardware has an analogue for — at minimum FrameStart, FrameEnd, VblankStart, Scanline and MemWatch — gated by EventMask exactly as rf-nes gates its own, so an unsubscribed session pays nothing
an armed watchpoint on a SNES session reports hits (W13-02e's facility, which already installs on both cores through CoreConfig and today reports on neither)
the event timeline panel shows SNES events, rather than an empty list a user reads as 'nothing happened'
no SNES golden frame, vector suite or save-state test is re-baselined: events are observation, and a core that changed behaviour when subscribed would fail the mode-invariant suites
notes: FILED BY W13-02e, 2026-09-04, and MEASURED rather than suspected: 'grep -rn CoreEvent crates/rf-snes/src' returns ZERO lines. FR-CORE-006's whole subscription channel — the one the enhancement runtime, the event timeline and now watchpoints all ride on — has no producer on SNES.

SCOPE OF THE CONSEQUENCE, so it is not rediscovered per feature: every CoreEvent consumer is NES-only today whatever its own code says. That includes the event timeline viewer, scroll telemetry, and W13-02e's watchpoints. W13-02a is the sibling gap on the STATE side (SnesCore::state_view returns empty slices); this is the same half-console shape on the EVENT side, and the two are independent — neither blocks the other.

START FROM rf-nes's OWN SHAPE rather than inventing one: the NES core queues events on the PPU (Ppu::queue_event) because that is where the frame boundary and the event mask already live, and NesBus::set_event_mask pushes the mask down to it. The SNES core has no equivalent owner yet, and choosing one — ppu, bus, or system — is the design decision this ticket makes.
HANDOFF 2026-09-04: write_scope widened to the two tests/** trees, app.rs (two test accessors) and docs/design/DEBUGGER.md, for the same reasons W13-02d and W13-02e recorded.

DONE 2026-09-04. THE DESIGN DECISION THIS TICKET WAS FILED TO MAKE — where the event queue lives — resolved to the BUS, not the PPU. rf-nes queues on its PPU because that is where its frame boundary, its event mask and its scanline counter all are. On the SNES they are not in one place: the frame clock is crate::timing::Timing (on the bus), watch hits come from SnesBus's own read/write, and the PPU knows about neither. The bus is the one owner that can see all of them.

EMISSION POINTS, each at the place that already knew: FrameEnd then FrameStart at timing Events::frame_started, in the order both variants' docs specify and rf-nes already uses; VblankStart at Events::vblank_started and — deliberately — WHETHER OR NOT the ROM enabled NMI, because a subscriber is watching the machine, not the program's interrupt configuration; one Scanline per visible line crossed, queued before that line's HDMA so the event marks the line's start; MemWatch from CpuBus::read/write, after a read (so the condition tests what the CPU got, register side effects included) and before a write (so it tests the value arriving).

CoreConfig IS NOW A REAL PATH ON THIS CORE, which it was not before: SnesCore::step pushes config.event_mask and config.watches to the bus on entry, so there is exactly one place the bus can disagree with the config. Note the asymmetry that remains and is NOT this ticket's to fix: rf-nes's mask lives on its Ppu and is not read from CoreConfig, so EmuStepper::set_event_mask still sets both. Recorded rather than quietly unified.

EVERY STEP DRAINS, not only a completed frame. An Instruction or Scanline step that trips a watchpoint has to report it at the step that caused it — that is the whole point of single-stepping with one armed. emit_frame drains first on a frame boundary, so the second drain is empty rather than a double delivery.

EVIDENCE: 4 tests in rf-snes/tests/snes_emits_core_events.rs — an unsubscribed core emits NOTHING (pay-for-use, ARCHITECTURE section 5); a subscribed one reports FrameStart/FrameEnd/VblankStart and >100 Scanlines per frame with FrameEnd before FrameStart; a watchpoint installed through CoreConfig reports hits and stops when cleared; and SUBSCRIBING DOES NOT CHANGE WHAT THE MACHINE DOES, compared by WRAM after three frames — a core whose debugger changed the game would be worse than one with no debugger. Plus an app-level test that a running SNES session actually feeds the event timeline, which is criterion 3. The test ROM is a 32 KiB LoROM built in the test rather than a fixture: the events come from the frame clock, which advances whatever the CPU does, so a fixture would only make the test depend on something else being right. Workspace 1750 passing / 0 failed / 33 ignored, up from 1745; no SNES golden, vector or save-state test was re-baselined (criterion 4).

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE EVIDENCE. The same harness, the same 600 frames, the same sink: NES produced a uniform screen for 7 of 1174 loadable titles (0.6%), SNES for roughly 76%. Whatever this is, it is SNES-side and systemic rather than a scattering of per-game bugs.

WHY THIS IS NOT W14-03's TO FIX: that ticket built the census and its bound. Acting on what it found is separate work in a different crate, and folding it in would have made a measurement ticket into an open-ended accuracy ticket.

DO NOT START BY CHANGING THE RENDERER. Criterion 1 asks for a diagnosis first because the plausible causes are several stages apart — INIDISP forced-blank/brightness, TM main-screen designation, CGRAM never being written, a tile fetch that returns zero — and the project's own lesson (RF-L-08, and W7-08's three wrong diagnoses) is that the first plausible theory here has been wrong more often than right.
