tickets.title: The sub-screen path clones the whole PPU once per scanline
acceptance: a hires or colour-math title renders at a frame cost in the same order as a plain one; the measured starting point is 100ms per frame against 1.5ms for Zelda on the same machine, and the close must state the new number rather than assert an improvement
the seventeen PPU golden frames and every mode-7/window/colour-math test still pass unchanged — this is a performance change and any pixel that moves is a bug, not a trade

the sub screen keeps the isolation the clone was providing: render_scanline_live mutates sprite-limit flags, and rendering the sub screen must not let those accumulate into the main screen's state (the forced-blank test documents why that matters)
notes: CLOSED 2026-09-16. 105 ms/frame -> 1.0 ms on Super Buster Bros. (release, 60 frames, same machine as the 100 ms figure); Radical Psycho Machine Racing 103 -> 0.94, Batman Forever 227 -> 2.5, Judge Dredd 166 -> 1.9, Zelda unchanged at 0.9. The diagnosis was short by 256x: besides the per-line clone, render_sub_scanline called layer_at once PER PIXEL and layer_at cloned the PPU and composed the whole line again. Fix is LineScratch save/restore (register file, two write latches, direct_color, overscan_changed, limit flags) with in-place composition; with_line_state became apply_line_state; the main-screen layer line is composed once per sub scanline. Pixel identity checked by hashing every emitted index over 60 frames of the five titles before and after (identical), plus all goldens. Criterion 3 pinned by sub_screen_composition_leaves_the_live_ppu_untouched, mutation-checked. Flintstones/Elite Soccer are fast and blank — a different hang, still on W14-07's list.

PROFILED, NOT GUESSED (2026-09-15, W14-07). macOS `sample` over Super Buster Bros: 4587 of 4609 samples are in render_scanline_masked -> render_scanline_hires, and inside render_sub_scanline the single largest leaf is `<rf_snes::ppu::Ppu as Clone>::clone` at 957 samples, essentially all of it in _platform_memmove.

THE LINE IS crates/rf-snes/src/ppu/mod.rs, render_sub_scanline: `let mut shadow = self.with_line_state(line).unwrap_or_else(|| self.clone());` — and with_line_state clones too, so either branch is one FULL Ppu copy PER SCANLINE. A Ppu carries 64 KiB of VRAM, CGRAM, OAM and two ~224-entry Vec-of-Vec fields, so a frame is ~14 MB of memmove plus tens of thousands of allocations.

WHY THE CLONE IS THERE, and why the fix is not just deleting it: render_scanline_live takes &mut self and mutates sprite-limit flags — the forced-blank test asserts those do NOT accumulate while the screen is off. The shadow gives the sub screen its own copy of that mutable state. Any replacement has to keep that isolation, which is what criterion 3 is for.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, not a prescription: during emit_frame the PPU is settled, so the big buffers do not change between lines and one clone per FRAME would do where 224 are done now. Alternatives are saving and restoring only the fields the shadow actually alters (bg enables, obj_enabled, the line-state fields, and the sprite-limit flags), or putting the frame-constant buffers behind a refcount so a clone is a pointer bump.

THIS IS NOT ONLY ABOUT TWO GAMES. The path is taken by any title using a hires mode or the sub screen for colour math, which is a large fraction of the library — the census's timed-out bucket is just where it crosses a 30-second cap.

tickets.title: The APU only runs while the CPU touches a port, and drops every cycle past 64
acceptance: the cause is DIAGNOSED with a trace from a specific title before anything changes: ActRaiser's stub at $0400 must see the CPU's $FF command, and the trace shows the SPC700 still inside its first zero-page clear loop two vblanks after being started

the SPC700 advances in proportion to master cycles whether or not the 65816 touches $2140-$2143, and DMA-stolen cycles count too; a unit test runs an uploaded SPC program under a CPU that never reads a port and asserts the program made progress
no APU debt is ever discarded: a unit test hands catch_up_apu more than any per-call bound and asserts the remainder is carried, not dropped
the boot census's SNES 'rendered a uniform screen' bucket falls substantially, re-measured over the same library with the same harness rather than asserted, and the number is stated in the close
the full gate plus the ignored SNES suites (blargg SPC, PeterLemon, undisbeliever, region goldens) are re-run, and any verdict that moves is recorded rather than smoothed over
notes: CLOSED 2026-09-16. Census over the same 1265 SNES archives: rendered something 870 -> 934, uniform screen 245 -> 181, refused 150, crashed 0, timed out 0. Fix: SnesSystem::step accrues master cycles (DMA included) and calls catch_up_apu every instruction; the per-call bound carries its remainder; overspend is an explicit apu_overspent balance (the old saturating fold-back forgave it and, once calls owed one cycle each, ran the SPC at 4.4x -- measured by the new ratio test, which pins the hardware ratio within 25%). apu_overspent is in the save state. blargg SPC verdicts byte-identical; PeterLemon/undisbeliever/region goldens and the dsp6 phase probe pass. Still in the bucket after this: Illusion of Gaia (moved to a different port wait) and The Flintstones (unchanged) -- next probe.

FOUND 2026-09-16 BY PROBING THE 245-TITLE UNIFORM-SCREEN BUCKET after W14-08, six titles instruction-stepped with a ring buffer of APU port changes. Two shapes: (a) ActRaiser, Final Fantasy III, Cool Spot: the 65816 polls $2140 for $BBAA (the IPL ready signature) forever while the SPC driver runs its N-SPC main loop normally; (b) Cybernator, Illusion of Gaia, The Flintstones: the 65816 runs freely and the SPC700 is pinned at a single PC.

TRACED ON ACTRAISER, NOT REASONED ABOUT. The CPU uploads a stub to $0400, starts it, waits two vblanks ($9AC1 polls $4210), writes $FF to $2140 and waits for $BBAA. The stub handles $FF at $0601 by CALLing $0F0C, which republishes $AA/$BB itself (the only MOVW $F4,YA in the driver). But the stub's init writes $F1=$30 at $042A, clearing the incoming ports. In the trace the CPU's $FF landed 1558 CPU instructions BEFORE that clear: two vblanks after being started, the SPC700 was still at $0407 inside its very first zero-page clear loop (240 iterations, ~2400 SPC cycles, ~2.3 ms on hardware).

THE MECHANISM IS THE SCHEDULER, in bus.rs catch_up_apu. It is called ONLY from the $2140-$2143 read/write arms. It computes the whole debt, subtracts all of it, then caps the run at 64 SPC cycles — every cycle past 64 is DISCARDED. So while a game waits on $4210 or a RAM flag, the SPC700 does not run at all, and when the game comes back to a port it gets 64 cycles per access. Shape (b) is the same bug from the other side: a CPU that never touches a port starves the SPC entirely, which is what 'pinned at one PC' looks like. system.rs also never adds DMA cycles to apu_debt, so the APU freezes during every transfer.

WHY THE 64 WAS THERE: its comment fears a long DMA or a paused debugger handing the APU millions of cycles inside one bus access. With the debt settled every CPU instruction the per-call amount is one to a few SPC cycles, and the largest single lump is a full-bank DMA (~25k SPC cycles, milliseconds). A bound can stay as a sanity limit but the remainder must CARRY, never drop. EMULATION_CORES.md §1 ('each chip runs catch_up(to_master_cycle) first, Mesen-style') and line 232 ('catch-up sync with main CPU port accesses, never a free-running thread') both permit per-instruction settlement; the latter forbids a thread, not a schedule.

tickets.title: Disabling H/V IRQs in $4200 must drop a latched IRQ
acceptance: the cause is DIAGNOSED from a trace on a specific title before anything changes: Final Fantasy Mystic Quest's path into its STP trap goes IRQ vector -> $0117 trampoline -> $00:B821 BRK -> $011B trampoline -> $008253 STP, taken immediately after a PLP with $4200 already written to 0

writing $4200 with bits 4-5 clear drops the latched TIMEUP flag, cited to fullsnes $4211 and cross-checked against bsnes cpu io, and a unit test pins it (flag set, $4200 <- 0, no IRQ taken when I is cleared)
Final Fantasy Mystic Quest renders something within the census's 600 frames, measured with the same harness rather than asserted
the full gate plus the ignored SNES suites are re-run and any moved verdict is recorded
notes: ADDENDUM 2026-09-17 (loop iteration after W14-16), the garbage-execution class traced with title_probe: NOT one class. Super Ninja Boy: after a successful APU upload, the first NMI handler kicks channel 0 at $8E92 with count 0 -- a 65536-byte fixed-source VRAM fill that spans a vblank, so a fresh NMI lands the moment the kick returns, the handler never reaches STZ $78, and ~20 nested entries later a mismatched PLP/RTI returns to $8E95 with P=00 and the CPU walks graphics data in bank $89. The zero count comes from routine D at $99E0-$99F5 (STA $4300; STA $4302; STZ $4305): with M set that zeroes only the low byte and leaves a short fill; our CPU had M CLEAR there, so both bytes went to zero. The 65816 passes 2.5M single-step vectors, so this is a flag-STATE divergence upstream (an NMI landing in a different REP/SEP window than hardware, or a path taken on timing), not an opcode bug; unresolved, needs a P-at-NMI-entry trace from reset. NHL 95: executing WRAM $7E:0000-$03FF before 1.2M instructions with NMI disabled and no interrupt entries -- a different failure, untraced. Probe gained P in the PC ring (PROBE_RINGP), WRAM peeks (PROBE_PEEK), DMA/timing prints and a 6000-entry ring for this.

CLOSED 2026-09-16. Census over the same 1265 SNES archives: rendered something 934 -> 1001, uniform screen 181 -> 114, refused 150, crashed 0, timed out 0. Four fixes, each traced first: (1) $4200 with H/V IRQ off drops a latched TIMEUP flag; (2) the H/V counter latch ($2137/$213C/$213D/$213F/$4201) exists, cited to fullsnes; (3) the boot hand-over keeps the IPL banked in ($F1 bit 7 is only cleared by the program) so a commanded jump to $FFC0 reboots into the handshake; (4) re-entry waits the boot ROM's 2404-cycle zero-page clear before publishing $AA/$BB, keeping the jump counter's echo readable. A 1800-frame sweep of all 181 uniform titles found exactly one that was merely slow (Knights of the Round, frame 909). blargg SPC verdicts byte-identical; PPU goldens pass. STILL IN THE BUCKET, CAUSES NAMED: Final Fantasy Mystic Quest gets past both traps, runs with the screen on under a V-IRQ/H-IRQ raster chain that rewrites its own vector trampoline, and still shows a uniform frame (needs an IRQ event trace). Soul Blazer: a driver-side upload completes, then a track-data command indexes past the dispatch table at $0994 and the push/RET dispatch jumps to $0102 (either a corrupted upload or a 65816 defect). Blackthorne polls a voice ENVX via $F3 until it decays below 8 -- S-DSP envelope, W7-08 (blocked). NHL 95 executes WRAM garbage; The Flintstones sits in an RTS loop -- CPU-core suspects. Illusion of Gaia and ActRaiser 2 run a scripted APU sequence with long frame waits, cause open. Clay Fighter's driver clears ARAM for seconds and re-uploads; slow, cause open.

FOUND 2026-09-16 probing the uniform bucket after W14-09. Mystic Quest (USA) and (Japan) sit with the 65816 halted at $008254, the second of three STP/BRA traps behind a routine at $008247 that does STZ $4200 / LDA #$80 / STA $2100 -- the game's own fatal-error path.

TRACED, NOT REASONED ABOUT. A ring of the last 120 distinct PCs before the halt reads ... 00B853 000117 00B821 00011B 008253. The native vectors at $00:FFE4-FFEF are COP=$FFFF, BRK=$011B, ABORT=$8000, NMI=$0113, IRQ=$0117. WRAM $0117 is JML $00B821 and $011B is JML $008253. $00:B821 holds $00 (BRK). So: an IRQ was taken right after the PLP at $00:B853, its handler is a BRK, and BRK's vector is the STP trap -- the game's way of saying an IRQ here is impossible. The routine that ran ($00:B82C-B857) had already written $4200 = 0 at $00:B833 (STZ $4200) before that PLP.

THE MECHANISM: SnesBus writes $4200 as `self.nmitimen = NmiTimen(value)` and nothing else. IrqTimer.fired stays latched from an earlier H/V IRQ; SnesSystem::step takes an IRQ whenever `irq.fired && !I`. The PLP cleared I, the stale flag fired. On hardware disabling the H/V IRQ in $4200 deasserts the IRQ line: fullsnes $4211 ('the flag is reset ... on disabling IRQs via 4200h'), and bsnes cpu/io.cpp clears irqLine when neither hirq nor virq is enabled after a $4200 write.

tickets.title: MMC2 (mapper 9): a CHR latch the PPU switches at the fetch

the latch switches INSIDE the PPU at the pattern fetch that triggers it (nesdev MMC2: $0FD8/$0FE8 for the left half, $1FD8-$1FDF/$1FE8-$1FEF for the right), not at the end of the CPU instruction -- a unit test reads the trigger address and asserts the very next pattern read comes from the other bank

notes: CLOSED 2026-09-17. NES census over the same 1281 archives: rendered 1180 -> 1184, refused 95 -> 91, uniform 6 (all non-retail), crashed 0, timed out 0. All four Punch-Out!! archives render. Design as filed: Mapper::chr_latch supplies four 4 KiB banks, the PPU flips the selection in mem_read right after the triggering read, note_chr_latch copies it back each instruction for the save state. Also closed on the way: a mapper state load never re-pushed the restored bank registers into the PPU (every banked CHR-ROM mapper resumed with the pre-load window); the load arm now re-pushes window, latch and mirroring. Remaining NES refused, each its own ticket: MMC5 (11), RAMBO-1 (9), FME-7 (4), TQROM (3), multicart/unlicensed long tail (~64). FILED 2026-09-17 from the W14-12 header tally: mapper 9 is 4 archives (Punch-Out!! and Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!, two revisions each). The Mapper trait pushes a materialised CHR window into the PPU after CPU writes and pulls A12 edges back; MMC2's latch is driven by PPU pattern FETCHES, so a pull-and-push at instruction granularity would land up to two tile fetches late and corrupt the tiles after every $FD/$FE tile. The design here keeps the push shape: the mapper supplies four 4 KiB latch banks through a new chr_latch() hook, the PPU holds them and flips the selection itself in mem_read, and the bus copies the selection back to the mapper each instruction (note_chr_latch) so the mapper's save state carries it.

WHY IT IS NOT ONE MORE MAPPER FILE. The crate's mappers push a materialised CHR window and a Mirroring into the PPU; MMC5 needs the PPU to (a) read two nametables from memory only the cartridge has -- its 1 KiB ExRAM, or a constant fill tile+attribute -- (b) fetch 8x16 sprite patterns from a different CHR bank set than the background, (c) tell the mapper each rendered scanline so $5203 compares and the in-frame flag ($5204 bit 6) tracks rendering, and (d) answer CPU reads in $5000-$5FFF. Each is a small seam: ppu/mem.rs's nametable arm already dispatches on Mirroring (PerTable exists since W14-12; add ExRam and Fill kinds per table, with a PPU-owned 1 KiB buffer the bus writes on $5C00 stores and a fill tile/attr pair); sprites.rs:546 is the one sprite pattern read (route through a sprite CHR view when 8x16 and the mapper provides one); the A12 pull in NesBus::drain_a12_edges is the model for a take_scanline_starts pull; cpu_read_expansion is the read twin of cpu_write_expansion.

WHAT NOT TO DO FIRST: ExGrafix (per-tile CHR bank and palette from ExRAM in $5104 mode 1) changes the background fetch itself and the vertical split rewrites scrolling mid-line; both are slice 2. Castlevania III boots and plays without either. The scanline counter on real MMC5 detects scanlines from three identical consecutive nametable fetches; a PPU-side per-scanline signal is the honest model here and matches what Mesen exposes.

MEASUREMENT 2026-09-18 (W16-12): compact Real-ESRGAN-class model = ~335 ms per 256x240 frame on the M4 Max, CPU and CoreML alike; 20x over the 16.67 ms gate. A real-time neural pass with ESRGAN-class models is not viable here. Options when this ticket is picked: (a) MetalFX spatial via W16-08 as the real-time path, (b) a purpose-trained tiny model (e.g. FSRCNN-class, ~10 KB params) measured first with the W16-01 harness, (c) close as measured-not-viable and keep the offline studio. acceptance: the cause is DIAGNOSED from a trace before anything changes: W17-04 found apu.cpu.stopped=true while apu.boot_running=true on Super Mario RPG, the main CPU parked at $C4:0541 CMP $2140 / BNE; the trace names which SPC700 instruction or IPL-boot transition set stopped (an unimplemented opcode, a STOP/SLEEP, or a boot state-machine exit) and at what point of the upload

Super Mario RPG renders in the census child (exit 0); the SNES census is re-run and every title that moved is named in docs/TESTING.md, since a boot-upload defect is systemic, not per-title

notes: FILED 2026-09-19 on Brad's 'continue with next fixes' after Wave 17 closed. Evidence from W17-04: SMRPG's main CPU spins on $2140 with the SPC700 halted mid-boot. Same census/probe method as the W14-10 drive (title_probe PROBE_PORTS=1, PROBE_RINGP=1).

BLOCKED 2026-09-19. Diagnosis complete, trace-confirmed, docs/TESTING.md has the full writeup. The halt is NOT the IPL handshake (W17-04's framing was too narrow): the first-stage IPL transfer completes cleanly (37 bytes to $0200, boot=Running, ipl still banked in) and control passes to real uploaded driver code. Pinned with PROBE_STOP_ON_SPC_STOP/PROBE_PORTS/PROBE_ARAM: SPC halts at PC $09B6 executing SLEEP ($EF) at ARAM $09B5; that byte was live code (MOV A,$16) at instruction 70,000 and became FD EF (MOV Y,A; SLEEP) by the halt because the uploaded driver's OWN command-receive loop stores 3 bytes per call at $0912+X/$0913+X/$0914+X with no bound or reset on X, traced climbing 0x98->0x9B->0x9E->0xA1->0xA4 by 3/call; at X=0xA1 the stores hit $09B3/$09B4/$09B5 and the driver overwrites its own code with incoming data. Ruled out by trace: unimplemented opcode (EF is implemented, ops.rs:800, returns Ok not Err), IPL machine exiting into the SLEEP-filled $FFC0 window (ipl=false throughout, halt PC is in ARAM), and a short/misaddressed first-stage upload (landed correctly at $0200). A fix was ATTEMPTED and REVERTED: extrapolated nesdev's S-SMP 'skip $00 on wraparound' rule (documented only for the two-step next-block increment) to every ordinary +1 continuation in IplBoot's counter prediction. Disproved by same-tree A/B against the census baseline: Wild Guns' real uploader wraps $FF->$00 plainly (no skip), and the skip-zero prediction misread that legitimate continuation as a counter mismatch, jumping to a bogus address $A400 -- regressing a previously-rendering title. Working tree at ticket close is byte-identical to before the ticket started (git stash + drop, verified clean). Root cause is downstream of IplBoot, inside the uploaded driver's own runtime loop, and is not fixable within this ticket's write_scope as currently understood: the driver bytes are the game's own and real hardware runs the identical code, so either a timing/rate mismatch against real hardware or a buffer-sizing assumption this emulator isn't honouring remains to be found. Unconfirmed lead for the follow-up: under the reverted fix, SMRPG got past this SLEEP into a SECOND IplBoot-managed transfer (driver jumps back to $FFC0) before hanging on a different spin (LDA $2142/BNE $086E waiting for $2143==2); ports_out[3] is only set by an SPC write to $F7, which neither Publish nor reenter_ipl touch -- worth instrumenting write_register($F6/$F7) with the writing SPC PC next time, but this was observed only under reverted code and is not a current-tree finding. Census not re-run (no code changed). Gate on the clean/reverted tree: cargo fmt/clippy/rf-snes clean; full workspace count in the closing commit.

BLOCKED 2026-09-19 (stage 2). Corrects stage 1's own 'unbounded X, no bound and no reset' framing: a manual SPC700 disassembly of ARAM $0970-$09E2 (title_probe, PROBE_TIMERLOG/PROBE_PACKETLOG added this session, module doc has the contract) shows the receive loop is bounded by DBNZ Y with an explicit ADC/BCC carry chain into three self-patched page bytes ($09BE/$09C3/$09C8) -- not a raw unbounded index. All three ranked mechanisms from this ticket's brief were traced and rejected: (1) timer0/timer1 were enabled from instruction 74,213 through 988,617 -- running for virtually the whole session and only disabled AFTER the corruption at instruction 984,014, not before, so 'consumer never runs' is refuted by the timer log itself; (2) duplicate/non-atomic port writes are refuted both by protocol (the receive loop gates only on $F4 changing, and the CPU always writes $2141-$2143 before $2140, so there is no intermediate state to double-count) and by count (ports_in0_changes=22218 > x_register_changes=17036, the opposite of over-consumption); (3) clock ratio is not reproduced -- catch_up_apu (W14-09) already runs the APU to the exact master-cycle count before every $2140-$2143 access, synchronous by construction, and the packet cadence is steady throughout. The actual corruption was pinned with a one-shot Apu::write trace (added and reverted this session, not shipped): the self-patched page-byte carry chain has no bound and no periodic reset, so after ~199 page-carries it walks down through ARAM page $00, at which point the SAME receive loop's own stores (MOV !$4B13+X,A at $09C1 / MOV !$4B14+X,A at $09C6) land on $0000/$0001 -- the 16-bit pointer that seeds the whole scheme -- and stamp it with leftover incoming port data (dp$01: 0x48->0x07 at instruction 984,014). Two more carries (07->08->09) walk the corrupted pointer onto the driver's own code page $09 by instruction 1,039,833, reproducing stage 1's $09B3-$09B5 SLEEP overwrite exactly. Not fixed: the carry chain is the game's own ROM bytes (law 5), and whether real hardware ever drives it through ~200 carries in one boot sequence (a rate/gating difference elsewhere, since clock ratio itself checked out synchronous) or reaches a reset this emulator's dispatcher never takes is unresolved and needs either a real-hardware $2140 traffic capture or disassembling the full command dispatcher (out of this session's budget). docs/TESTING.md has the full disassembly and trace. notes: FILED 2026-09-19 by the orchestrator from the 2026-09-17 triage: NMI storm caused by a 65536-byte DMA (size 0 with M clear at STZ $4305) — a flag-state divergence upstream of the crash; the CPU passes 2.5M singlestep vectors, so not a per-opcode bug. Interrupt-entry/exit P handling and XCE/native-mode transitions are the suspects.

CLOSED-AS-BLOCKED 2026-09-19: the M-clear/STZ $4305 hypothesis does NOT reproduce. Every store to $4305/$4306 in this ROM (three STA sites at 80:8F9A, 80:9394, 80:94AD, plus the one STZ at 80:99F5) executes with M forced to 1 by a SEP #$30/#$20 on the same code path, immediately before the store; STA/STZ absolute is 3 bytes regardless of M so this is exact, not an artifact of the disassembler. The 2026-09-17 reading most likely came from trace::disassemble being handed one snapshot cpu.p for a whole linear PROBE_DIS range, which desyncs at every immediate-operand width change once a REP/SEP is crossed (seen directly: 80:9334 prints as LDY #$B100 under a stale 16-bit-X snapshot, but decodes as the correct LDY #$00 / LDA ($AA),Y once the snapshot lines up with SEP #$30 at 80:9324 -- a tool artifact, not a CPU bug). ACTUAL MECHANISM, confirmed with a temporary W1425_DAS/DMA/A/TIMING eprintln trace (not committed; reproduce by instrumenting SnesSystem::step and SnesBus::service_dma the same way): the shared DMA-arm helper at 80:8D2A (called by both a direct-fire caller at 80:92DC/92E0/92E3 and, unconditionally, via its own TSB $78) arms WRAM $78 bit 0 as a queue latch for channel 0, and the NMI handler (80:8E69) unconditionally drains that same latch and re-fires MDMAEN with whatever channel-0 registers currently hold, then does STZ $78 to clear it. Sequence observed at the actual crash (n=1619670-1619743 in the instruction trace): 8D2A arms $78=1 and programs channel 0 for a legitimate 16384-byte VRAM fill (control=$08 fixed-source, B=$18, count=16384); the direct caller has not yet reached its own STA $420B/TRB $78 cleanup when this transfer runs long enough (131080 master cycles = 8 cyc/byte + overhead per fullsnes DMA timing, ~96 scanlines) to cross the next vblank edge (trace: entry line 181/frame 102, exit line 15/frame 103, vblank_start=240 with overscan) before the CPU can execute the cleanup. The NMI fires first, drains $78 (still 1) and re-triggers channel 0 with the now-completed transfer's post-run register state -- count=0, which is DASxL/H=0 meaning 65536 bytes per fullsnes "SNES DMA/HDMA Registers", not a clobbered write. That 65536-byte transfer is itself long enough (524296 cycles, ~384 lines, over one full 262-line frame) to guarantee crossing another vblank edge before ITS OWN STZ $78 cleanup runs, so the NMI handler re-enters before ever reaching STZ $78 -- $78 is never cleared, and the storm is self-sustaining forever. A second, non-storming instance of the identical 16384-byte transfer was captured for comparison (armed at line 85/frame 138, fires line 86->182, well clear of the vblank_start=240 boundary) -- proving Timing::advance itself is arithmetically correct (verified line-by-line: entry+96 lines matches exit exactly, including the frame wrap, in both cases) and the only variable is WHICH SCANLINE the game's own code reaches this DMA-arm sequence at, which is fixed by how many cycles everything since the previous vblank actually cost. This is a bona fide race in the GAME's own shared DMA-queue routine (it unconditionally arms a queue-latch even for its own synchronous, direct-fire use, with no margin against an NMI landing between arm and cleanup) that would degrade the same way on real hardware IF real hardware reaches this code at the same late scanline (observed: line 181 of 262, only 59 lines before the overscan vblank_start=240) -- but whether real hardware ever lands there, or always arrives earlier with more margin (as the safe instance at line 85 does), depends on cycle-exact timing of everything since the prior vblank that this investigation cannot certify without a real-hardware or known-good-emulator (bsnes/higan) reference trace of this exact ROM, which is out of this ticket's tooling. NAMED NEXT STEP: capture a cycle-exact trace of Super Ninja Boy's boot from a reference emulator (bsnes performance-accurate core preferred) up to this same DMA-arm call and compare the scanline/cycle count reached against rf-snes's own -- a divergence there would point at a specific CPU/PPU/APU timing defect upstream; an exact match would mean the game genuinely ships this race and RetroForge is reproducing real hardware behaviour, in which case W14-25 should close as WONTFIX (law 5: no patching around a game's own code) rather than reopen as a timing-fix ticket. No code changed in rf-snes or rf-harness this pass; PROBE_DIS/title_probe env-var contract already covers everything needed to redo this trace (PROBE_ROMS, PROBE_INSTR, PROBE_DIS, PROBE_RINGP/PROBE_RING, PROBE_PEEK).

BLOCKED 2026-09-20: the fetch/operand-skip loop is exonerated in full -- there is no length table at all. Disassembled $0701-$0745 by hand from the ARAM dump (cross-checked byte-length arithmetic against two independent anchors) and confirmed every branch consumes a FIXED number of bytes decided by inline MSB tests (bit7 of byte1 at $0723, bit7 of byte2 at $072B), never a table lookup -- W14-27's '$0A8A parallel operand-length array' was a misreading of the jump table's own overrun tail, not a second table the fetch loop reads. PROBE_SPCPCCOUNT shows $0701 fires EXACTLY ONCE in the whole run: this channel's loop has no prior note in its own history, so no mis-skipped operand could have desynced anything -- the very first byte it ever reads is $FE. That byte is genuinely at ARAM $90F1 (dumped directly, confirmed). Its channel-init copy loop ($06C0-$06CA, 'MOV A,[$16]+Y / MOV !$00D4+Y,A / DEC Y / BPL') and the 32-byte source table it copies from ($0C10-$0C2F, containing the literal F1,90 pointer bytes) are BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL to the ROM at LoROM 9F:F962 (PROBE_FINDROM). So the STARTING pointer is exactly what the ROM commands, not an emulator computation defect -- W14-27's ticket-brief question is answered end to end: verified clean, no fix in this loop.  But this does NOT close WONTFIX, because the byte AT that pointer is not ROM content: PROBE_ARAM at $90E0-$9110 is all-zero through CPU instruction 4,000,000 and fully populated by 4,700,000 -- it is written at RUNTIME, not uploaded at boot, and PROBE_FINDROM finds no match for it anywhere in the 1MB ROM file (multiple window sizes tried, 7-32 bytes, all zero hits) despite the driver CODE and its init TABLE both matching ROM exactly a few hundred bytes away. PROBE_SPCMEMWATCH pins the single write: ARAM $90F1 goes 00->FE at CPU instruction 4,114,366 (caveat, now in title_probe's module doc: PROBE_SPCMEMWATCH/SPCREGPC sample once per 65816 instruction, so the printed spcpc is wherever the SPC700 had reached by then, not necessarily the storing instruction -- this misattributed the write to a wrong instruction twice this session before the correction below). Two hypotheses were run down and both come back negative: (1) a driver-side $F4/$F5 APU-upload race duplicating or dropping port bytes -- new PROBE_APUPORTLOG traces the accepted (index,data) sequence directly and it is perfectly clean and monotonic (indices 223,224,225 carrying data FE,30,D3 with no dup/skip) for the transfer segment matching this same ROM byte-run elsewhere in ARAM, and that transfer's own destination arithmetic proves it physically cannot reach $90F1 (base $9336 + unsigned Y never yields an address below $9336); (2) the S-DSP echo buffer sweeping over $90xx -- refuted directly, `apu.dsp.echo.write_disabled=true` for the entire run (reset default, matches FLG's real hardware reset value) and `base_page=$F7` (buffer at $F700-$FEFF) throughout, nowhere near $90xx. Named next step: find the SPC700 instruction (or subsystem) that executes at CPU instruction ~4,114,366 and writes ARAM $90F1 -- it is neither the traced $0F18 receive loop (destination arithmetic rules it out), nor the DSP echo sweep (write_disabled all run), nor the IPL boot HLE's direct-from-Rust BootAction::Store (boot_running=true, i.e. already handed off to real SPC700 execution, at exactly this instruction) -- candidates still open: a different upload chunk's destination-page bookkeeping (the CPU sender's outer 'DEC $0C' loop restarts with a fresh $2142/$2143 destination per chunk, and this session did not enumerate every chunk), or a driver routine that computes/expands table data into scratch RAM at runtime (a per-voice envelope/pitch buffer construction, common in SNES sound drivers) that happens to alias this channel's track-pointer target. a BLOCKED verdict must trace the chain back to ROM bytes or a register read whose value is checked against fullsnes — 'game's own data' without that chain is not accepted (W14-24/26/28 all hid behind such verdicts)
notes: W14-33 continuation 2026-09-20 (review requested closing the 'why doesn't a shipped game deadlock on hardware' gap): for Rival Turf!, walked the exact write/read chain with PROBE_APUPORTLOG+PROBE_SPCMEMWATCH -- the SPC never reads stale data (every dp$0X write is preceded by the matching CPU port write, catch_up_apu runs before every $2140-$2143 access both directions, no $F1 write occurs in this window since the driver's only $F1 write is a one-time setup at ARAM $063D and PROBE_SDUMP=00e402 confirms this whole transfer is a single call entered once at n=481134 with X=$0001, never re-entered). Walked the CPU's indirect-long source pointer (bank $17, address $8000+Y, from PROBE_SDUMP=00e425's d=0000/bank0-dump) to the mapped LoROM file offset (0xB8000+Y) and confirmed byte-exact against the unzipped ROM file: offset 0xBCF81-84 = 00 00 00 80, exactly the four bytes the CPU sent -- genuine, unmodified game data, not a mapping bug. Then did a cycle-exact race analysis using PROBE_ACCESSWIN and the vector-verified SPC700 CYCLES table (spc700/timing.rs): the CPU's fixed per-byte pacing loop ($E434-$E43C) provides 784 master cycles (measured) = ~37.3 SPC cycles between one byte's echo and its next 'done?' check; the SPC's finalize sequence from echo to asserting out[2]=$FF costs 55 SPC cycles by the same vector-derived table. 55 > 37.3 is a fixed ~18-cycle shortfall given two independently vector-verified cycle tables, not a coin-flip or an emulator-only artifact -- meaning this exact game-code shape (uploader's byte-pump pacing shorter than the driver's own finalize path) would deadlock identically on real hardware if reached. What is NOT settled: whether real hardware's boot sequence ever reaches this exact zero-count header in normal play (this session found no earlier dispatcher/table-selection step to blame -- the transfer is one straight-line call from a byte-exact ROM table) -- left as a real-hardware-capture question, not something this session's tools could resolve further. For Super Turrican: found a NEW, more precise mechanism -- the stale 'go' trigger byte ($F0) the CPU wrote to end the IPL transfer survives IplBoot::Run's handoff untouched (ports_in is not zeroed on Run, matching real memory-mapped-latch behaviour), and the driver's very first command-loop read ($F018) consumes and echoes it as an unrecognized command 4 samples before the CPU's own separate cleanup write (ports_in[0]=0) lands. Named the one specific, checkable gap: this crate's IplBoot is HLE (boot.rs's own module doc) and hands control over in the same instant it detects the CPU's 'go' write, whereas the real IPL boot ROM (snes.nesdev.org S-SMP page) may spend a few real SPC cycles on its own jump sequence between those two events -- if so, real hardware's SPC would reach $F018 correspondingly later relative to the CPU's cleanup write, closing this exact race. Not verified against that page in this session; named as the next step. For Wario's Woods: checked and RULED OUT the same stale-byte mechanism -- its driver zeroes out[0]/out[1] before ever reading in[0], and its real wait (CMPW YA,$F4 against a hardcoded $0333) is never falsely satisfied by the handoff residue ($0059 spc). Its deadlock is the same shape the first pass found, re-confirmed, no register/timing divergence from fullsnes found. All three remain BLOCKED; no code changed, diagnostics only. See docs/TESTING.md's 2026-09-20 continuation section under the W14-33 write-up for full traces.
